421	=== editing/enable-picture-and-sound
422	---
423	title: Turn a clip's picture or sound off
424	description: What it means when one half of a clip is switched off, which commands do it, and how the clip then looks on the timeline.
425	---
426	
427	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
428	
429	A clip has two halves, its picture and its sound, and each can be switched off while the clip stays where it is. A switched-off half adds nothing to the picture or the mix, and it comes back when the half is switched on again.
430	
431	<AtAGlance
432	  menu={['Clip ▸ Detach Audio', 'Clip ▸ Attach Audio']}
433	  keys={['⌥⌘D', '⇧⌥⌘D']}
434	  tools="set_enabled"
435	/>
436	
437	## Turn a half off
438	
439	There's no switch for this in the inspector. Commands flip the halves as part of what they do:
440	
441	| Command | What it switches |
442	| --- | --- |
443	| [**Clip ▸ Detach Audio**](/audio/detach-and-attach/) | Turns the clip's sound off and adds a sound-only copy on the track below, with its picture off. |
444	| [**Clip ▸ Attach Audio**](/audio/detach-and-attach/) | Merges a detached pair back into one clip with its sound on. |
445	| [**Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…**](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) | Can turn off the picture of the camera clips it replaces, and their sound when **Mute the cameras' own sound** is ticked. |
446	
447	To silence a clip's sound by hand, use **Mute** on the [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/). To hide its picture, set its [opacity](/canvas/transform/) to 0 or [hide the track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/).
448	
449	## How the clip looks
450	
451	| Switched off | On the timeline |
452	| --- | --- |
453	| The picture of a movie clip | It reads as an audio clip, with the audio tint and symbol, and has no filmstrip. |
454	| The sound | It has no waveform. |
455	| Both | It's dimmed, like a clip on a hidden track. |
456	
457	A clip with its sound off has no **Sound** tab in the inspector, because there's nothing there to adjust. Its **Picture** tab stays, even with the picture off.
458	
459	## Good to know
460	
461	- A clip with its sound off can't be transcribed, and **Remove Silences** doesn't count it as audible.
462	- Copies keep the switches of the clip they came from.
463	- [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/) leaves the target's switches alone.
464	
465	## With an agent
466	
467	`set_enabled` switches either half of any clip directly, which no command in the app does on its own. Give it `video`, `audio` or both, as true or false, and a half you leave out stays as it is. See [Tools: moving and trimming](/mcp/tools-move-and-trim/#set_enabled).
468	
469	## Related

471	- [Detach and Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/)

473	- [Mute and solo tracks](/audio/mute-and-solo/)
474	=== editing/how-edits-work
475	---
476	title: "How edits work"
477	description: What an edit acts on, why clips never push each other, and the rules every timeline edit keeps.
478	---
479	
480	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
481	
482	Every edit in Frame Job acts on something you've already pointed at, and every edit keeps the same few rules. Once you know them, you can tell what a command will touch and why one sometimes won't go through.
483	
484	<AtAGlance
485	  menu={['Mark ▸ Set In', 'Mark ▸ Set Out', 'Mark ▸ Clear Range']}
486	  keys={['I', 'O', '⌥X']}
487	  where="The timeline: the selection, the playhead and the range"
488	  tools={['set_selection', 'set_playhead', 'set_range']}
489	/>
490	
491	## What an edit acts on
492	
493	Most commands act on the selected clips. Some also use the playhead, the in and out range or the current track.
494	
495	| What | What it is | What uses it |
496	| --- | --- | --- |
497	| **The selection** | The clips outlined in coral on the timeline. See [Select clips](/timeline/selecting-clips/). | Most commands |
498	| **The playhead** | The moment you're looking at. | Split, trim to the playhead, Freeze Frame, Paste, Insert and Overwrite at Playhead |
499	| **The in and out range** | The stretch between the points set with <kbd>I</kbd> and <kbd>O</kbd>. <kbd>⌥X</kbd> clears both. See [The in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/). | With nothing selected, Delete and Ripple Delete act on the range |
500	| **The current track** | The track of the first selected clip, or the front-most track when nothing is selected. With a [nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/) open, it's a track inside the nest. | Close Gap, Select All on Track, Insert and Overwrite at Playhead |
501	
502	A selected clip's linked partner, such as its [detached sound](/audio/detach-and-attach/), shows a dashed outline. Most edits take it along, as long as its track isn't locked.
503	
504	## Clips never push each other
505	
506	A clip you drag never shoves its neighbours out of the way. A place that would need a neighbour to move isn't available, so the clip [stops short of it](/editing/move-clips/#when-a-drop-wont-go-where-you-let-go).
507	
508	Only the edits that are there to move other clips do so: [Ripple Delete](/editing/delete-clips/), [Close Gap](/editing/close-gaps/), [Insert](/editing/insert-and-overwrite/#insert-a-file), [inserting time](/editing/close-gaps/#insert-time) and [Freeze Frame](/speed/freeze-frame/). They open or close time across every unlocked track. A [locked track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/) stays where it is.
509	
510	## The overlap rule
511	
512	Two clips on one track may overlap a little, and that overlap is a [transition](/motion/transitions/). The rule has three parts:
513	
514	- A clip can overlap at most one neighbour on each side.
515	- Each overlap can be at most half the length of the shorter clip.
516	- An adjustment clip can't overlap another clip at all, because it can't take a transition. Fade it with opacity instead.
517	
518	An edit that leaves a clip overlapping the clip before it gives that clip a Cross Dissolve over the overlap, unless it already has a transition.
519	
520	Moves, trims, nudges, duplicates, gap closes and nests won't break the rule. Paste and Un-nest put a clip that would break it on a new track at the front instead. The rule never stops a ripple delete: a clip it slides onto a neighbour gets a Cross Dissolve.
521	
522	## Times land on frames
523	
524	Every time you give an edit, by dragging or typing, lands on a whole frame of the project's [frame rate](/projects/frame-rate/). A moved or trimmed clip goes to the nearest frame, so you can't place a clip between two frames. A time before the start of the timeline stops at 0.
525	
526	The exceptions are the short audio times typed in the **Sound** sub-tab, such as a fade length or a compressor's attack, which keep the value you typed. A fade dragged by its handle on the clip still lands on a frame.
527	
528	A move or a ripple shifts every clip by exactly the same amount, so clips stay in step. At a frame rate that doesn't divide evenly, such as 7 fps, a shifted start can sit off the frame grid by a sliver too small to see.
529	
530	## One frame minimum
531	
532	[Trims](/editing/trimming/) and [rolls](/editing/slip-and-roll/) always leave a clip at least one frame long. The drag stops there, however far you pull.
533	
534	## Project limits
535	
536	| A project holds up to | |
537	| --- | --- |
538	| Clips | 4,096 |
539	| Tracks | 64 |
540	| Levels of nesting | 8 |
541	| Markers | 1,024 |
542	| Media files | 1,024 |
543	
544	Clips and tracks inside nests count towards the same totals as the ones on the timeline. An edit that would pass a limit doesn't happen, and the project stays as it was. See [Limits](/reference/limits/).
545	
546	## When an edit doesn't go through
547	
548	Frame Job beeps, changes nothing and adds no undo step. When a rule stopped the edit, the reason appears at the foot of the inspector. An edit that would change nothing beeps too, with no reason given. An edit Frame Job can't carry out at all, such as placing a file shorter than one frame or passing a project limit, shows an alert instead of a beep.
549	
550	A drag is quieter. It stays at the last position the project allows, with no beep. See [When an edit is refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/).
551	
552	## With an agent
553	
554	`set_selection`, `set_playhead` and `set_range` set the selection, the playhead and the range. They aren't edits and they add no undo step. See [Tools: playhead, range and selection](/mcp/tools-view-state/).
555	
556	An agent's times land on frames too. A negative position on the timeline becomes 0, but a negative length is an error and nothing changes.
557	
558	## Related
559	
560	- [Core concepts](/getting-started/core-concepts/)
561	- [Select clips](/timeline/selecting-clips/)
562	- [When an edit is refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/)
563	- [Undo and saving](/getting-started/undo-and-saving/)
564	- [Hide and lock tracks](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/)
565	=== editing/insert-and-overwrite
566	---
567	title: "Insert and overwrite"
568	description: Bring a file into a cut that's already timed, either by making room for it or by replacing what's there.
569	---
570	
571	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
572	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
573	
574	Insert and Overwrite bring a file into a cut that's already timed. Insert makes room for it and pushes everything later along. Overwrite replaces what's there and moves nothing.
575	
576	<AtAGlance
577	  menu={['Edit ▸ Insert at Playhead', 'Edit ▸ Overwrite at Playhead']}
578	  keys={['⌥-drop', '⇧⌥-drop']}
579	  where="Right-click a row in the Media tab"
580	  tools={['insert_clip', 'overwrite_clip']}
581	/>
582	
583	## Place a file at the playhead
584	
585	<Steps>
586	
587	1. Click the file's row in the Media tab.
588	
589	2. Move the playhead to where the file should start.
590	
591	3. To choose the track, select a clip on it. With nothing selected, the file goes on the front track.
592	
593	4. Choose **Edit ▸ Insert at Playhead** or **Edit ▸ Overwrite at Playhead**.
594	
595	</Steps>
596	
597	Neither item has a shortcut. You can also right-click a row and choose either item there, which acts on that row and selects it.
598	
599	The file lands on the [current track](/editing/how-edits-work/#what-an-edit-acts-on). With a [nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/) open, that's a track inside the nest.
600	
601	## Drop with a modifier
602	
603	Drag a row from the Media tab onto a track, and hold a modifier as you let go. Only the keys held at that moment count.
604	
605	| Hold | What the drop does |
606	| --- | --- |
607	| Nothing, or <kbd>⇧</kbd> alone | [Adds the clip](/editing/add-clips/#drag-media-onto-a-track) without moving anything |
608	| <kbd>⌥</kbd> | Inserts at the drop point |
609	| <kbd>⇧⌥</kbd> | Overwrites at the drop point |
610	
611	The modifiers only work on a track. A drop on the preview canvas always [adds the file on a new track](/editing/add-clips/#drop-media-on-the-canvas).
612	
613	## Insert a file
614	
615	Insert keeps everything you've already cut, and the timeline gets longer by the length of the file.
616	
617	- If the point falls inside a clip on the destination track, that clip is split there.
618	- Every unlocked track opens up by the file's length. Clips that start at or after the point move later, and so do markers.
619	- The file lands in the room this makes.
620	
621	Only the destination track is cut. A clip on another track that spans the point stays whole and where it is, so a music bed plays on unbroken under the new file. The exception is a [detached sound](/audio/detach-and-attach/) linked to the clip that was cut. It's cut at the same point, so the pair stays in step.
622	
623	The whole edit is one undo step, Insert.
624	
625	## Overwrite with a file
626	
627	Overwrite moves nothing, and what was there is gone. The timeline only gets longer if the file runs past its end.
628	
629	- The destination track is cut at both ends of the file's length.
630	- Whatever lies between the cuts is removed.
631	- The file lands in the space.
632	
633	Nothing shifts and no other track is touched. The exception is again a detached sound linked to a clip that was cut. It's cut at the same points, and its piece under the new file stays, no longer linked.
634	
635	The whole edit is one undo step, Overwrite.
636	
637	## Good to know
638	
639	- **Locked tracks.** Insert won't work on a locked destination track, because the track can't open up, and the reason appears at the foot of the inspector. Insert elsewhere leaves locked tracks where they are, so their clips can fall out of step with the rest. Overwrite still clears a locked track, because you chose that track and nothing has to move.
640	- **When the menu items are dimmed.** They need a selected row in the Media tab, and that row can't be a `.cube` LUT. A LUT is [applied as a look](/color/luts/), so its right-click **Insert at Playhead** and **Overwrite at Playhead** are dimmed too. A filter that hides the selected row clears the selection.
641	- **The length is the whole file.** Both edits place the file from its first frame to its last. To use part of it, [trim the clip](/editing/trimming/) afterwards. After an Insert, trimming leaves a gap, which [Close Gap](/editing/close-gaps/) removes.
642	
643	## With an agent
644	
645	`insert_clip` and `overwrite_clip` make the same edits. Each takes a track, a file and a time, so an agent doesn't need the playhead or a selected row, and it can place a file inside a nest without opening it. See [Tools: adding clips](/mcp/tools-adding-clips/) and [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/).
646	
647	## Related
648	
649	- [Add clips to the timeline](/editing/add-clips/)
650	- [Trim clips](/editing/trimming/)
651	- [Close gaps and insert time](/editing/close-gaps/)

653	=== editing/inside-a-nest
654	---
655	title: "Work inside a nest"
656	description: "Open a nest to edit its clips in place, find your way back out, and see what stays project-wide while you're inside."
657	---
658	
659	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
660	
661	Open a [nest](/editing/nests/) to change the clips inside it without taking the group apart. The nest clip keeps its own position, scale, opacity, fades and volume, which [Un-nest](/editing/nests/#un-nest) would throw away.
662	
663	<AtAGlance
664	  menu={['Clip ▸ Open Nest', 'Clip ▸ Close Nest']}
665	  keys={['⌘↓', '⌘↑']}
666	  where={['Double-click a nest clip', 'The breadcrumb, in the corner above the track headers']}
667	  tools="set_scope"
668	/>
669	
670	## Open a nest
671	
672	Double-click a nest clip. You can also select one nest clip and choose **Clip ▸ Open Nest** (<kbd>⌘↓</kbd>).
673	
674	**Clip ▸ Open Nest** needs exactly one nest clip selected, so it's greyed out with two selected. A double-click works whatever else is selected, because it opens the clip you clicked.
675	
676	A nest can hold nests. Open one the same way from inside, down to eight levels.
677	
678	Because a double-click opens a nest clip, it can't rename one. Use **Clip ▸ Rename…** (<kbd>⇧⌘R</kbd>) or the name field in the Clip tab.
679	
680	## Come back out
681	
682	Choose **Clip ▸ Close Nest** (<kbd>⌘↑</kbd>), or click the [breadcrumb](#use-the-breadcrumb). Either one goes out one level, and the nest clip you went in through is selected again.
683	
684	**Clip ▸ Close Nest** is greyed out at the top level. **Open Nest** and **Close Nest** are both greyed out while you're typing in a field, so <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> and <kbd>⌘↑</kbd> stay with the text.
685	
686	## Use the breadcrumb
687	
688	While a nest is open, the corner above the track headers shows a path such as `Timeline › Intro`, with a back arrow in front of it.
689	
690	- It shows the last two levels: the one you'd return to, then the one you're in, in bold. Hover over it for the full path.
691	- A level is named after the nest clip you went in through, so renaming that clip changes the path.
692	- A long name is shortened in the middle, so `Lower Third 1` and `Lower Third 2` still look different.
693	
694	Click anywhere in the corner to go out one level, the same as <kbd>⌘↑</kbd>. A double-click counts as one click, so to go up two levels, click twice with a pause or press <kbd>⌘↑</kbd> twice.
695	
696	With no nest open, the corner is empty and does nothing.
697	
698	## What you see inside
699	
700	The timeline shows the nest's own tracks and clips, with time counted from the start of the nest. That's all of its contents, including anything the nest clip's [trim](/editing/nest-copies/#trim-a-nest-clip) is hiding on the outer timeline.
701	
702	The canvas shows the nest at its fixed size, without the nest clip's position, scale, opacity or fades, and you hear it without the nest clip's volume. You're seeing the group by itself, and the nest clip's settings apply again when you leave.
703	
704	## Where the playhead goes
705	
706	The playhead moves with you, so the frame under it doesn't change. It also carries back out. If a nest clip starts at 10 s and the playhead is at 12 s, you go in at 2 s. Move to 3 s, come out, and you're at 13 s.
707	
708	That holds while the playhead is over the nest clip. If it's before the clip when you double-click, you go in at the nest's first frame and come out at the clip's start. If it's past the clip's end, or you move past that point inside, the playhead is on a part of the nest the clip doesn't play, so the canvas inside shows a frame the outer timeline never will.
709	
710	Going in or out also stops playback.
711	
712	## Going in and out isn't an edit
713	
714	Opening or closing a nest makes no undo step and doesn't mark the project as changed.
715	
716	- **Selection:** going in clears the selection. Coming out selects the nest clip again.
717	- **In/out range:** it's cleared both ways, because a range means one thing inside a nest and another on the timeline. You can set a new [range](/timeline/in-out-range/) inside, and looping and Ripple Delete use it as they do on the timeline.
718	- **Reopening:** a project always opens on its timeline, even if you saved with a nest open.
719	
720	## Edit inside a nest
721	
722	Every clip edit works inside a nest, with times counted from the start of the nest. That includes **Clip ▸ Nest**, which makes a nest inside this one, and **Clip ▸ Un-nest**.
723	
724	Each edit is one step on the project's single undo history:
725	
726	- <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> after you've come out still undoes an edit you made inside.
727	- If an undo removes the nest you're in, you land in the deepest level that's left, and the in/out range clears.
728	
729	When more than one clip shows this nest, your edit reaches all of them. See [Shared copies](/editing/nest-copies/#shared-copies).
730	
731	The nest clip on the outer timeline keeps its length whatever you do inside. Material you add past its end stays hidden until you drag the clip's end out, and if the contents get shorter, the clip shows nothing over what's left of it.
732	
733	## What stays project-wide
734	
735	Some things belong to the project, not to the nest you have open. They still work, and they change the whole project.
736	
737	- **Media:** the Media tab lists the project's media. Adding, relinking or removing a file works as usual. Drag a row from the Media tab onto the nest's timeline to put its clip in the nest. A file dragged from the Finder onto the timeline opens as a project of its own, so add it on the Media tab first.
738	- **The Document tab:** it shows the project's settings. Changing the project's size doesn't change the nest's size, which is [fixed](/editing/nests/#a-nests-size-is-fixed).
739	- **Markers:** the Document tab's list stays, but the ruler shows none. You can still rename a marker, change its **Chapter** box or delete it. See [Markers](/timeline/markers/).
740	- **Export:** **File ▸ Export…** writes the whole timeline, not the nest. A range you set inside a nest can't be used, so the **Range** pop-up stays on **Whole project**. Close the nest and set the range on the timeline.
741	
742	**File ▸ Save Frame…** is the exception: it saves what the canvas shows, so with a nest open you get a frame of the nest.
743	
744	## What you can't use inside a nest
745	
746	| Command | While a nest is open |
747	| --- | --- |
748	| **Mark ▸ Add Marker**, **Next Marker**, **Previous Marker** | Greyed out, and <kbd>M</kbd> beeps. **Go** in the Document tab's Markers list is greyed out too. A marker's time is on the outer timeline, and the playhead inside a nest counts from the nest's start. |
749	| **Insert ▸ Adjustment Clip** | Greyed out. An [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) only works on the timeline, never inside a nest. |
750	| **Insert ▸ Text Behind Subject** | Greyed out, and the Picture tab has no **Behind Subject** section. See [Text Behind Subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/). |
751	| **File ▸ New Project from Range…** | Greyed out. See [New Project from Range](/projects/new-project-from-range/). |
752	| **File ▸ Make Vertical Version…** | Greyed out. See [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/). |
753	| **File ▸ Rename Graphic…** | Greyed out. See [Rename, delete and restore graphics](/graphics/manage-graphics/). |
754	| **Track ▸ Mix…** | **Compressor** and **Limit peaks** are greyed out, because a nest's mix plays through the track that holds the nest clip. The track's volume and pan still work. |
755	
756	## Limits count the whole project
757	
758	A project holds up to 4,096 clips and 64 tracks, and nests go eight levels deep. Clips and tracks are counted across the timeline and every nest together, and the depth is counted from the timeline. So an edit that looks fine inside a nest can still take the whole project over. When it would, Frame Job shows an alert naming the limit and changes nothing.
759	
760	A nest's contents count once, however many clips show it. Un-nest the last clip showing a nest to take its tracks out of the count. Deleting that clip instead leaves the nest's clips and tracks counted.
761	
762	## With an agent
763	
764	An agent can open a nest in the window with `set_scope`, as you would. This only changes the view, so it adds no undo step, and `set_scope` with no arguments comes back out. Given a nest two clips show, it goes in through the earlier one.
765	
766	An agent can also edit inside any nest without opening it, by naming the nest on the edit. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/), which lists the edits that can't be made that way.
767	
768	## Related

775	=== editing/move-clips
776	---
777	title: "Move clips"
778	description: Drag clips along the timeline and between tracks, alone or together, and see what stops a drop.
779	---
780	
781	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
782	
783	Drag a clip to change when it plays or which track it sits on. The clip you see moving while you drag is the real edit, not a stand-in.
784	
785	<AtAGlance
786	  where="Timeline ▸ drag a clip's body"
787	  tools="move_clip"
788	/>
789	
790	## Drag a clip
791	
792	Drag a clip's body left or right to move it in time, and up or down to move it to another track. A clip stops at the start of the timeline.
793	
794	The drag [snaps](/timeline/snapping/) to nearby edits when snapping is on. Hold <kbd>⌘</kbd> during the drag to turn snapping off for that moment.
795	
796	You can't start a drag on a clip on a [locked track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/).
797	
798	To drag a copy and leave the original, hold <kbd>⌥</kbd> as you press. See [Duplicate clips](/editing/duplicate-clips/).
799	
800	## Move several clips together
801	
802	Select the clips, then drag any one of them. They all move, and they stay the same time and the same number of tracks apart. If the earliest clip reaches the start of the timeline, it stops at 0 and the others keep their distance from it.
803	
804	## Move a clip to a new track
805	
806	Let go above the top lane to make a new track at the front, or below the bottom lane to make a new track at the back. The new track and the move are one undo step.
807	
808	## Clips that come along
809	
810	A clip's linked partner, such as its [detached sound](/audio/detach-and-attach/), moves in time by the same amount and keeps its own track. So you can drag a sound onto a track of its own and its picture stays on its track. A partner on a locked track doesn't move.
811	
812	## Overlaps make a transition
813	
814	If you drop a clip so that it overlaps the clip before it on the track, it gets a Cross Dissolve over the overlap, unless it already has a transition. The overlap has to keep to the [overlap rule](/editing/how-edits-work/#the-overlap-rule).
815	
816	## When a drop won't go where you let go
817	
818	While you drag, the clip only goes where the project allows. Over a position that would break the [overlap rule](/editing/how-edits-work/#the-overlap-rule), it waits at the last position that was allowed, and catches up when you reach one that is.
819	
820	If you let go over a position that isn't allowed, the clip stays at that last allowed position, and a ghost of it slides there from where you let go. If it never reached an allowed position, it's back where it started and nothing has changed. There's no beep and no message.
821	
822	## One undo step per drag
823	
824	A whole drag is one undo step, however long it lasts. **Edit ▸ Undo** (<kbd>⌘Z</kbd>) names it Move Clips. A click that doesn't move the clip adds no undo step.
825	
826	## Good to know
827	
828	- A locked clip that's part of a selection moves with the others if you start the drag on an unlocked clip.
829	- Clips selected on more than one track can't make a new track at the front. Let go above the top lane and they stay at the last allowed position. Below the bottom lane works.
830	- With 64 tracks in the project, there's no new track to make. A drop above or below the lanes moves the clips in time only.
831	- To shift clips by an exact number of frames, [nudge them](/editing/nudge-clips/).
832	
833	## With an agent
834	
835	`move_clip` takes the clips and how far to shift them, where a negative shift moves them earlier. Give it a track to move them there as well, and leave that out to keep them on their tracks. Like a drag, it won't break the overlap rule. See [Tools: moving and trimming](/mcp/tools-move-and-trim/#move_clip).
836	
837	## Related
838	
839	- [Select clips](/timeline/selecting-clips/)
840	- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
841	- [Nudge clips](/editing/nudge-clips/)
842	- [Duplicate clips](/editing/duplicate-clips/)

1	=== editing/nest-copies
2	---
3	title: "Shared and independent nest copies"
4	description: "Know which copies of a nest clip edit together, make a copy of your own, and see what trimming a nest clip really does."
5	---
6	
7	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
8	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
9	
10	A nest clip is a view of a [nest](/editing/nests/), not the nest itself. Two clips can show one nest, so an edit inside it reaches both. This page covers which copies share their contents, how to get one that doesn't, and what a trim does to a nest clip.
11	
12	<AtAGlance
13	  menu={['Edit ▸ Duplicate', 'Clip ▸ Split', 'Clip ▸ Un-nest', 'Clip ▸ Nest']}
14	  keys={['⌘D', '⌘T', '⇧⌘G', '⌘G']}
15	  where="⌥-drag a nest clip"
16	  tools={['duplicate', 'split', 'paste', 'unnest', 'nest']}
17	/>
18	
19	## Shared copies
20	
21	These all leave you with clips that show one nest:
22	
23	| Do this | You get |
24	| --- | --- |
25	| **Edit ▸ Duplicate** (<kbd>⌘D</kbd>) | A second clip showing the same nest, straight after the selection. |
26	| <kbd>⌥</kbd>-drag a nest clip | A second clip showing the same nest, where you drop it. |
27	| **Clip ▸ Split** (<kbd>⌘T</kbd>) | Two clips showing the same nest, cut at the playhead. |
28	
29	[Open](/editing/inside-a-nest/#open-a-nest) any of them and edit, and every clip showing that nest changes.
30	
31	Only the contents are shared. Each nest clip keeps its own place on the timeline, its own length, and its own position, scale, opacity, fades and volume.
32	
33	[Un-nesting](/editing/nests/#un-nest) one clip gives you its contents as ordinary clips and leaves the others showing the nest. The nest goes when you un-nest the last clip that shows it.
34	
35	:::caution[A split nest clip starts again]
36	A nest clip always plays from the nest's first frame. So when you split one, the second part starts from the top of the nest, not from where you cut, and the join shows. The same goes for anything else that cuts through a nest clip, such as a ripple delete over a range.
37	
38	To cut the contents at a moment, [open the nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/) and split inside it.
39	:::
40	
41	## Make an independent copy
42	
43	To get a copy you can edit on its own, turn a duplicate back into clips and nest them again.
44	
45	<Steps>
46	
47	1. Select the nest clip and press <kbd>⌘D</kbd>. The selection stays on the original.
48	
49	2. Click the new copy, then press <kbd>⇧⌘G</kbd> to un-nest it. Its contents come out as ordinary clips, all selected.
50	
51	3. Press <kbd>⌘G</kbd>. Those clips become a new nest of their own.
52	
53	</Steps>
54	
55	Un-nesting drops the copy's own position, scale, opacity, fades and volume, so set those again on the new nest clip. The new nest also takes the project's current size, which may differ from the original's. Un-nesting gives back everything in the nest, so a [trim](#trim-a-nest-clip) on the copy is gone too.
56	
57	This separates one level. A nest clip among the contents still shows the same inner nest as the original, so an edit inside that inner nest reaches both. Un-nest it too, before step 3, if you need it separate.
58	
59	:::caution[Copy and Paste don't work on a nest clip]
60	**Edit ▸ Copy** puts the nest clip on the clipboard but not what's inside it. **Edit ▸ Paste** then pastes nothing and shows an alert saying the pasted clip shows a nest "which the payload does not carry". That's true of any selection with a nest clip in it, in this project or another one.
61	
62	**Edit ▸ Cut** still removes the clip, so after a failed paste, press <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> until it's back.
63	:::
64	
65	## Trim a nest clip
66	
67	Trimming a nest clip changes how much of the nest plays. It never cuts anything out of the nest. The clip always plays from the nest's first frame for as long as the clip lasts, which makes its two edges behave differently from a media clip's:
68	
69	| Drag | What happens |
70	| --- | --- |
71	| The end edge in | The tail of the nest is hidden. |
72	| The end edge out | More of the nest plays. Past the end of the contents, the clip shows nothing. The contents set no limit on how far you can drag. |
73	| The start edge later | The clip starts later and the whole nest moves later with it. The opening still plays, and the tail is what gets hidden. |
74	| The start edge earlier | The nest moves earlier with it, and more of the tail plays. |
75	
76	So you can't hide a nest's opening with a trim. To do that, [open the nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/) and edit inside it, which changes every clip showing the nest.
77	
78	**Clip ▸ Un-nest** (<kbd>⇧⌘G</kbd>) gives back everything, however short the clip was trimmed. Hidden clips come back where they sit in the nest, counted from the nest clip's start, even past the clip's end. One that would then collide with what's after it goes on a new track in front.
79	
80	## With an agent
81	
82	An agent can make the independent copy in one step. `paste` makes a separate nest when it's given the nest's contents as well as the clip, with every level inside it, and editing the copy leaves the original alone. See [Tools: copying and nesting](/mcp/tools-copy-and-nest/).
83

92	=== editing/nests
93	---
94	title: Nests
95	description: Collapse several clips into one clip that moves, trims, fades and transforms as a group, and open it back out when you're done.
96	---
97	
98	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
99	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
100	
101	A nest collapses several clips into one clip that stands for the group. From then on the group moves, trims, fades and transforms as one thing, and the clips inside stay as you built them.
102	
103	<AtAGlance
104	  menu={['Clip ▸ Nest', 'Clip ▸ Un-nest']}
105	  keys={['⌘G', '⇧⌘G']}
106	  tools={['nest', 'unnest', 'set_clip']}
107	/>
108	
109	## Make a nest
110	
111	<Steps>
112	
113	1. Select the clips.
114	
115	2. Press <kbd>⌘G</kbd>, or choose **Clip ▸ Nest**.
116	
117	</Steps>
118	
119	The clips are replaced by one nest clip, which is selected so you can move or transform it straight away. The nest is one undo step, called Nest.
120	
121	The nest clip goes on the front-most track the selection used, and runs from the earliest start to the latest end, including any gaps. A matte track is the exception: the nest clip goes on the front-most track that isn't a matte, and a matte only stays one inside the nest if the track it cuts goes in with it. See [Mattes inside nests](/canvas/mattes-in-nests/).
122	
123	A clip's [detached sound](/audio/detach-and-attach/) goes in with it, unless the sound is on a locked track.
124	
125	To work on the contents later, double-click the nest clip. See [Work inside a nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/).
126	
127	## What a nest keeps
128	
129	Inside the nest, clips keep their properties, [actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/) and transitions, their timing relative to each other and their stacking order. The earliest clip starts at 0 on the nest's own timeline.
130	
131	The tracks inside are new, and each keeps the name, the hidden, muted, locked and solo states, and the volume and pan of the track it came from. There are two exceptions:
132	
133	- The track the nest clip lands on still applies its volume and pan over the whole nest clip, so its copy inside starts at full volume and centred. A selection from one track sounds the same nested.
134	- A track [compressor or limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/) isn't copied inside. The one on the nest clip's own track goes on working over the nest clip.
135	
136	The nest clip itself starts at the default position and scale, at full opacity. It has a **Sound** tab only when something inside can make a sound.
137	
138	## Name a nest
139	
140	Nests are named `Nest 1`, `Nest 2` and so on. To give a nest clip your own name, select it and press <kbd>⇧⌘R</kbd> (**Clip ▸ Rename…**), or use the name field at the top of the Clip tab.
141	
142	A double-click on a nest clip opens it, so it doesn't start a rename as it does on other clips.
143	
144	## A nest's size is fixed
145	
146	A nest's canvas is fixed at the project's size at the moment you nest. Changing the [project's size](/projects/canvas-size/) later doesn't re-lay out what's inside, and opening the nest lets you edit its contents but not its size.
147	
148	To change a nest's size:
149	
150	<Steps>
151	
152	1. Press <kbd>⇧⌘G</kbd> to un-nest it.
153	
154	2. Change the project size if you need to.
155	
156	3. Press <kbd>⌘G</kbd> to nest it again.
157	
158	</Steps>
159	
160	## Un-nest
161	
162	Select one or more nest clips and press <kbd>⇧⌘G</kbd>, or choose **Clip ▸ Un-nest**. The item is available when the selection includes a nest clip, and anything else selected is left alone.
163	
164	Every selected nest clip opens back out in one undo step, called Un-nest, or Un-nest Clips for several. What came out is selected.
165	
166	- Clips return at the nest clip's start plus their own times, on tracks counted back from the nest clip's track. Missing tracks are added behind it.
167	- A clip that would break the [overlap rule](/editing/how-edits-work/#the-overlap-rule) goes on a new front track and isn't lost.
168	- A nest clip trimmed shorter than its contents still gives everything back, because trimming a nest hides content and doesn't cut it.
169	- If other clips show the same nest, they keep it. See [Shared and independent nest copies](/editing/nest-copies/).
170	
171	:::caution
172	Un-nesting discards the nest clip's own transform, opacity, fades and volume. To change the contents and keep those, [open the nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/) and edit inside it.
173	:::
174	
175	The settings of the tracks inside the nest don't come out either. Clips that return take on the settings of the timeline tracks they land on.
176	
177	## Nests inside nests
178	
179	A nest can hold other nests, up to eight levels deep. Select a nest clip with other clips and press <kbd>⌘G</kbd>, or press it while a nest is open.
180	
181	The depth counts the whole project, even while you edit inside a nest, so an edit that looks fine there can still stop at the limit. The same goes for the project's limits of 64 tracks and 4,096 clips, and a nest's own tracks count towards the 64.
182	
183	## When Nest won't work
184	
185	**Clip ▸ Nest** is greyed out with nothing selected, and when the only selected clip is already a nest clip, since wrapping one nest in another on its own changes nothing you can see.
186	
187	With the item available, two things can still stop a nest. Frame Job beeps, changes nothing, and gives the reason at the foot of the inspector.
188	
189	- **Something unselected is in the way.** The nest clip would overlap a clip you didn't select on its track, by more than the [overlap rule](/editing/how-edits-work/#the-overlap-rule) allows. This often means an unselected clip sits inside the span. Select it too, or move it.
190	- **The selection holds an adjustment clip.** An [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) can't go inside a nest.
191	
192	If the nest clip overlaps the clip before it by an amount the rule allows, it gets a Cross Dissolve over the overlap. See [Transitions](/motion/transitions/).
193	
194	## With an agent
195	
196	`nest` can name the nest as it's made, `set_clip` renames a nest clip, and `get_project` lists every nest with its own tracks and clips. `unnest` opens one nest clip at a time, and gives an error on any other kind of clip. The clips it brings back are new clips, with new ids. See [Tools: copying and nesting](/mcp/tools-copy-and-nest/#nest) and [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/).
197	
198	## Related
199	
200	- [Work inside a nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/)
201	- [Shared and independent nest copies](/editing/nest-copies/)
202	- [Mattes inside nests](/canvas/mattes-in-nests/)
203	=== editing/nudge-clips
204	---
205	title: "Nudge clips"
206	description: Move the selected clips one or ten frames at a time from the keyboard.
207	---
208	
209	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
210	
211	A nudge moves the selected clips by an exact number of frames, for the small corrections that are hard to make with a drag.
212	
213	<AtAGlance keys={[',', '.', '⇧,', '⇧.']} tools="move_clip" />
214	
215	## Nudge the selection
216	
217	| Keys | Moves the selection |
218	| --- | --- |
219	| <kbd>,</kbd> | One frame earlier |
220	| <kbd>.</kbd> | One frame later |
221	| <kbd>⇧,</kbd> | Ten frames earlier |
222	| <kbd>⇧.</kbd> | Ten frames later |
223	
224	On a US keyboard, <kbd>⇧,</kbd> and <kbd>⇧.</kbd> are the keys that type `<` and `>`.
225	
226	Each press is one undo step, Nudge Clips. These keys have no <kbd>⌘</kbd>, so while a text field has the focus they type into it instead. See [Keys and typing](/getting-started/keys-and-typing/).
227	
228	## Good to know
229	
230	A nudge is an ordinary [move](/editing/move-clips/), with the same rules:
231	
232	- It beeps with nothing selected.
233	- A nudge that would break the [overlap rule](/editing/how-edits-work/#the-overlap-rule) beeps and changes nothing, and the reason appears at the foot of the inspector. A nudge that lands on a small enough overlap makes a Cross Dissolve.
234	- The earliest clip stops at the start of the timeline, so <kbd>⇧,</kbd> on a clip three frames from the start moves it three frames. A clip already at the start beeps.
235	- A linked partner on an unlocked track moves with its clip.
236	
237	Unlike a drag, a nudge moves a selected clip on a [locked track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/). It doesn't snap, and it never changes a clip's track.
238	
239	## With an agent
240	
241	An agent nudges with `move_clip`, giving the shift as a time. See [Tools: moving and trimming](/mcp/tools-move-and-trim/#move_clip).
242	
243	## Related

249	---
250	title: Paste Attributes
251	description: Copy one clip's look and sound settings onto any number of other clips in a single step.
252	---
253	
254	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
255	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
256	
257	Paste Attributes makes other clips look and sound like the one you copied. Set up one clip, then give the same settings to the rest in one undo step.
258	
259	<AtAGlance
260	  menu="Edit ▸ Paste Attributes"
261	  keys="⌥⌘V"
262	  tools="paste_attributes"
263	/>
264	
265	## Paste a clip's attributes
266	
267	<Steps>
268	
269	1. Select the clip that has the settings you want and press <kbd>⌘C</kbd>.
270	
271	2. Select the clips that should take them.
272	
273	3. Press <kbd>⌥⌘V</kbd>, or choose **Edit ▸ Paste Attributes**.
274	
275	</Steps>
276	
277	The item is available when Frame Job clips are on the clipboard and something is selected. If nothing would change, Frame Job beeps. The paste is one undo step, called Paste Attributes.
278	
279	If you copied several clips, only one of them counts: the one that starts earliest. At the same start it's the one on the front-most track.
280	
281	## What travels
282	
283	Settings travel in four groups, and a group is only copied when both clips have it. A movie's settings pasted onto a text clip bring its picture settings and leave the text styling alone, and its sound settings go nowhere.
284	
285	Each group replaces the target's whole group, so it isn't a merge. A shadow on the target disappears if the copied clip had none.
286	
287	| Group | What travels | What the target keeps |
288	| --- | --- | --- |
289	| **Video** | Everything about the picture: position, scale, rotation, opacity, crop, corner radius, blend mode, shadow, reflection, filters, spotlight, obscure regions, chroma key, Remove Background, Text Behind Subject, Hide While Silent, motion presets, motion blur, the grade and its look, and the [drawn cursor's](/recording/cursor-settings/) settings | Nothing, apart from an adjustment clip's [qualifier](#adjustment-clips-and-qualifiers) |
290	| **Audio** | Everything about the sound: volume, Mute, fades and their shapes, pan, Mix to mono, channels, Keep pitch, ducking, noise reduction, voice isolation, EQ, hum removal, gate, de-esser, leveller, compressor, limiter and voice effects | Nothing |
291	| **Text** | Font, size, colours, alignment, spacing, case, outline, backdrop, text box width, reveal animation and word caption style | Its own words and their timings |
292	| **Shape** | Fill, stroke, gradient, corner radius and arrowheads | Its kind, its size and the end points of a line |
293	
294	:::caution
295	The Video group includes position and scale. Pasting onto a clip you've already placed moves it to where the copied clip sits.
296	:::
297	
298	A look's `.cube` file comes along too, so a grade pasted from another project keeps its LUT.
299	
300	## What stays on the target
301	
302	Paste Attributes copies how a clip looks and sounds, not what makes it that clip. The target keeps:
303	
304	- its place on the timeline and its length
305	- its speed, including a [speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/)
306	- its [actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/), so nothing animated travels
307	- its transition
308	- its name and label
309	- which halves are [switched on](/editing/enable-picture-and-sound/)
310	
311	Graphic properties don't travel either. Use [Paste Graphic Properties](/graphics/copy-properties/) for those.
312	
313	## Adjustment clips and qualifiers
314	
315	A qualifier belongs to an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/), so it follows the kind of clip:
316	
317	| Pasting | The qualifier |
318	| --- | --- |
319	| Onto an ordinary clip | Is dropped |
320	| From an ordinary clip onto an adjustment clip | Stays as the adjustment clip had it |
321	| From one adjustment clip onto another | Is copied |
322	
323	See [Copy a grade](/color/copy-a-grade/) for moving a grade between clips.
324	
325	## When a paste stops
326	
327	Some picture settings can't land on some kinds of clip. When one can't, Frame Job shows an error saying why and changes nothing, even on the other selected clips.
328	
329	| The target | Can't take |
330	| --- | --- |
331	| An adjustment clip | Blur, sharpen or pixelate filters, a blend mode, Remove Background, Text Behind Subject, motion blur |
332	| A nest clip | A blend mode, Remove Background, Text Behind Subject, motion blur, Hide While Silent |
333	| A text, shape or graphic clip | Remove Background |
334	| A movie or still clip | Remove Background with its subject set to Foreground, which only an image clip can take |
335	| Any clip except a text or adjustment clip | A crop that would leave nothing of it, such as one copied from a much larger source |
336	
337	To get past one, take the setting off the copied clip, copy it again and paste, or select only the clips that can take it.
338	
339	## With an agent
340	
341	`paste_attributes` can do two things the menu item can't.
342	
343	- **Choose the groups.** `groups` names which ones travel, out of `video`, `audio`, `text`, `shape` and `graphic`, so `["audio"]` pastes the sound alone and leaves the picture settings. Left out, it behaves as the menu item does, and `graphic` only travels when it's named. An empty list won't run.
344	- **Skip what doesn't fit.** A named group that either side lacks normally stops the paste with an error. With `skip_missing` on, a group the copied clip lacks is dropped and a clip that can't take a group is skipped, so a mixed selection goes through. It's off by default, and only applies with `groups`.
345	
346	See [Tools: copying and nesting](/mcp/tools-copy-and-nest/#paste_attributes).
347	
348	## Related
349

351	- [Copy a grade](/color/copy-a-grade/)
352	- [Paste Graphic Properties](/graphics/copy-properties/)

354	=== editing/slip-and-roll
355	---
356	title: "Slip and roll"
357	description: "Change which footage a clip shows, or move the cut between two clips, without moving anything else on the timeline."
358	---
359	
360	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
361	
362	Slip and roll are for fine-tuning once your clips are where they belong. A slip changes which part of the file a clip shows. A roll moves the cut between two clips. Neither moves any other clip.
363	
364	<AtAGlance
365	  keys={['⌥⇧-drag body', '⌥⇧-drag edge']}
366	  where="The timeline"
367	  tools={['slip', 'roll', 'trim_start', 'trim_end']}
368	/>
369	
370	## Slip a clip
371	
372	Hold <kbd>⌥⇧</kbd> and drag the body of a clip. The clip stays where it is at the same length, and the footage slides underneath it. Drag right to show later footage and left to show earlier footage.
373	
374	The whole drag is one undo step, named Slip. It doesn't change the selection, so you can slip a clip without selecting it.
375	
376	- A slip stops when the clip reaches either end of its file, and keeps what it reached. It doesn't turn into a trim. If there's no footage to slide into, the drag changes nothing.
377	- It moves in whole frames and never snaps, because the timeline's snap points mean nothing inside the footage.
378	- The footage moves at the clip's speed. At ×2, dragging one frame slides the footage two frames.
379	- A [freeze frame](/speed/freeze-frame/) slips too, which changes the frame it holds. It stops one frame short of the end of its file.
380	- A linked sound clip on an unlocked track slips with its picture, so the two stay in sync. They move by the smaller of the two distances they each have room for.
381	
382	Only clips that play a file have footage to slide. The drag does nothing on text, a shape, a picture, a graphic or a nest.
383	
384	## Roll a cut
385	
386	Hold <kbd>⌥⇧</kbd> and drag a clip's edge, the outer 7 points of the clip. The cut moves: one clip gets longer and the other gets shorter by the same amount, and the outer edges of the pair stay where they are.
387	
388	| Edge you drag | Cut that moves |
389	| --- | --- |
390	| The clip's start | The cut with the clip before it |
391	| The clip's end | The cut with the clip after it |
392	
393	The whole drag is one undo step, named Roll.
394	
395	- A roll [snaps](/timeline/snapping/) like a trim. Hold <kbd>⌘</kbd> during the drag to stop snapping.
396	- Each clip keeps at least one frame.
397	- A clip that plays a file can't grow past what the file has. Text, shapes and pictures have no such limit.
398	- A roll needs two clips that touch exactly. With a gap at that edge there's no cut to move, and with an overlap there's a [transition](/motion/transition-settings/), whose length you set in its own section. Either way the drag does nothing.
399	- A clip under about 21 points wide on screen has no edges to grab, and the drag slips it instead. [Zoom in](/timeline/zoom-and-scroll/) first.
400	
401	When you roll a picture's cut, a linked sound clip rolls with it, as long as it starts at the same point, it touches a clip before it, and its track is unlocked.
402	
403	## Move a sound clip's edge alone
404	
405	A [detached sound clip](/audio/detach-and-attach/) that's still linked to its picture can move an edge on its own. This is how a [J-cut or L-cut](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/) is made. These move only the sound's edge and leave the picture where it is:
406	
407	- Drag the sound clip's edge.
408	- Select it and press <kbd>W</kbd> or <kbd>E</kbd> to [trim it to the playhead](/editing/trimming/).
409	- Hold <kbd>⌥⇧</kbd> and drag the sound clip's edge to roll its cut.
410	
411	It works in that direction only. Trimming or rolling the picture's edge also moves the sound's edge when the two line up, and a slip always takes both.
412	
413	## What happens to actions and timed words
414	
415	A slip leaves [actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/) where they are, because only the footage inside the clip moves.
416	
417	A roll leaves each clip's actions at the same distance from that clip's start. So on the clip after the cut, the actions move with the cut along the timeline. On the clip before it, they stay put, and if that clip gets shorter it can end before an action does.
418	
419	Timed caption words are the exception. They stay on the speech they time, so a roll doesn't shift them against the sound. A [graphic](/graphics/size-and-timing/) after the cut stays in step too: its **In** moves with the cut.
420	
421	## Good to know
422	
423	- Neither gesture works on a locked track. The drag does nothing. A linked clip on a locked track stays put while the clip you drag moves.
424	- On a clip with a [speed ramp](/speed/edit-a-ramped-clip/), the actions stay where they are and the limits come from the ramp, so a cut stops rolling where the clip would no longer fit its file.
425	
426	## With an agent
427	
428	`slip` takes a clip and how far to slide, and a positive distance shows later footage. Where the drag does nothing on text, a shape, a picture, a graphic or a nest, the tool gives an error.
429	
430	`roll` takes the clip to the right of the cut and the time the cut moves to. If no clip on the track ends where that clip begins, it gives an error saying so.
431	
432	With `alone`, `roll` moves a picture's cut and leaves a lined-up linked sound on an unlocked track where it is. No gesture can do that. `trim_start` and `trim_end` take `alone` too, to move one clip's edge without its partner's. See [Tools: moving and trimming](/mcp/tools-move-and-trim/).
433	
434	## Related
435	
436	- [Trim clips](/editing/trimming/)
437	- [J-cuts and L-cuts](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/)
438	- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
439	- [How edits move actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/)
440	=== editing/split-at-shot-changes
441	---
442	title: "Split at Shot Changes"
443	description: "Cut a finished edit, a download or a stream recording into one clip per shot, with the cuts found on your Mac."
444	---
445	
446	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
447	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
448	
449	Split at Shot Changes takes a clip that already has cuts in it, such as a finished edit, a downloaded clip or a stream recording, and cuts it at each one, giving you one clip per shot.
450	
451	<AtAGlance
452	  menu="Clip ▸ Split at Shot Changes"
453	  tools={['split_at_shots', 'get_media_analysis']}
454	  needs="Nothing. The cuts are found on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
455	/>
456	
457	## Split a clip at its shot changes
458	
459	<Steps>
460	
461	1. Select one or more clips that show a video file's picture.
462	
463	2. Choose **Clip ▸ Split at Shot Changes**. It has no shortcut.
464	
465	3. If Frame Job hasn't looked at this footage yet, wait for the [Analyzing sheet](#while-the-cuts-are-found) to finish.
466	
467	</Steps>
468	
469	Each selected clip is cut at every hard cut inside the part of the file it plays. All the cuts are one undo step, named Split at Shot Changes.
470	
471	The command is greyed out until a selected clip shows a video file's picture. Anything else in the selection is left alone: text, an image, a freeze frame, an audio file, a nest, or a clip with its [picture turned off](/editing/enable-picture-and-sound/).
472	
473	If the footage holds no shot change inside any selected clip, Frame Job beeps and nothing changes.
474	
475	## While the cuts are found
476	
477	When the footage has already been read, the split lands at once. Otherwise the **Analyzing** sheet appears, with one row per file:
478	
479	| A file's row reads | What it means |
480	| --- | --- |
481	| Waiting | Its first frame hasn't been read yet. |
482	| A percentage, with a bar | How much has been read. |
483	| Done | Its cuts have been found. |
484	
485	The split lands as soon as every file is done. Editing commands are off while the sheet is up.
486	
487	**Stop** closes the sheet and changes nothing. Frame Job saves what it has found every 30 seconds or so, and that stays in the cache, so a long file doesn't start from nothing next time.
488	
489	If the project changes anyway while the sheet is up, for example through an agent, nothing is split, and the inspector says to choose the command again.
490	
491	## What counts as a hard cut
492	
493	A hard cut is a change from one picture to another between two frames. Frame Job compares each frame's colours with those of the frames before it. It's a plain measurement of the picture, with no machine learning, so the same footage always gives the same cuts.
494	
495	- A gradual dissolve isn't a cut.
496	- A single flash frame isn't a cut, because the picture after it matches the one before.
497	- A dissolve between flat-coloured pictures, such as slides or title cards, can be found as one cut.
498	- Two shots with very similar colours can be missed, because the comparison looks at colour rather than at what's in the frame.
499	- Of two cuts within 12 frames of each other in the file, only the stronger is found.
500	
501	## Found on this Mac and cached
502	
503	Shot changes are found on your Mac. Nothing is sent anywhere and you don't need a key.
504	
505	The results are kept in the project's cache, so a second split of the same footage starts at once. See [On-device media analysis](/projects/media-analysis/).
506	
507	## Where the cuts land
508	
509	Each cut lands on the project's frame grid, worked out through the clip's speed, [speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/) and [reversal](/speed/reverse/). In a project whose frame rate differs from the file's, that's the nearest project frame.
510	
511	A cut within one frame of either end of a clip isn't made, so you won't get a piece one frame long at a clip's edge.
512	
513	Each cut is an ordinary [split](/editing/splitting/), so actions, word timings and graphics divide the same way.
514	
515	## Locked tracks and linked sound
516	
517	A selected clip on a locked track is still cut. Its linked sound is cut with it when the sound's track is unlocked, as with [Split](/editing/splitting/#linked-sound).
518	
519	## The clip ceiling
520	
521	A project holds up to 4,096 clips, counting the clips inside nests. If the splits would pass that, nothing is split at all, and the inspector says how many clips the command would add and how many more would fit. The count includes each linked clip the splits also cut.
522	
523	## When it can't run
524	
525	Frame Job beeps and gives the reason at the foot of the inspector:
526	
527	| What happened | What to do |
528	| --- | --- |
529	| A file is missing or can't be read | [Relink it](/projects/relink-media/), then choose the command again. |
530	| The analysis of a file failed | The message names the file and the reason. Nothing is split. |
531	| The analysis is no longer in the project's cache | Choose the command again, and Frame Job reads the file again. |
532	
533	## With an agent
534	
535	`split_at_shots` works on the clips it's given, and lists any it can't cut under `skipped`. Without a list, it takes every clip of a video file on an unlocked track, so a clip on a locked track is cut only when it's named. It shows no sheet. It waits up to 60 seconds for the cuts, and if they aren't ready it stops without splitting and keeps what it has saved so far, so calling it again carries on.
536	
537	With no cut inside any clip, it reports that no clips were added and leaves no undo step. See [Tools: cutting and deleting](/mcp/tools-cut-and-delete/#split_at_shots).
538	
539	`get_media_analysis`, with the kind `shots`, reads a file's cuts without splitting anything. See [Tools: reading analysis](/mcp/tools-analysis/).
540	
541	## Related
542	
543	- [Split clips](/editing/splitting/)
544	- [On-device media analysis](/projects/media-analysis/)
545	- [Select clips](/timeline/selecting-clips/)
546	- [Delete, Ripple Delete and Lift](/editing/delete-clips/)
547	=== editing/splitting
548	---
549	title: "Split clips"
550	description: "Cut clips in two at the playhead, and see what each piece keeps of the footage, actions, word timings and graphics."
551	---
552	
553	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
554	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
555	
556	Split cuts a clip in two at the playhead, so you can trim, move or remove one piece without touching the other.
557	
558	<AtAGlance
559	  menu="Clip ▸ Split"
560	  keys="⌘T"
561	  where="The scissors button in the timeline bar"
562	  tools="split"
563	/>
564	
565	## Split at the playhead
566	
567	<Steps>
568	
569	1. Move the playhead to the frame you want to cut on.
570	
571	2. Select the clips to cut, or select nothing to cut everything under the playhead.
572	
573	3. Press <kbd>⌘T</kbd>, choose **Clip ▸ Split**, or click the scissors button in the timeline bar.
574	
575	</Steps>
576	
577	| What's selected | What gets cut |
578	| --- | --- |
579	| One or more clips | Each selected clip the playhead is inside |
580	| Nothing | Every clip under the playhead on every unlocked track |
581	
582	It's one undo step, named Split, however many clips it cuts. The command is available whenever the timeline has clips.
583	
584	The playhead has to be strictly inside a clip. A playhead sitting exactly on a clip's edge is at a cut already, so that clip is left alone. If nothing can be cut, Frame Job beeps and nothing changes.
585	
586	A clip on a locked track is left alone when nothing is selected, but it's still cut if you selected it.
587	
588	## Footage stays continuous
589	
590	The second piece carries on playing the footage from where the first stopped, at the same speed, so the split doesn't show when you play it back. If an action is animating the clip, the second piece starts from where that animation had got to at the cut, such as its position or volume. It keeps the clip's name, label and settings.
591	
592	On a clip with a [speed ramp](/speed/edit-a-ramped-clip/), the two pieces meet at exactly the same point in the footage, and the second starts at the rate in force at the cut.
593	
594	## Linked sound
595	
596	A [linked clip](/audio/detach-and-attach/) on an unlocked track is cut too, when the playhead is inside it, and the two second halves are linked to each other.
597	
598	If the linked clip isn't cut, because its track is locked or the playhead isn't inside it, it stays linked to whichever piece shares more of its time. The other piece isn't linked to anything.
599	
600	## Actions and word timings
601	
602	[Actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/) stay with the piece they fall in:
603	
604	- An action that ends at or before the cut stays on the first piece.
605	- An action that starts at or after the cut moves to the second piece.
606	- An action that spans the cut becomes two. The first half ends at the value it had reached at the cut, and the second carries on to the original target, so the join doesn't show. Both keep the action's curve.
607	
608	An [entrance and exit preset](/motion/entrances-and-exits/) is tied to the clip's ends, so the first piece keeps the entrance and the second keeps the exit. A [text reveal](/text-and-shapes/text-reveal/) divides the same way. Otherwise the clip would leave at the cut and arrive again on the far side of it.
609	
610	Caption word timings stay on their words. Both pieces keep the full text, the first with its timings as they were and the second with its timings moved to match its new start.
611	
612	The one exception is a text clip whose wording an action changes. If the second piece's text at the cut no longer has the same number of words as its timings, the second piece loses its word timings and shows its text all at once.
613	
614	## Split a graphic
615	
616	A [graphic](/graphics/size-and-timing/) carries on across the cut rather than starting again, and plays its outro once, at the true end.
617	
618	The graphic's **In** on the second piece starts at the cut, so it picks up where the first piece left off. Both pieces keep the original's **Length**, so an outro still plays at the same moment. That pins the length, so **Follow Clip** is off on both pieces afterwards.
619	
620	Trimming the start of a graphic, or [rolling the cut](/editing/slip-and-roll/#roll-a-cut) before it, moves **In** in the same way. Trimming the end leaves a pinned **Length** alone. With **Follow Clip** on, the graphic's own timeline ends at the new end.
621	
622	## Good to know
623	
624	- The cut lands on the project's frame grid.
625	- A [transition](/motion/transitions/) into the clip stays on the first piece. The second piece starts with a hard cut.
626	- [Sound fades](/audio/fades/) are copied to both pieces. A clip with a fade-in fades in again at the cut, and one with a fade-out dips at the cut, so set them again on the side of the cut where you don't want them.
627	- A project holds up to 4,096 clips. A split that would pass that shows an error alert, and nothing changes.
628	
629	## With an agent
630	
631	`split` cuts at a time you give it, or at the playhead if you leave the time out. Give it a list of clips to cut those, or leave the list out to cut every clip on an unlocked track at that time, as the menu item does with nothing selected. See [Tools: cutting and deleting](/mcp/tools-cut-and-delete/#split).
632	
633	## Related
634	
635	- [Split at Shot Changes](/editing/split-at-shot-changes/)
636	- [Delete, Ripple Delete and Lift](/editing/delete-clips/)
637	- [Trim clips](/editing/trimming/)
638	- [How edits move actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/)
639	=== editing/timing-section
640	---
641	title: "Type a clip's timing"
642	description: "Trim a clip to an exact time by typing its In and Out, and read its length, in the Clip tab's Timing section."
643	---
644	
645	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
646	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
647	
648	The Timing section is for when you know the number. Type where a clip starts and ends on the timeline, and read how long it is, without dragging an edge.
649	
650	<AtAGlance
651	  where="Clip tab ▸ Clip ▸ Timing"
652	  tools={['trim_start', 'trim_end']}
653	/>
654	
655	## Type In and Out
656	
657	<Steps>
658	
659	1. Select one clip.
660	
661	2. In the [inspector's](/getting-started/inspector/) **Clip** tab, choose the **Clip** sub-tab, the last one. **Timing** is its first section, and it starts shut. Click its header to open it, and it stays open until you shut it. Shut, the header still shows the clip's length.
662	
663	3. Click **In** or **Out** and type a time. `1:23`, `83.5` and `1:23:04` all work, as they do in the toolbar's time field. See [Inspector fields](/getting-started/inspector-fields/).
664	
665	4. Press <kbd>Return</kbd> or <kbd>Tab</kbd>.
666	
667	</Steps>
668	
669	| Field | What it is | What typing does |
670	| --- | --- | --- |
671	| **In** | Where the clip starts on the timeline | Trims its front edge. The rest of the clip stays where it is. |
672	| **Out** | Where the clip ends on the timeline | Trims its back edge. |
673	
674	Both are positions on the timeline, not positions in the file. A later **In** hides the start of the footage, and an earlier one brings it back. To move the whole clip without trimming it, [drag it](/editing/move-clips/) instead.
675	
676	Each change is one undo step, named Trim Start or Trim End. The time lands on the project's frame grid.
677	
678	## How far an edge can go
679	
680	A number out of range doesn't beep. The edge goes as far as it can, and the field shows where it landed.
681	
682	| Field | Earliest | Latest |
683	| --- | --- | --- |
684	| **In** | The start of the timeline, or as far back as the file has footage | One frame before the clip's end |
685	| **Out** | One frame after the clip's start | As far as the file has footage |
686	
687	Only a clip that plays a video or audio file has a footage limit. Text, shapes, pictures and graphics have no file length to run out of.
688	
689	Three things leave the clip as it was:
690	
691	- If you type a new value but it puts the edge where it already is, Frame Job beeps.
692	- If the text can't be read as a time, Frame Job beeps and the field goes back to the old value.
693	- If the new edge would break the [overlap rule](/getting-started/refused-edits/), Frame Job beeps and gives the reason at the foot of the inspector.
694	
695	An overlap the rule allows goes through, and the clip that now overlaps the one before it gets a Cross Dissolve.
696	
697	## Read the duration
698	
699	**Duration** shows the clip's length, in the project's [timecode style](/projects/background-and-timecode/). You can't type in it: change the length through **In** and **Out**.
700	
701	## With several clips selected
702	
703	**In**, **Out** and **Duration** each describe one clip, so they go away when you select more than one.
704	
705	If every selected clip plays a video or audio file, Timing stays and holds only the [Reverse](/speed/reverse/) rows, which apply to all of them as one undo step. Its header shows the lengths of the selected clips added together, followed by "total".
706	
707	If the selection also holds anything else, such as text, a shape, a picture or a freeze frame, there's no Timing section.
708	
709	## Good to know
710	
711	- With one clip selected, the Reverse rows appear under **Duration** only for a clip that plays a video or audio file.
712	- Typing an edge also moves the same edge of a [linked clip](/audio/detach-and-attach/) when the two line up and its track isn't locked. That holds even when you type on the sound half. To move a sound's edge without its picture, [use a drag, <kbd>W</kbd> or <kbd>E</kbd>](/editing/slip-and-roll/#move-a-sound-clips-edge-alone).
713	- A locked track stops drags, not these fields. If a clip on a locked track is selected, typing still trims it.
714	- Inside a [nest](/editing/nests/), the times count from the nest's own start.
715	- [Actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/) keep their place measured from the clip's start, so trimming the front edge moves them along the timeline with it.
716	
717	## With an agent
718	
719	`trim_start` and `trim_end` move the same two edges to a time on the timeline, and stop at the same limits. With `alone`, the edge moves without its linked partner's. See [Tools: moving and trimming](/mcp/tools-move-and-trim/).
720	
721	## Related
722	
723	- [Trim clips](/editing/trimming/)
724	- [Slip and roll](/editing/slip-and-roll/)

727	=== editing/trimming
728	---
729	title: "Trim clips"
730	description: Shorten or lengthen a clip by dragging an edge, trimming to the playhead or typing a time.
731	---
732	
733	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
734	
735	Trimming changes where a clip starts or ends without moving the footage inside it. Use it to take the slack off a shot, or to pull back in what you cut too tightly.
736	
737	<AtAGlance
738	  menu={['Clip ▸ Trim Start to Playhead', 'Clip ▸ Trim End to Playhead']}
739	  keys={['W', 'E']}
740	  where={[
741	    'Timeline ▸ drag a clip edge',
742	    'The Trim Start to Playhead and Trim End to Playhead buttons in the timeline bar',
743	    'Clip tab ▸ Clip ▸ Timing ▸ In and Out',
744	  ]}
745	  tools={['trim_start', 'trim_end']}
746	/>
747	
748	## Drag an edge
749	
750	Drag either edge of a clip. The edge is the outer 7 points of the clip. The pointer becomes a left-right resize cursor there, and a selected clip shows trim grips.
751	
752	- **A clip 21 points wide or less** on screen is all body, so [zoom in](/timeline/zoom-and-scroll/) to trim it.
753	- **Clips on locked tracks** have no edges to grab and show no resize cursor. <kbd>W</kbd>, <kbd>E</kbd> and the **In** and **Out** fields still trim one, if you've selected it by clicking.
754	- **A fade handle or an action band** under the pointer takes the press before the edge does.
755	
756	The drag [snaps](/timeline/snapping/) when snapping is on, and holding <kbd>⌘</kbd> turns snapping off for that moment. The whole drag is one undo step, Trim Clip.
757	
758	Hold <kbd>⌥</kbd> as you press a media clip's end edge to [rate stretch](/speed/rate-stretch/) it instead, which changes its speed to fill the new length. <kbd>⌥</kbd> on the start edge is an ordinary trim. <kbd>⌥⇧</kbd> on either edge is a [roll](/editing/slip-and-roll/).
759	
760	## What each edge does
761	
762	**A start trim** moves the clip's start and its place in the footage together. The frame under the edge stays put, and the rest of the clip stays where it is on the timeline.
763	
764	**An end trim** moves the clip's end. Nothing else about the clip changes.
765	
766	Neither trim moves the clips around it, so a trim leaves a gap or fills one. If you pull a clip over its neighbour, the overlap has to keep to the [overlap rule](/editing/how-edits-work/#the-overlap-rule). Where it does, the later clip gets a Cross Dissolve over the overlap, unless it already has a transition. Where it doesn't, a dragged edge waits at the last position that was allowed, and <kbd>W</kbd>, <kbd>E</kbd> or a typed time beeps and changes nothing.
767	
768	## Trim to the playhead
769	
770	Select the clips, move the playhead inside them, then press <kbd>W</kbd> to trim their starts to the playhead or <kbd>E</kbd> to trim their ends. **Clip ▸ Trim Start to Playhead**, **Clip ▸ Trim End to Playhead** and the matching buttons in the timeline bar do the same.
771	
772	Each selected clip the playhead is inside is trimmed, as one undo step: Trim Start for <kbd>W</kbd> and Trim End for <kbd>E</kbd>.
773	
774	When no selected clip crosses the playhead, the menu items are greyed out and the keys beep. The menu doesn't show <kbd>W</kbd> and <kbd>E</kbd> beside its items, but the buttons' tooltips name them.
775	
776	## Type a time
777	
778	Select one clip and open the **Timing** section of the Clip tab's **Clip** sub-tab. **In** is where the clip starts on the timeline and **Out** is where it ends. Typing a new time is the same trim as dragging that edge.
779	
780	A time past what the clip can reach lands at the limit, and the field shows where it went. See [Type a clip's timing](/editing/timing-section/).
781	
782	## How far a trim goes
783	
784	A clip always keeps at least one frame.
785	
786	A media clip's trim stops at the start and end of its file. The end stops on the last whole frame the file still holds. A [slip or a roll](/editing/slip-and-roll/) can't pass either end of the file either.
787	
788	Pictures, freeze frames, text, shapes, graphics, adjustment clips and nests have no file length, so they trim to any length. A trimmed [nest](/editing/nests/) cuts nothing inside it. Trimming its end hides the tail. A nest always plays from its own first frame, so trimming its start moves what's inside along with the new start, rather than cutting into it.
789	
790	## What a trim keeps
791	
792	- **Linked sound.** Trim a picture and its [detached sound](/audio/detach-and-attach/) follows, if the two edges matched and the sound's track isn't locked. Trim the sound half and it goes alone, which is how you make a [J-cut or an L-cut](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/). <kbd>W</kbd> and <kbd>E</kbd> work the same way. The **In** and **Out** fields always take a matching partner along, whichever half you selected.
793	- **Actions.** They keep their time from the clip's start, so they stay put relative to the new start. An action past a new end is kept, and only the part inside the clip plays. See [How edits move actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/).
794	- **Caption words.** Timed words stay on their speech.
795	- **Speed ramps.** On a [ramped clip](/speed/edit-a-ramped-clip/), the ramp stays where it is in the clip, so what plays after a new start can change. The start stops where the clip still fits its media.
796	
797	## Trim a graphic
798	
799	Trimming the front of a graphic clip cuts into its animation. The **In** row of the **Timeline** section in the **Graphic** sub-tab moves forward, and the outro keeps its timing. That **In** counts the graphic's own frames, so it isn't the **In** field under **Timing**.
800	
801	A graphic has no file to run out of, so you can also drag its start back earlier. The graphic's **In** stops at 0, and the clip keeps growing.
802	
803	Trimming the end leaves a pinned **Length** alone. With **Follow Clip** on, the graphic's own timeline ends at the clip's new end. A clip longer than a pinned **Length** keeps drawing frames past it, with its progress held at the end. See [Graphic size and timing](/graphics/size-and-timing/).
804	
805	## With an agent
806	
807	`trim_start` and `trim_end` move an edge to a time you give them. With `alone`, they trim either half of a linked pair on its own. On the timeline, only the sound half trims alone. See [Tools: moving and trimming](/mcp/tools-move-and-trim/).
808	
809	## Related

812	- [Rate stretch](/speed/rate-stretch/)
813	- [Split clips](/editing/splitting/)
814	- [Type a clip's timing](/editing/timing-section/)
815	- [J-cuts and L-cuts](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/)
