354	=== editing/slip-and-roll
355	---
356	title: "Slip and roll"
357	description: "Change which footage a clip shows, or move the cut between two clips, without moving anything else on the timeline."
358	---
359	
360	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
361	
362	Slip and roll are for fine-tuning once your clips are where they belong. A slip changes which part of the file a clip shows. A roll moves the cut between two clips. Neither moves any other clip.
363	
364	<AtAGlance
365	  keys={['⌥⇧-drag body', '⌥⇧-drag edge']}
366	  where="The timeline"
367	  tools={['slip', 'roll', 'trim_start', 'trim_end']}
368	/>
369	
370	## Slip a clip
371	
372	Hold <kbd>⌥⇧</kbd> and drag the body of a clip. The clip stays where it is at the same length, and the footage slides underneath it. Drag right to show later footage and left to show earlier footage.
373	
374	The whole drag is one undo step, named Slip. It doesn't change the selection, so you can slip a clip without selecting it.
375	
376	- A slip stops when the clip reaches either end of its file, and keeps what it reached. It doesn't turn into a trim. If there's no footage to slide into, the drag changes nothing.
377	- It moves in whole frames and never snaps, because the timeline's snap points mean nothing inside the footage.
378	- The footage moves at the clip's speed. At ×2, dragging one frame slides the footage two frames.
379	- A [freeze frame](/speed/freeze-frame/) slips too, which changes the frame it holds. It stops one frame short of the end of its file.
380	- A linked sound clip on an unlocked track slips with its picture, so the two stay in sync. They move by the smaller of the two distances they each have room for.
381	
382	Only clips that play a file have footage to slide. The drag does nothing on text, a shape, a picture, a graphic or a nest.
383	
384	## Roll a cut
385	
386	Hold <kbd>⌥⇧</kbd> and drag a clip's edge, the outer 7 points of the clip. The cut moves: one clip gets longer and the other gets shorter by the same amount, and the outer edges of the pair stay where they are.
387	
388	| Edge you drag | Cut that moves |
389	| --- | --- |
390	| The clip's start | The cut with the clip before it |
391	| The clip's end | The cut with the clip after it |
392	
393	The whole drag is one undo step, named Roll.
394	
395	- A roll [snaps](/timeline/snapping/) like a trim. Hold <kbd>⌘</kbd> during the drag to stop snapping.
396	- Each clip keeps at least one frame.
397	- A clip that plays a file can't grow past what the file has. Text, shapes and pictures have no such limit.
398	- A roll needs two clips that touch exactly. With a gap at that edge there's no cut to move, and with an overlap there's a [transition](/motion/transition-settings/), whose length you set in its own section. Either way the drag does nothing.
399	- A clip under about 21 points wide on screen has no edges to grab, and the drag slips it instead. [Zoom in](/timeline/zoom-and-scroll/) first.
400	
401	When you roll a picture's cut, a linked sound clip rolls with it, as long as it starts at the same point, it touches a clip before it, and its track is unlocked.
402	
403	## Move a sound clip's edge alone
404	
405	A [detached sound clip](/audio/detach-and-attach/) that's still linked to its picture can move an edge on its own. This is how a [J-cut or L-cut](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/) is made. These move only the sound's edge and leave the picture where it is:
406	
407	- Drag the sound clip's edge.
408	- Select it and press <kbd>W</kbd> or <kbd>E</kbd> to [trim it to the playhead](/editing/trimming/).
409	- Hold <kbd>⌥⇧</kbd> and drag the sound clip's edge to roll its cut.
410	
411	It works in that direction only. Trimming or rolling the picture's edge also moves the sound's edge when the two line up, and a slip always takes both.
412	
413	## What happens to actions and timed words
414	
415	A slip leaves [actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/) where they are, because only the footage inside the clip moves.
416	
417	A roll leaves each clip's actions at the same distance from that clip's start. So on the clip after the cut, the actions move with the cut along the timeline. On the clip before it, they stay put, and if that clip gets shorter it can end before an action does.
418	
419	Timed caption words are the exception. They stay on the speech they time, so a roll doesn't shift them against the sound. A [graphic](/graphics/size-and-timing/) after the cut stays in step too: its **In** moves with the cut.
420	
421	## Good to know
422	
423	- Neither gesture works on a locked track. The drag does nothing. A linked clip on a locked track stays put while the clip you drag moves.
424	- On a clip with a [speed ramp](/speed/edit-a-ramped-clip/), the actions stay where they are and the limits come from the ramp, so a cut stops rolling where the clip would no longer fit its file.
425	
426	## With an agent
427	
428	`slip` takes a clip and how far to slide, and a positive distance shows later footage. Where the drag does nothing on text, a shape, a picture, a graphic or a nest, the tool gives an error.
429	
430	`roll` takes the clip to the right of the cut and the time the cut moves to. If no clip on the track ends where that clip begins, it gives an error saying so.
431	
432	With `alone`, `roll` moves a picture's cut and leaves a lined-up linked sound on an unlocked track where it is. No gesture can do that. `trim_start` and `trim_end` take `alone` too, to move one clip's edge without its partner's. See [Tools: moving and trimming](/mcp/tools-move-and-trim/).
433	
434	## Related
435	
436	- [Trim clips](/editing/trimming/)
437	- [J-cuts and L-cuts](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/)
438	- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
439	- [How edits move actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/)
440	=== editing/split-at-shot-changes
441	---
442	title: "Split at Shot Changes"
443	description: "Cut a finished edit, a download or a stream recording into one clip per shot, with the cuts found on your Mac."
444	---
445	
446	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
447	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
448	
449	Split at Shot Changes takes a clip that already has cuts in it, such as a finished edit, a downloaded clip or a stream recording, and cuts it at each one, giving you one clip per shot.
450	
451	<AtAGlance
452	  menu="Clip ▸ Split at Shot Changes"
453	  tools={['split_at_shots', 'get_media_analysis']}
454	  needs="Nothing. The cuts are found on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
455	/>
456	
457	## Split a clip at its shot changes
458	
459	<Steps>
460	
461	1. Select one or more clips that show a video file's picture.
462	
463	2. Choose **Clip ▸ Split at Shot Changes**. It has no shortcut.
464	
465	3. If Frame Job hasn't looked at this footage yet, wait for the [Analyzing sheet](#while-the-cuts-are-found) to finish.
466	
467	</Steps>
468	
469	Each selected clip is cut at every hard cut inside the part of the file it plays. All the cuts are one undo step, named Split at Shot Changes.
470	
471	The command is greyed out until a selected clip shows a video file's picture. Anything else in the selection is left alone: text, an image, a freeze frame, an audio file, a nest, or a clip with its [picture turned off](/editing/enable-picture-and-sound/).
472	
473	If the footage holds no shot change inside any selected clip, Frame Job beeps and nothing changes.
474	
475	## While the cuts are found
476	
477	When the footage has already been read, the split lands at once. Otherwise the **Analyzing** sheet appears, with one row per file:
478	
479	| A file's row reads | What it means |
480	| --- | --- |
481	| Waiting | Its first frame hasn't been read yet. |
482	| A percentage, with a bar | How much has been read. |
483	| Done | Its cuts have been found. |
484	
485	The split lands as soon as every file is done. Editing commands are off while the sheet is up.
486	
487	**Stop** closes the sheet and changes nothing. Frame Job saves what it has found every 30 seconds or so, and that stays in the cache, so a long file doesn't start from nothing next time.
488	
489	If the project changes anyway while the sheet is up, for example through an agent, nothing is split, and the inspector says to choose the command again.
490	
491	## What counts as a hard cut
492	
493	A hard cut is a change from one picture to another between two frames. Frame Job compares each frame's colours with those of the frames before it. It's a plain measurement of the picture, with no machine learning, so the same footage always gives the same cuts.
494	
495	- A gradual dissolve isn't a cut.
496	- A single flash frame isn't a cut, because the picture after it matches the one before.
497	- A dissolve between flat-coloured pictures, such as slides or title cards, can be found as one cut.
498	- Two shots with very similar colours can be missed, because the comparison looks at colour rather than at what's in the frame.
499	- Of two cuts within 12 frames of each other in the file, only the stronger is found.
500	
501	## Found on this Mac and cached
502	
503	Shot changes are found on your Mac. Nothing is sent anywhere and you don't need a key.
504	
505	The results are kept in the project's cache, so a second split of the same footage starts at once. See [On-device media analysis](/projects/media-analysis/).
506	
507	## Where the cuts land
508	
509	Each cut lands on the project's frame grid, worked out through the clip's speed, [speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/) and [reversal](/speed/reverse/). In a project whose frame rate differs from the file's, that's the nearest project frame.
510	
511	A cut within one frame of either end of a clip isn't made, so you won't get a piece one frame long at a clip's edge.
512	
513	Each cut is an ordinary [split](/editing/splitting/), so actions, word timings and graphics divide the same way.
514	
515	## Locked tracks and linked sound
516	
517	A selected clip on a locked track is still cut. Its linked sound is cut with it when the sound's track is unlocked, as with [Split](/editing/splitting/#linked-sound).
518	
519	## The clip ceiling
520	
521	A project holds up to 4,096 clips, counting the clips inside nests. If the splits would pass that, nothing is split at all, and the inspector says how many clips the command would add and how many more would fit. The count includes each linked clip the splits also cut.
522	
523	## When it can't run
524	
525	Frame Job beeps and gives the reason at the foot of the inspector:
526	
527	| What happened | What to do |
528	| --- | --- |
529	| A file is missing or can't be read | [Relink it](/projects/relink-media/), then choose the command again. |
530	| The analysis of a file failed | The message names the file and the reason. Nothing is split. |
531	| The analysis is no longer in the project's cache | Choose the command again, and Frame Job reads the file again. |
532	
533	## With an agent
534	
535	`split_at_shots` works on the clips it's given, and lists any it can't cut under `skipped`. Without a list, it takes every clip of a video file on an unlocked track, so a clip on a locked track is cut only when it's named. It shows no sheet. It waits up to 60 seconds for the cuts, and if they aren't ready it stops without splitting and keeps what it has saved so far, so calling it again carries on.
536	
537	With no cut inside any clip, it reports that no clips were added and leaves no undo step. See [Tools: cutting and deleting](/mcp/tools-cut-and-delete/#split_at_shots).
538	
539	`get_media_analysis`, with the kind `shots`, reads a file's cuts without splitting anything. See [Tools: reading analysis](/mcp/tools-analysis/).
540	
541	## Related
542	
543	- [Split clips](/editing/splitting/)
544	- [On-device media analysis](/projects/media-analysis/)
545	- [Select clips](/timeline/selecting-clips/)
546	- [Delete, Ripple Delete and Lift](/editing/delete-clips/)
547	=== editing/splitting
548	---
549	title: "Split clips"
550	description: "Cut clips in two at the playhead, and see what each piece keeps of the footage, actions, word timings and graphics."
551	---
552	
553	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
554	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
555	
556	Split cuts a clip in two at the playhead, so you can trim, move or remove one piece without touching the other.
557	
558	<AtAGlance
559	  menu="Clip ▸ Split"
560	  keys="⌘T"
561	  where="The scissors button in the timeline bar"
562	  tools="split"
563	/>
564	
565	## Split at the playhead
566	
567	<Steps>
568	
569	1. Move the playhead to the frame you want to cut on.
570	
571	2. Select the clips to cut, or select nothing to cut everything under the playhead.
572	
573	3. Press <kbd>⌘T</kbd>, choose **Clip ▸ Split**, or click the scissors button in the timeline bar.
574	
575	</Steps>
576	
577	| What's selected | What gets cut |
578	| --- | --- |
579	| One or more clips | Each selected clip the playhead is inside |
580	| Nothing | Every clip under the playhead on every unlocked track |
581	
582	It's one undo step, named Split, however many clips it cuts. The command is available whenever the timeline has clips.
583	
584	The playhead has to be strictly inside a clip. A playhead sitting exactly on a clip's edge is at a cut already, so that clip is left alone. If nothing can be cut, Frame Job beeps and nothing changes.
585	
586	A clip on a locked track is left alone when nothing is selected, but it's still cut if you selected it.
587	
588	## Footage stays continuous
589	
590	The second piece carries on playing the footage from where the first stopped, at the same speed, so the split doesn't show when you play it back. If an action is animating the clip, the second piece starts from where that animation had got to at the cut, such as its position or volume. It keeps the clip's name, label and settings.
591	
592	On a clip with a [speed ramp](/speed/edit-a-ramped-clip/), the two pieces meet at exactly the same point in the footage, and the second starts at the rate in force at the cut.
593	
594	## Linked sound
595	
596	A [linked clip](/audio/detach-and-attach/) on an unlocked track is cut too, when the playhead is inside it, and the two second halves are linked to each other.
597	
598	If the linked clip isn't cut, because its track is locked or the playhead isn't inside it, it stays linked to whichever piece shares more of its time. The other piece isn't linked to anything.
599	
600	## Actions and word timings
601	
602	[Actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/) stay with the piece they fall in:
603	
604	- An action that ends at or before the cut stays on the first piece.
605	- An action that starts at or after the cut moves to the second piece.
606	- An action that spans the cut becomes two. The first half ends at the value it had reached at the cut, and the second carries on to the original target, so the join doesn't show. Both keep the action's curve.
607	
608	An [entrance and exit preset](/motion/entrances-and-exits/) is tied to the clip's ends, so the first piece keeps the entrance and the second keeps the exit. A [text reveal](/text-and-shapes/text-reveal/) divides the same way. Otherwise the clip would leave at the cut and arrive again on the far side of it.
609	
610	Caption word timings stay on their words. Both pieces keep the full text, the first with its timings as they were and the second with its timings moved to match its new start.
611	
612	The one exception is a text clip whose wording an action changes. If the second piece's text at the cut no longer has the same number of words as its timings, the second piece loses its word timings and shows its text all at once.
613	
614	## Split a graphic
615	
616	A [graphic](/graphics/size-and-timing/) carries on across the cut rather than starting again, and plays its outro once, at the true end.
617	
618	The graphic's **In** on the second piece starts at the cut, so it picks up where the first piece left off. Both pieces keep the original's **Length**, so an outro still plays at the same moment. That pins the length, so **Follow Clip** is off on both pieces afterwards.
619	
620	Trimming the start of a graphic, or [rolling the cut](/editing/slip-and-roll/#roll-a-cut) before it, moves **In** in the same way. Trimming the end leaves a pinned **Length** alone. With **Follow Clip** on, the graphic's own timeline ends at the new end.
621	
622	## Good to know
623	
624	- The cut lands on the project's frame grid.
625	- A [transition](/motion/transitions/) into the clip stays on the first piece. The second piece starts with a hard cut.
626	- [Sound fades](/audio/fades/) are copied to both pieces. A clip with a fade-in fades in again at the cut, and one with a fade-out dips at the cut, so set them again on the side of the cut where you don't want them.
627	- A project holds up to 4,096 clips. A split that would pass that shows an error alert, and nothing changes.
628	
629	## With an agent
630	
631	`split` cuts at a time you give it, or at the playhead if you leave the time out. Give it a list of clips to cut those, or leave the list out to cut every clip on an unlocked track at that time, as the menu item does with nothing selected. See [Tools: cutting and deleting](/mcp/tools-cut-and-delete/#split).
632	
633	## Related
634	
635	- [Split at Shot Changes](/editing/split-at-shot-changes/)
636	- [Delete, Ripple Delete and Lift](/editing/delete-clips/)
637	- [Trim clips](/editing/trimming/)
638	- [How edits move actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/)
639	=== editing/timing-section
640	---
641	title: "Type a clip's timing"
642	description: "Trim a clip to an exact time by typing its In and Out, and read its length, in the Clip tab's Timing section."
643	---
644	
645	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
646	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
647	
648	The Timing section is for when you know the number. Type where a clip starts and ends on the timeline, and read how long it is, without dragging an edge.
649	
650	<AtAGlance
651	  where="Clip tab ▸ Clip ▸ Timing"
652	  tools={['trim_start', 'trim_end']}
653	/>
654	
655	## Type In and Out
656	
657	<Steps>
658	
659	1. Select one clip.
660	
661	2. In the [inspector's](/getting-started/inspector/) **Clip** tab, choose the **Clip** sub-tab, the last one. **Timing** is its first section, and it starts shut. Click its header to open it, and it stays open until you shut it. Shut, the header still shows the clip's length.
662	
663	3. Click **In** or **Out** and type a time. `1:23`, `83.5` and `1:23:04` all work, as they do in the toolbar's time field. See [Inspector fields](/getting-started/inspector-fields/).
664	
665	4. Press <kbd>Return</kbd> or <kbd>Tab</kbd>.
666	
667	</Steps>
668	
669	| Field | What it is | What typing does |
670	| --- | --- | --- |
671	| **In** | Where the clip starts on the timeline | Trims its front edge. The rest of the clip stays where it is. |
672	| **Out** | Where the clip ends on the timeline | Trims its back edge. |
673	
674	Both are positions on the timeline, not positions in the file. A later **In** hides the start of the footage, and an earlier one brings it back. To move the whole clip without trimming it, [drag it](/editing/move-clips/) instead.
675	
676	Each change is one undo step, named Trim Start or Trim End. The time lands on the project's frame grid.
677	
678	## How far an edge can go
679	
680	A number out of range doesn't beep. The edge goes as far as it can, and the field shows where it landed.
681	
682	| Field | Earliest | Latest |
683	| --- | --- | --- |
684	| **In** | The start of the timeline, or as far back as the file has footage | One frame before the clip's end |
685	| **Out** | One frame after the clip's start | As far as the file has footage |
686	
687	Only a clip that plays a video or audio file has a footage limit. Text, shapes, pictures and graphics have no file length to run out of.
688	
689	Three things leave the clip as it was:
690	
691	- If you type a new value but it puts the edge where it already is, Frame Job beeps.
692	- If the text can't be read as a time, Frame Job beeps and the field goes back to the old value.
693	- If the new edge would break the [overlap rule](/getting-started/refused-edits/), Frame Job beeps and gives the reason at the foot of the inspector.
694	
695	An overlap the rule allows goes through, and the clip that now overlaps the one before it gets a Cross Dissolve.
696	
697	## Read the duration
698	
699	**Duration** shows the clip's length, in the project's [timecode style](/projects/background-and-timecode/). You can't type in it: change the length through **In** and **Out**.
700	
701	## With several clips selected
702	
703	**In**, **Out** and **Duration** each describe one clip, so they go away when you select more than one.
704	
705	If every selected clip plays a video or audio file, Timing stays and holds only the [Reverse](/speed/reverse/) rows, which apply to all of them as one undo step. Its header shows the lengths of the selected clips added together, followed by "total".
706	
707	If the selection also holds anything else, such as text, a shape, a picture or a freeze frame, there's no Timing section.
708	
709	## Good to know
710	
711	- With one clip selected, the Reverse rows appear under **Duration** only for a clip that plays a video or audio file.
712	- Typing an edge also moves the same edge of a [linked clip](/audio/detach-and-attach/) when the two line up and its track isn't locked. That holds even when you type on the sound half. To move a sound's edge without its picture, [use a drag, <kbd>W</kbd> or <kbd>E</kbd>](/editing/slip-and-roll/#move-a-sound-clips-edge-alone).
713	- A locked track stops drags, not these fields. If a clip on a locked track is selected, typing still trims it.
714	- Inside a [nest](/editing/nests/), the times count from the nest's own start.
715	- [Actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/) keep their place measured from the clip's start, so trimming the front edge moves them along the timeline with it.
716	
717	## With an agent
718	
719	`trim_start` and `trim_end` move the same two edges to a time on the timeline, and stop at the same limits. With `alone`, the edge moves without its linked partner's. See [Tools: moving and trimming](/mcp/tools-move-and-trim/).
720	
721	## Related
722	
723	- [Trim clips](/editing/trimming/)
724	- [Slip and roll](/editing/slip-and-roll/)
725	- [Reverse a clip](/speed/reverse/)
726	- [Fit a clip to a length](/speed/fit-to-duration/)
727	=== editing/trimming
728	---
729	title: "Trim clips"
730	description: Shorten or lengthen a clip by dragging an edge, trimming to the playhead or typing a time.
731	---
732	
733	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
734	
735	Trimming changes where a clip starts or ends without moving the footage inside it. Use it to take the slack off a shot, or to pull back in what you cut too tightly.
736	
737	<AtAGlance
738	  menu={['Clip ▸ Trim Start to Playhead', 'Clip ▸ Trim End to Playhead']}
739	  keys={['W', 'E']}
740	  where={[
741	    'Timeline ▸ drag a clip edge',
742	    'The Trim Start to Playhead and Trim End to Playhead buttons in the timeline bar',
743	    'Clip tab ▸ Clip ▸ Timing ▸ In and Out',
744	  ]}
745	  tools={['trim_start', 'trim_end']}
746	/>
747	
748	## Drag an edge
749	
750	Drag either edge of a clip. The edge is the outer 7 points of the clip. The pointer becomes a left-right resize cursor there, and a selected clip shows trim grips.
751	
752	- **A clip 21 points wide or less** on screen is all body, so [zoom in](/timeline/zoom-and-scroll/) to trim it.
753	- **Clips on locked tracks** have no edges to grab and show no resize cursor. <kbd>W</kbd>, <kbd>E</kbd> and the **In** and **Out** fields still trim one, if you've selected it by clicking.
754	- **A fade handle or an action band** under the pointer takes the press before the edge does.
755	
756	The drag [snaps](/timeline/snapping/) when snapping is on, and holding <kbd>⌘</kbd> turns snapping off for that moment. The whole drag is one undo step, Trim Clip.
757	
758	Hold <kbd>⌥</kbd> as you press a media clip's end edge to [rate stretch](/speed/rate-stretch/) it instead, which changes its speed to fill the new length. <kbd>⌥</kbd> on the start edge is an ordinary trim. <kbd>⌥⇧</kbd> on either edge is a [roll](/editing/slip-and-roll/).
759	
760	## What each edge does
761	
762	**A start trim** moves the clip's start and its place in the footage together. The frame under the edge stays put, and the rest of the clip stays where it is on the timeline.
763	
764	**An end trim** moves the clip's end. Nothing else about the clip changes.
765	
766	Neither trim moves the clips around it, so a trim leaves a gap or fills one. If you pull a clip over its neighbour, the overlap has to keep to the [overlap rule](/editing/how-edits-work/#the-overlap-rule). Where it does, the later clip gets a Cross Dissolve over the overlap, unless it already has a transition. Where it doesn't, a dragged edge waits at the last position that was allowed, and <kbd>W</kbd>, <kbd>E</kbd> or a typed time beeps and changes nothing.
767	
768	## Trim to the playhead
769	
770	Select the clips, move the playhead inside them, then press <kbd>W</kbd> to trim their starts to the playhead or <kbd>E</kbd> to trim their ends. **Clip ▸ Trim Start to Playhead**, **Clip ▸ Trim End to Playhead** and the matching buttons in the timeline bar do the same.
771	
772	Each selected clip the playhead is inside is trimmed, as one undo step: Trim Start for <kbd>W</kbd> and Trim End for <kbd>E</kbd>.
773	
774	When no selected clip crosses the playhead, the menu items are greyed out and the keys beep. The menu doesn't show <kbd>W</kbd> and <kbd>E</kbd> beside its items, but the buttons' tooltips name them.
775	
776	## Type a time
777	
778	Select one clip and open the **Timing** section of the Clip tab's **Clip** sub-tab. **In** is where the clip starts on the timeline and **Out** is where it ends. Typing a new time is the same trim as dragging that edge.
779	
780	A time past what the clip can reach lands at the limit, and the field shows where it went. See [Type a clip's timing](/editing/timing-section/).
781	
782	## How far a trim goes
783	
784	A clip always keeps at least one frame.
785	
786	A media clip's trim stops at the start and end of its file. The end stops on the last whole frame the file still holds. A [slip or a roll](/editing/slip-and-roll/) can't pass either end of the file either.
787	
788	Pictures, freeze frames, text, shapes, graphics, adjustment clips and nests have no file length, so they trim to any length. A trimmed [nest](/editing/nests/) cuts nothing inside it. Trimming its end hides the tail. A nest always plays from its own first frame, so trimming its start moves what's inside along with the new start, rather than cutting into it.
789	
790	## What a trim keeps
791	
792	- **Linked sound.** Trim a picture and its [detached sound](/audio/detach-and-attach/) follows, if the two edges matched and the sound's track isn't locked. Trim the sound half and it goes alone, which is how you make a [J-cut or an L-cut](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/). <kbd>W</kbd> and <kbd>E</kbd> work the same way. The **In** and **Out** fields always take a matching partner along, whichever half you selected.
793	- **Actions.** They keep their time from the clip's start, so they stay put relative to the new start. An action past a new end is kept, and only the part inside the clip plays. See [How edits move actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/).
794	- **Caption words.** Timed words stay on their speech.
795	- **Speed ramps.** On a [ramped clip](/speed/edit-a-ramped-clip/), the ramp stays where it is in the clip, so what plays after a new start can change. The start stops where the clip still fits its media.
796	
797	## Trim a graphic
798	
799	Trimming the front of a graphic clip cuts into its animation. The **In** row of the **Timeline** section in the **Graphic** sub-tab moves forward, and the outro keeps its timing. That **In** counts the graphic's own frames, so it isn't the **In** field under **Timing**.
800	
801	A graphic has no file to run out of, so you can also drag its start back earlier. The graphic's **In** stops at 0, and the clip keeps growing.
802	
803	Trimming the end leaves a pinned **Length** alone. With **Follow Clip** on, the graphic's own timeline ends at the clip's new end. A clip longer than a pinned **Length** keeps drawing frames past it, with its progress held at the end. See [Graphic size and timing](/graphics/size-and-timing/).
804	
805	## With an agent
806	
807	`trim_start` and `trim_end` move an edge to a time you give them. With `alone`, they trim either half of a linked pair on its own. On the timeline, only the sound half trims alone. See [Tools: moving and trimming](/mcp/tools-move-and-trim/).
808	
809	## Related
810	
811	- [Slip and roll](/editing/slip-and-roll/)
812	- [Rate stretch](/speed/rate-stretch/)
813	- [Split clips](/editing/splitting/)
814	- [Type a clip's timing](/editing/timing-section/)
815	- [J-cuts and L-cuts](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/)

1	=== timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks.mdx
2	---
3	title: Hide and lock tracks
4	description: Take a track's picture out of your video without touching its clips, and protect a track from being moved or cut by accident.
5	---
6	
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	**Hide Video** takes a track's picture out of your video and leaves its clips where they are. **Lock Track** protects a track's clips while you edit everything around them.
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  menu={['Track ▸ Hide Video', 'Track ▸ Lock Track']}
13	  where={['The eye and padlock switches in a track header', 'Right-click a track header or an empty stretch of its lane']}
14	  tools={['set_track']}
15	/>
16	
17	## Hide Video
18	
19	Click the eye in the track's header. It becomes a struck-through eye and the track's clips draw dimmed on the timeline. Click it again to bring the picture back.
20	
21	**Hide Video** in the [track context menu](/timeline/manage-tracks/#the-track-context-menu) does the same for the track you clicked, and **Track ▸ Hide Video** for the [current track](/timeline/tracks/#the-current-track).
22	
23	While a track is hidden:
24	
25	- Its picture is gone from the preview and from every export.
26	- Its clips aren't drawn on the canvas, so you can't click them there. You can still select and edit them on the timeline.
27	- Its sound keeps playing. To silence it as well, use [Mute Audio](/audio/mute-and-solo/).
28	- A hidden [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/) cuts nothing, so the track behind it shows whole.
29	- If it holds a [nest](/editing/nests/), everything inside the nest is hidden too.
30	
31	## Lock Track
32	
33	Click the open padlock in the track's header. It closes and the lane is hatched. Click it again to unlock.
34	
35	**Lock Track** in the [track context menu](/timeline/manage-tracks/#the-track-context-menu) does the same for the track you clicked, and **Track ▸ Lock Track** for the [current track](/timeline/tracks/#the-current-track).
36	
37	### What a lock stops
38	
39	On the timeline, you can't drag, trim, slip or roll a locked track's clips with the mouse. Their trim edges are gone, and their fade handles, volume lines and action bands don't respond. A marquee skips them.
40	
41	On the preview, you can't select, drag or nudge them. A click passes through to the unlocked clip behind.
42	
43	Edits that reach across the timeline leave a locked track alone:
44	
45	- [**Split**](/editing/splitting/) with nothing selected doesn't cut its clips.
46	- [**Lift** and the range form of **Ripple Delete**](/editing/delete-clips/) leave them uncut.
47	- Ripples, [closed gaps](/editing/close-gaps/) and inserted time don't shift them. That includes the cuts from [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/).
48	- A clip on a locked track isn't moved, cut or deleted along with a linked partner on an unlocked track.
49	
50	### What Frame Job won't do
51	
52	A few edits need to shift or cut a locked track to work, so Frame Job stops them.
53	
54	| Edit | What happens |
55	| --- | --- |
56	| [Insert](/editing/insert-and-overwrite/) onto a locked track | Beeps and says why at the foot of the inspector. |
57	| [Close Gap](/editing/close-gaps/) on a locked track | Beeps and says why at the foot of the inspector. |
58	| [Retime Range](/speed/retime-range/) | Won't run while a locked track has a clip that ends after the range's start, because that clip would fall out of step. |
59	
60	### What a lock doesn't stop
61	
62	A lock protects where a clip sits, not what it looks like. You can still rename a clip on a locked track and change it in the inspector.
63	
64	You can also still select one by clicking it on the timeline, with <kbd>⌥</kbd>-click on the header, or with **Edit ▸ Select All on Track**. Once a locked clip is selected, the edits you aim at it still work:
65	
66	- **Delete** and **Ripple Delete** remove it.
67	- **Split** cuts it.
68	- **Clip ▸ Trim Start to Playhead** (<kbd>W</kbd>) and **Clip ▸ Trim End to Playhead** (<kbd>E</kbd>) trim it.
69	- <kbd>,</kbd> and <kbd>.</kbd> nudge it along the timeline.
70	- If you drag an unlocked clip in the same selection, the locked clip moves with it.
71	
72	A few other things get past a lock too:
73	
74	- [**Overwrite**](/editing/insert-and-overwrite/) still clears the span it needs on a locked track.
75	- You can drop a clip or a file onto a locked track.
76	- You can [reorder](/timeline/manage-tracks/#reorder-tracks) or [remove](/timeline/manage-tracks/#remove-track) a locked track.
77	- [New Project from Range](/projects/new-project-from-range/) cuts locked tracks like any other, and the new project keeps their locks.
78	
79	## Good to know
80	
81	- Each flip is one undo step, named Hide Track or Lock Track.
82	- **Track ▸ Hide Video** and **Track ▸ Lock Track** show no checkmark, so read the state from the track's header. The context menu does show one.
83	
84	## With an agent
85	
86	`set_track` sets both switches, as `hidden` and `locked`. See [Tools: tracks, markers and canvas](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/#set_track).
87	
88	A lock holds back gestures in the window and edits that reach across the timeline. As with a clip you've selected, an agent that names a clip on a locked track can still move, trim, cut or delete it. See [Tools: moving and trimming](/mcp/tools-move-and-trim/).
89	
90	## Related
91	
92	- [Tracks](/timeline/tracks/)
93	- [How edits work](/editing/how-edits-work/)
94	- [Mute and solo tracks](/audio/mute-and-solo/)
95	- [Matte tracks](/canvas/matte-tracks/)
96	=== timeline/in-out-range.mdx
97	---
98	title: "The in/out range"
99	description: Mark a span of the timeline with I and O, so Loop, deletes, exports and other commands work on that passage alone.
100	---
101	
102	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
103	
104	The in/out range marks one passage of the timeline. Set it when you want to loop a section, cut it out, export it on its own, or point another command at it.
105	
106	<AtAGlance
107	  menu={['Mark ▸ Set In', 'Mark ▸ Set Out', 'Mark ▸ Clear Range']}
108	  keys={['I', 'O', '⌥X']}
109	  where="Shaded across the timeline's ruler and lanes"
110	  tools="set_range"
111	/>
112	
113	## Set In
114	
115	Move the playhead to where the passage starts and press <kbd>I</kbd>, or choose **Mark ▸ Set In**. With no range yet, the out point goes to the end of the timeline, so the range runs from the playhead to the end.
116	
117	## Set Out
118	
119	Move the playhead to where the passage ends and press <kbd>O</kbd>, or choose **Mark ▸ Set Out**. With no range yet, the in point goes to the start of the timeline.
120	
121	<kbd>I</kbd> and <kbd>O</kbd> are single-letter keys, so the menu shows no shortcut beside them, and they don't fire while you're typing in a field. See [Keys and typing](/getting-started/keys-and-typing/).
122	
123	## Clear Range
124	
125	Press <kbd>⌥X</kbd> or choose **Mark ▸ Clear Range**. The item is available only while a range is set.
126	
127	## What the range is
128	
129	The range is a span shaded across the ruler and the lanes. It changes nothing by itself. These commands read it:
130	
131	| Command | What it does with the range |
132	| --- | --- |
133	| [Loop](/timeline/loop/) | Plays the range over and over, instead of the whole timeline. |
134	| <kbd>⌫</kbd> and <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> | With no clip selected, [Lift or Ripple Delete](/editing/delete-clips/) the range. With nothing selected and no range, they beep. |
135	| [Speed ramp presets](/speed/make-a-ramp/) | Cover the range when it lies entirely inside the clip. |
136	| [**Insert ▸ Adjustment Clip**](/color/adjustment-clips/) | Covers the range. With no range it covers the selected clips, or the whole timeline. |
137	| [Export](/export/range/) | Writes only the range when you set **Range:** to **In/out range**. |
138	| [Retime Range](/speed/retime-range/) | Changes the speed of everything in the range. |
139	| [New Project from Range](/projects/new-project-from-range/) | Opens a new project made of the range. |
140	| [Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/) | Offers **In/out range** under **From**, which takes every clip that overlaps the range, whole. |
141	| [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) | Works over the range. With no range it works over the selected angle clips. |
142	
143	Two other things set the range for you. Selecting words in the [Transcript tab](/captions/delete-words/) makes them the range, and clearing that selection clears it. **Preview** for a [motion preset](/motion/motion-presets/) sets the range to the clip and turns Loop on, and both stay until you clear them.
144	
145	## Crossing points
146	
147	Setting an in point after the out point moves the out point to match, and setting an out point before the in point moves the in point. Both points then sit on the playhead, which is a range of no length, until you set the other end.
148	
149	A range of no length isn't shaded, and Loop plays the whole timeline. <kbd>⌫</kbd> and <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> treat it as no range at all, and the export sheet doesn't offer it. **Mark ▸ Clear Range** still clears it.
150	
151	## The range isn't saved
152	
153	The range belongs to the window you're working in, not to the project:
154	
155	- Setting or clearing it isn't an undo step, and it doesn't mark the project as edited.
156	- It isn't saved, so a project always opens with no range.
157	- It clears when you enter or leave a [nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/), because a nest's time counts from its own start.
158	
159	## Good to know
160	
161	- Edits don't move the range. It stays at the same times while the clips under it change. After <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> on a range, the range is still there and now covers what moved up into it, so a second <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> cuts again. Cutting words in the Transcript tab is the exception, and clears the range.
162	- Inside a nest you can set a range for Loop, deleting and **Retime Range**, but not for an export. The export sheet's **Range:** stays on **Whole project**, and its tooltip explains that the range belongs to the nest. **New Project from Range** is off while a nest is open.
163	
164	## With an agent
165	
166	`set_range` sets either end or both, and clears the range when called with neither. Given one end, the other keeps its value, or falls back to the start or the end of the project when there's no range yet. Unlike Set In and Set Out, it won't move the other point for you, so an end at or before the start is an error.
167	
168	`get_project` reports the range as `in_out_range`, and `export` with `range` set to `in_out` writes only that span. See [Tools: playhead, range and selection](/mcp/tools-view-state/).
169	
170	## Related
171	
172	- [Loop playback](/timeline/loop/)
173	- [Delete, Ripple Delete and Lift](/editing/delete-clips/)
174	- [Export a range](/export/range/)
175	- [Markers](/timeline/markers/)
176	=== timeline/loop.mdx
177	---
178	title: "Loop playback"
179	description: "Repeat a passage of the timeline while you watch and adjust."
180	---
181	
182	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
183	
184	Loop keeps playback going round, so you can watch a passage over and over while you adjust it.
185	
186	<AtAGlance where="The Loop button in the toolbar" />
187	
188	## Turn Loop on
189	
190	Click **Loop**, the repeat button at the end of the transport in the toolbar. The button is dimmed while Loop is off and at full strength while it's on. Click it again to turn Loop off.
191	
192	Loop has no menu item and no key. It's off when a window opens, each window has its own setting, and it isn't saved with the project.
193	
194	## What it repeats
195	
196	| What's set | What Loop repeats |
197	| --- | --- |
198	| An [in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/) | The range |
199	| No range, or a range of no length | The whole timeline, going back to its start and stopping there |
200	
201	With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, the whole timeline means the whole nest. Entering or leaving a nest clears the range.
202	
203	The loop follows as things change. Set a new in or out point, clear the range or change the timeline's length while Loop is on, and the next pass uses the new span.
204	
205	## How playback goes round
206	
207	When playback reaches the end of the loop, it jumps back to the loop's start and carries on, at [×2 and ×4](/timeline/playback/#j-k-and-l) as well.
208	
209	A loop that ends at the very end of the timeline is different, and that includes the whole timeline. Playback jumps back to the loop's start and stops there, so press play to go round again. To keep going round, set the out point before the end of the timeline.
210	
211	- Press play at or past the end of the loop and it starts again from the loop's start.
212	- Press play before the start of the loop and it plays from where the playhead is. It only jumps back once it reaches the loop's end.
213	- Loop only works forwards. Playing backwards with <kbd>J</kbd> doesn't go round, and carries on past the start of the loop.
214	
215	## Good to know
216	
217	- The **Preview** button in the [**Motion presets**](/motion/motion-presets/) section, and **Clip ▸ Motion ▸ Preview**, set the in/out range to the clip and turn Loop on. Both stay that way until you clear the range and turn Loop off.
218	- Selecting words in the Transcript tab sets the range, so Loop plays those words. See [Follow along and jump](/captions/follow-the-transcript/).

225	=== timeline/manage-tracks.mdx
226	---
227	title: Add, rename and reorder tracks
228	description: Add a track, name it, change its place in the stack, remove it, and use the Track menu and a track's right-click menu.
229	---
230	
231	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
232	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
233	
234	Add a track when you need another layer, name it so the stack stays readable, and clear out the tracks you've stopped using.
235	
236	<AtAGlance
237	  menu={['Track ▸ New Track', 'Track ▸ Remove Track', 'Track ▸ Remove Empty Tracks']}
238	  keys="⇧⌘N"
239	  where={['Double-click or drag a track header', 'Right-click a track header or an empty stretch of its lane']}
240	  tools={['add_track', 'remove_track', 'move_track', 'set_track', 'remove_empty_tracks']}
241	/>
242	
243	## New Track
244	
245	Choose **Track ▸ New Track** or press <kbd>⇧⌘N</kbd>. An empty track appears at the front, as the top lane. It's named from the track count, such as `Track 4` when there are three tracks.
246	
247	A project holds at most 64 tracks, and the tracks inside nests count towards that. Past the limit, Frame Job shows an error and adds nothing.
248	
249	## Drop past the stack
250	
251	You can make a track and fill it in one move:
252	
253	- Drag clips above the top lane to make a new front track for them.
254	- Drag clips below the bottom lane to make a new back track for them.
255	
256	The new track and the move are one undo step, and this works for a <kbd>⌥</kbd>-drag duplicate too. See [Move clips](/editing/move-clips/).
257	
258	Dropping a file from the Media tab on the preview also adds a new front track for it.
259	
260	## Rename a track
261	
262	<Steps>
263	
264	1. Double-click the track's header, away from its switches. A name field opens in place.
265	
266	2. Type the new name.
267	
268	3. Press <kbd>Return</kbd> or <kbd>Tab</kbd>, or click somewhere else.
269	
270	</Steps>
271	
272	<kbd>Esc</kbd> closes the field and keeps the old name. So does clearing the field, because this field can't leave a track with no name. Spaces at either end of the name are dropped. [Clips](/timeline/names-and-labels/#rename-a-clip) and [markers](/timeline/markers/#move-rename-and-remove-a-marker) rename in the same kind of field.
273	
274	## Reorder tracks
275	
276	Drag a track's header up or down. A coral line shows where it will land, and the track moves there when you let go.
277	
278	Dragging a header changes what draws in front of what. It also changes what a [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/) cuts, because a matte cuts the track directly behind it. A locked track can be moved like any other.
279	
280	## Remove Track
281	
282	**Track ▸ Remove Track** removes the [current track](/timeline/tracks/#the-current-track). **Remove Track** in the [track context menu](#the-track-context-menu) removes the track you clicked, which is how you remove an empty track that isn't the front-most, since an empty track has no clip to select.
283	
284	An empty track goes at once. A track that still holds clips asks first, in an alert titled with the track's name: "The track still holds 3 clips, which will be removed with it." Choose **Remove** or **Cancel**. One undo brings back the track and its clips.
285	
286	A project always keeps one track, so the last one can't be removed. **Remove Track** is greyed out on it in the context menu. **Track ▸ Remove Track** stays available, but Frame Job beeps and says why at the foot of the inspector. If that last track holds clips, the alert comes first.
287	
288	## Remove Empty Tracks
289	
290	**Track ▸ Remove Empty Tracks** drops every track that holds no clips, as one undo step. Hidden, locked and named tracks go too if they're empty. If every track is empty, the back-most one stays. If no track is empty, Frame Job beeps.
291	
292	## The Track menu
293	
294	The **Track** menu's commands work on the [current track](/timeline/tracks/#the-current-track), apart from **New Track** and **Remove Empty Tracks**.
295	
296	| Item | Key | What it does |
297	| --- | --- | --- |
298	| **New Track** | <kbd>⇧⌘N</kbd> | Adds an empty track at the front. |
299	| **Remove Track** | | Removes the current track. |
300	| **Remove Empty Tracks** | | Drops every track with no clips. |
301	| **Hide Video** | | Flips the current track's [Hide Video](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/#hide-video) switch. |
302	| **Mute Audio** | | Flips its [Mute Audio](/audio/mute-and-solo/) switch. |
303	| **Lock Track** | | Flips its [Lock Track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/#lock-track) switch. |
304	| **Solo** | | Flips its [Solo](/audio/mute-and-solo/) switch. |
305	| **Mix…** | | Opens its [mix panel](/audio/track-volume-and-pan/). |
306	| **Matte** | | Makes it a [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/): **Off**, **Alpha**, **Inverted Alpha**, **Luma** or **Inverted Luma**. |
307	
308	Of the four switches, only **Solo** shows a checkmark in this menu, because a soloed track with nothing on it still silences the rest and you can't always hear that. For the other three, read the track's header.
309	
310	## The track context menu
311	
312	Right-click or <kbd>⌃</kbd>-click a track's header, or the empty part of its lane, to get a menu for that track:
313	
314	- **Hide Video**, **Mute Audio**, **Lock Track** and **Solo**, each checked when it's on
315	- **Mix…**
316	- **Matte**, with the track's mode checked
317	- **Remove Track**, greyed out on the last track
318	
319	Every item acts on the track you clicked, not the current track, and shows that track's own state. A right-click on a clip, the ruler or the corner above the headers opens no menu.
320	
321	## Undo names
322	
323	Every switch flip, rename and reorder is one undo step, and **Edit ▸ Undo** (<kbd>⌘Z</kbd>) names the edit it will reverse. The names for edits to tracks, markers and clip labels are:
324	
325	| Edit | Undo name |
326	| --- | --- |
327	| Track switches | Hide Track, Mute Track, Lock Track, Solo Track |
328	| A track's matte | Track Matte |
329	| A track's mix | Track Volume, Track Pan, Track Compressor, Track Limiter, Reset Track Mix |
330	| Track names and order | Rename Track, Reorder Track |
331	| Adding and removing tracks | New Track, Remove Track, Remove Empty Tracks |
332	| Markers | Add Marker, Move Marker, Rename Marker, Chapter Marker, Remove Marker |
333	| Clip names and labels | Rename Clip, Label Clip |
334	
335	## Good to know
336	
337	- With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, everything on this page works on the nest's own tracks, except that the mix panel's compressor and limiter are turned off there.
338	- **Remove Track** takes only the clips on that track. A linked picture or sound on another track stays, and is no longer linked.
339	
340	## With an agent
341	
342	`add_track` can put a new track anywhere in the stack and name it as it's made, where you'd add it at the front and then drag it. `move_track` moves a track to a numbered place in the stack, 0 being the back. To do what a drop past the stack does, an agent adds the track and then moves the clips onto it with `move_clip`.
343	
344	`remove_track` never asks: it leaves a track that holds clips alone unless it's told to take them too, and it won't remove the last track.
345	
346	These tools also work on the tracks inside a nest. See [Tools: tracks, markers and canvas](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/) and [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/).
347	
348	## Related
349	
350	- [Tracks](/timeline/tracks/)
351	- [Hide and lock tracks](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/)
352	- [Move clips](/editing/move-clips/)
353	- [Undo and saving](/getting-started/undo-and-saving/)
354	=== timeline/markers.mdx
355	---
356	title: Markers
357	description: Flag moments on the timeline, name them, jump between them, and turn them into chapters in an exported movie.
358	---
359	
360	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
361	
362	A marker is a flag on the ruler that remembers a moment in the project: a beat to cut on, a line to come back to, the start of a chapter.
363	
364	<AtAGlance
365	  menu={['Mark ▸ Add Marker', 'Mark ▸ Next Marker', 'Mark ▸ Previous Marker']}
366	  keys="M"
367	  where={['The bookmark button in the timeline bar', 'Document tab ▸ Markers']}
368	  tools={['add_marker', 'set_marker', 'remove_marker']}
369	/>
370	
371	## Add a marker
372	
373	Move the playhead to the moment and press <kbd>M</kbd>. The bookmark button in the timeline bar and **Mark ▸ Add Marker** do the same. <kbd>M</kbd> is a [single-letter key](/getting-started/keys-and-typing/), so the menu shows no shortcut beside the item, and it doesn't fire while you're typing in a field.
374	
375	A new marker is red and is called `Marker 1`, `Marker 2` and so on. Markers sit on whole frames, and two can't share one, so pressing <kbd>M</kbd> on a frame that already has one adds nothing and shows an alert saying a marker is already there.
376	
377	A marker draws on the ruler as a small flag with a thin line down the ruler, in its colour. An ordinary marker's flag is an outline, and a [chapter](#make-a-chapter) marker's is filled. A project can hold up to 1,024 markers.
378	
379	## Move, rename and remove a marker
380	
381	| To | Do this |
382	| --- | --- |
383	| Move a marker | Drag its flag along the ruler. You can grab it within 6 points of its line. It snaps as the playhead does, and it won't land on a frame that already has a marker. |
384	| Rename a marker | Double-click its flag, or type in its row in the Document tab. |
385	| Remove a marker | Choose **Delete** in its row in the Document tab. |
386	
387	Each of these is one undo step: **Move Marker**, **Rename Marker** or **Remove Marker**.
388	
389	Double-clicking a flag opens a field on the ruler. Return, Tab or a click elsewhere saves the name. <kbd>Esc</kbd> closes the field and keeps the old name, and saving an empty field does nothing. The name field in the Document tab is different: empty it and the marker has no name, and the field shows **Marker** in grey.
390	
391	## Jump between markers
392	
393	**Mark ▸ Next Marker** and **Mark ▸ Previous Marker** pause playback and move the playhead to the marker. Neither has a keyboard shortcut. They beep when there's no marker further in that direction, and they're dimmed when the project has no markers.
394	
395	You can also choose **Go** in a marker's row in the Document tab.
396	
397	## The Markers list
398	
399	The **Markers** section of the [Document tab](/projects/document-tab/) lists every marker in time order, with its time, its name, **Chapter**, **Go** and **Delete**. With no markers it reads "No markers. Press M to add one."
400	
401	## Make a chapter
402	
403	Tick **Chapter** in a marker's row, and its flag fills. It's one undo step, **Chapter Marker**, and unticking the box makes it an ordinary marker again.
404	
405	Chapter markers become chapters in exported MP4, MOV, M4A and WebM files, in time order. A chapter takes the marker's name, or "Chapter 1", "Chapter 2" and so on when the marker has no name. See [Chapters](/export/chapters/) for how a range export treats them.
406	
407	## Marker colours
408	
409	Markers are red unless an agent changes them, because a colour can only be set with `add_marker` or `set_marker`. The Document tab has no colour control. The colours are names, not hex values: `red`, `orange`, `yellow`, `green`, `blue` and `purple`, the same six as [clip labels](/timeline/names-and-labels/#colour-labels). Any other name draws the marker in the neutral text colour.
410	
411	## Good to know
412	
413	Markers belong to the whole timeline, and a nest has none of its own. While a [nest](/editing/nests/) is open:
414	
415	- The ruler shows no markers, and drags don't snap to them.
416	- The three marker commands in the **Mark** menu are off, and pressing <kbd>M</kbd> beeps.
417	- **Go** is disabled, because the playhead inside a nest counts from the nest's own start. Leave the nest with <kbd>⌘↑</kbd> to use it.
418	- The Document tab's list still shows every marker, and its name field, **Chapter** and **Delete** still work.
419	
420	## With an agent
421	
422	`add_marker` adds a marker at the playhead or at a time you give it, with its name, colour and chapter setting in the same call. `set_marker` moves a marker or changes any of those, and anything you leave out keeps its value. `remove_marker` removes one. See [Tools: tracks, markers and canvas](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/).
423	
424	An agent works to the same rule as you do inside a nest. With a nest open it can't add a marker or move one, but it can rename one, change its colour or chapter setting, or remove it. Sending any of the three with an explicit `scope` fails, because a nest has no markers. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/).
425	
426	## Related
427	
428	- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
429	- [The in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/)
430	- [Chapters](/export/chapters/)
431	- [The Document tab](/projects/document-tab/)
432	=== timeline/move-the-playhead.mdx
433	---
434	title: "Jump around the timeline"
435	description: "Move the playhead straight to the next cut, either end of the timeline, or a time you type."
436	---
437	
438	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
439	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
440	
441	These are the quick ways to put the playhead where you want it: hop from cut to cut, go to either end of the timeline, or type a time. To drag it along the ruler, see [The ruler and playhead](/timeline/ruler-and-playhead/). To step frame by frame, see [Play, pause and shuttle](/timeline/playback/). To hop between flags, see [Markers](/timeline/markers/).
442	
443	<AtAGlance
444	  keys={['↑', '↓', 'Home', 'End']}
445	  where={['The transport buttons in the toolbar', 'The timecode field in the toolbar']}
446	  tools="set_playhead"
447	/>
448	
449	## Jump between edit points
450	
451	Press <kbd>↑</kbd> for the previous edit point and <kbd>↓</kbd> for the next. The **Previous Edit Point** and **Next Edit Point** buttons either side of Play in the toolbar do the same.
452	
453	An edit point is the start or end of any clip, on any track, and the two ends of the timeline.
454	
455	- <kbd>↑</kbd> with nothing earlier goes to the start of the timeline.
456	- <kbd>↓</kbd> on the last edit point stays where it is.
457	- Playback keeps going. The playhead jumps and plays on from there.
458	- With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, these step through the nest's clips.
459	
460	## Go to the start or end
461	
462	Press <kbd>Home</kbd> for the start of the timeline and <kbd>End</kbd> for the end, or use the **Go to Start** and **Go to End** buttons, on the outer side of the edit point buttons. Both pause playback first.
463	
464	The keypad's Home and End work too, and so does the <kbd>fn</kbd> key with <kbd>←</kbd> or <kbd>→</kbd> on a keyboard without them. With a nest open, they go to the start and end of the nest.
465	
466	## Type a time to jump
467	
468	The toolbar shows the playhead's time in a field. You can type into it.
469	
470	<Steps>
471	
472	1. Click the time.
473	
474	2. Type where you want to go.
475	
476	3. Press <kbd>Return</kbd> or <kbd>Tab</kbd>, or click somewhere else in the editor.
477	
478	</Steps>
479	
480	Playback pauses, the playhead moves to the nearest frame, and the keys go back to the editor, so <kbd>Space</kbd> plays straight away.
481	
482	The field takes any of these, whichever way the project displays time. You can leave out leading zeros, so `1:05` and `01:05` mean the same.
483	
484	| You type | Example | It means |
485	| --- | --- | --- |
486	| Hours, minutes, seconds and frames | `00:01:23:12` | 1 minute 23 seconds and 12 frames |
487	| Hours, minutes and seconds with milliseconds | `00:01:23.500` | 1 minute 23.5 seconds |
488	| Hours, minutes and seconds | `1:23:04` | 1 hour 23 minutes 4 seconds |
489	| Minutes and seconds | `1:23` | 1 minute 23 seconds |
490	| Seconds with a decimal | `83.5` | 83.5 seconds |
491	| A bare number of seconds | `83` | 83 seconds |
492	
493	Text that isn't a time beeps, and the field goes back to the playhead's time. Only whole numbers count as frames, so `00:00:01:12.5` isn't a time.
494	
495	A leading minus sign is accepted, but the playhead can't go before the start, so a negative time lands on the first frame.
496	
497	The field shows frames by default. The [Document tab's **Timecode** row](/projects/background-and-timecode/) switches it to milliseconds, along with the duration beside it, the ruler and the times in the **Clip** and **Document** tabs. The field stops following the playhead while you type in it.
498	
499	## Read the duration
500	
501	After the time, the toolbar shows a slash and the length of what the timeline shows, such as `/ 00:00:05:07`. It's written the same way as the time, in frames or milliseconds.
502	
503	With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, both numbers are the nest's: the time counts from the nest's own start, and the duration is the nest's length.
504	
505	## Good to know
506	
507	- Moving the playhead is never an edit. It makes no undo step, and it isn't saved with the project.
508	- When a jump lands outside the visible part of the timeline, the view scrolls to bring the playhead back.
509	- With the preview canvas in focus and a clip selected, the arrow keys [nudge the clip](/canvas/move-scale-rotate/) instead of moving the playhead.
510	- With the text of the [Transcript tab](/captions/transcript-keys/) in focus, the arrow keys move through its words.
511	- None of these keys work while you're typing in a field or while a sheet is open. They do work in the [Preview Window](/timeline/preview-window/).
512	
513	## With an agent
514	
515	`set_playhead` moves the playhead to a time and seeks the preview. It doesn't pause playback. `split`, `freeze_frame` and `add_marker` use the playhead when they're given no time. See [Tools: playhead, range and selection](/mcp/tools-view-state/).
516	
517	## Related
518	
519	- [The ruler and playhead](/timeline/ruler-and-playhead/)
520	- [Play, pause and shuttle](/timeline/playback/)
521	- [Markers](/timeline/markers/)
522	- [The in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/)
523	- [Keyboard shortcuts](/reference/keyboard-shortcuts/)
524	=== timeline/names-and-labels.mdx
525	---
526	title: "Clip names and labels"
527	description: Give a clip its own name, clear it again, and mark clips with a colour label so a busy timeline is easier to read.
528	---
529	
530	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
531	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
532	
533	A name says what a clip is, and a colour label sorts it. Both help you find your way around a busy timeline.
534	
535	<AtAGlance
536	  menu={['Clip ▸ Rename…', 'Clip ▸ Label']}
537	  keys="⇧⌘R"
538	  where={['Double-click a clip on the timeline', 'The name field at the top of the Clip tab']}
539	  tools="set_clip"
540	/>
541	
542	## Rename a clip
543	
544	<Steps>
545	
546	1. Double-click the clip on the timeline, or select it and press <kbd>⇧⌘R</kbd> (**Clip ▸ Rename…**). A field opens over its name strip, showing the name the strip shows. With **Clip ▸ Rename…**, the timeline scrolls the clip into view first if it needs to.
547	
548	2. Type the name.
549	
550	3. Press Return or Tab, or click elsewhere.
551	
552	</Steps>
553	
554	The new name is its own undo step, **Rename Clip**, even when the click that ended it also made an edit.
555	
556	<kbd>Esc</kbd> closes the field and keeps the old name, with no undo step. Saving an empty field or an unchanged name does nothing, so a field you opened by accident is harmless.
557	
558	**Clip ▸ Rename…** is available when something is selected. With several clips selected, it opens the field on the first of them in timeline order. Spaces at either end of a name are trimmed.
559	
560	Double-clicking a nest clip opens the nest instead of renaming it. To rename a nest clip, select it and press <kbd>⇧⌘R</kbd>, or use the name field in the [Clip tab](#clear-a-name).
561	
562	## What a clip shows with no name
563	
564	A clip with no name of its own shows what it holds:
565	
566	| Clip | Shows |
567	| --- | --- |
568	| A nest | The nest's name |
569	| A clip from a file | The file's name |
570	| Text | Its words, or `Text` when it has none |
571	| A shape | The kind of shape |
572	| A graphic | `Graphic` |
573	| An adjustment clip | `Adjustment` |
574	
575	## Clear a name
576	
577	The name field at the top of the [Clip tab](/getting-started/inspector/) names one clip. Empty it to clear the clip's name and go back to what the clip holds. This is the only place you can clear a name, because the field on the timeline ignores an empty name.
578	
579	The field also renames the clip when you type in it, and either way it's one undo step, **Rename Clip**. It appears only with a single clip selected. With several selected, the header reads how many, for example "3 clips selected".
580	
581	## Colour labels
582	
583	<Steps>
584	
585	1. Select the clips.
586	
587	2. Choose a colour from **Clip ▸ Label**: **Red**, **Orange**, **Yellow**, **Green**, **Blue** or **Purple**. Choose **None** to remove a label.
588	
589	</Steps>
590	
591	A label applies to every selected clip as one undo step, **Label Clip**. Labels are for your own sorting, and they don't change how a clip plays or exports.
592	
593	A labelled clip has a small dot in its colour at the right end of its name strip. On a clip too narrow to fit both, the strip keeps its kind icon and drops the dot. See [Reading a clip](/timeline/reading-a-clip/).
594	
595	The menu is available when something is selected. It checks a colour when every selected clip has that label, and **None** when none has a label. Choosing a label every selected clip already has beeps and changes nothing.
596	
597	The [Clip tab](/getting-started/inspector/)'s header shows the dot at the end of the name line when every selected clip has the same label. There's no dot when they differ or none has one.
598	
599	## Good to know
600	
601	- A clip on a locked track can still be renamed, because a lock protects a clip's place on the timeline, and a name isn't placement.
602	- Split, duplicate, detach and paste carry a clip's name and label to the new clip. [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/) never does.
603	- The field stays open through a zoom or a change an agent makes. If the clip is deleted while the field is open, the field closes and what you typed is dropped.
604	- The same field renames [tracks](/timeline/manage-tracks/) and [markers](/timeline/markers/).
605	
606	## With an agent
607	
608	`set_clip` names or labels several clips in one step, where a person names one at a time. A name or label you leave out stays as it is, and null or an empty string clears it. It stores any label it's given, and one outside the six colours draws in the neutral text colour, so keep to the six. See [Tools: text, shapes and clip names](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/).
609	
610	## Related
611	
612	- [Reading a clip on the timeline](/timeline/reading-a-clip/)
613	- [Select clips](/timeline/selecting-clips/)

615	=== timeline/playback.mdx
616	---
617	title: Play, pause and shuttle
618	description: Play the timeline with Space, shuttle it at up to four times speed with J, K and L, and step it frame by frame.
619	---
620	
621	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
622	
623	Play the timeline to watch your edit. It all runs from the keyboard: <kbd>Space</kbd> plays and pauses, <kbd>J</kbd>, <kbd>K</kbd> and <kbd>L</kbd> shuttle forwards or backwards at up to four times speed, and the arrow keys step to the frame you want.
624	
625	<AtAGlance
626	  keys={['Space', 'J', 'K', 'L', '←', '→', '⇧←', '⇧→']}
627	  where="The Play and Pause button in the toolbar"
628	  tools="set_playhead"
629	/>
630	
631	## Play and pause
632	
633	Press <kbd>Space</kbd>, or the Play button among the toolbar's transport buttons. The button shows Play or Pause to match, and it stays in the same spot. There's no menu item for it.
634	
635	<kbd>Space</kbd> works from wherever the focus is in the window, with a few exceptions:
636	
637	| Where you are | What <kbd>Space</kbd> does |
638	| --- | --- |
639	| Typing in a text field, the Text tab's text area, the canvas text editor or the Media tab's search field | Types a space. Typing ends with <kbd>Return</kbd>, <kbd>Tab</kbd> or a click outside the field, and <kbd>Space</kbd> plays straight after. |
640	| On the preview canvas | Plays or pauses when you let go, because the press gets ready to [pan](/canvas/zoom-and-pan/). If you panned while holding it, letting go does nothing. |
641	| On a button, pop-up or segmented control focused with Full Keyboard Access | Presses that control. |
642	| With a sheet open | Doesn't play or pause. |
643	
644	<kbd>⇧Space</kbd> plays and pauses too. Any other modifier leaves the key alone. Holding <kbd>Space</kbd> down doesn't toggle playback over and over.
645	
646	## J, K and L
647	
648	<kbd>L</kbd> plays forward, <kbd>J</kbd> plays in reverse and <kbd>K</kbd> pauses.
649	
650	| Press | What happens |
651	| --- | --- |
652	| <kbd>L</kbd> or <kbd>J</kbd> while stopped | Plays at ×1 in that direction. |
653	| The same key again | Steps up from ×1 to ×2 to ×4. At ×4 it stays at ×4. |
654	| The opposite key | Goes straight to ×1 in that direction. |
655	| <kbd>K</kbd> | Pauses. |
656	
657	These keys also work from the [Transcript tab](/captions/transcript-keys/) and the [Preview Window](/timeline/preview-window/). They don't work while you're typing in a field or while a sheet is open.
658	
659	## Step frames
660	
661	<kbd>←</kbd> and <kbd>→</kbd> pause playback and move the playhead one frame. With <kbd>⇧</kbd>, they move ten. This is the way to place a cut exactly.
662	
663	Stepping is silent, unlike a [scrub on the ruler](/timeline/ruler-and-playhead/#scrub-on-the-ruler). Two places use these keys for something else:
664	
665	- With the preview canvas focused and a clip selected, they [nudge the clip](/canvas/move-scale-rotate/) on the canvas.
666	- In the [Transcript tab](/captions/transcript-keys/), they move by word.
667	
668	To go further in one press, see [Jump around the timeline](/timeline/move-the-playhead/).
669	
670	## At the end
671	
672	Playback stops at the end of the timeline, and the playhead stays there. Press <kbd>Home</kbd> to [go back to the start](/timeline/move-the-playhead/). With [Loop](/timeline/loop/) on, playback goes back to the start of the loop instead.
673	
674	An empty timeline has nothing to play, so Play, <kbd>J</kbd> and <kbd>L</kbd> beep.
675	
676	## After an edit
677	
678	You can edit while the timeline plays. What you notice depends on what you changed.
679	
680	### Look-only edits
681	
682	A change that only alters how something looks, such as a clip's position, a colour or some text, redraws the frame in place. Playback isn't interrupted.
683	
684	### Structural edits
685	
686	A move, a trim, a new clip or anything else that changes the timeline's shape makes Frame Job rebuild what the preview plays, in the background. So does a change to the sound, such as volume, pan or the compressor. It keeps your place and keeps playing at the same speed. While you drag, the rebuild waits until you pause briefly.
687	
688	### Failed rebuild
689	
690	If a rebuild fails, Frame Job shows the error and the previous version of the timeline keeps playing.
691

701	---
702	title: "Preview Quality"
703	description: Draw the preview at half or a quarter of the canvas size so a heavy project plays more smoothly, without changing what you export.
704	---
705	
706	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
707	
708	Preview Quality draws the preview smaller and scales it back up to fit, so a heavy project plays more smoothly. It never changes an export.
709	
710	<AtAGlance menu="View ▸ Preview Quality" />
711	
712	## Full, Half, Quarter
713	
714	Choose **View ▸ Preview Quality ▸ Full**, **Half** or **Quarter**. The menu checks the current choice. The preview redraws straight away, paused or playing.
715	
716	| Choice | Draws the preview at | 1920 × 1080 canvas |
717	| --- | --- | --- |
718	| **Full** (default) | The canvas size | 1920 × 1080 |
719	| **Half** | Half the width and height | 960 × 540 |
720	| **Quarter** | A quarter of the width and height | 480 × 270 |
721	
722	The choice is remembered between launches, for every project. There's no keyboard shortcut, and no agent tool sets it. The [Preview Window](/timeline/preview-window/) shows the same picture, so it draws at the same quality.
723	
724	## What it changes
725	
726	Quality only affects the preview. It never changes an export, a [saved frame](/export/save-frame/) or a frame an agent renders.
727	
728	A lower choice saves the work of drawing each pixel of the picture. Decoding your footage, drawing shadows and playing the sound cost the same at every choice, so a project held back by those won't speed up as much.
729	
730	## Good to know
731	
732	The picture always keeps the canvas's exact shape, so that handles stay in the right place on it. On an awkward canvas size that means the preview can draw a little larger than the fraction, never smaller:
733	
734	| Canvas | Half | Quarter |
735	| --- | --- | --- |
736	| 999 × 666 | 501 × 334 | 252 × 168 |
737	| 1001 × 667 | 1001 × 667 | 1001 × 667 |
738	
739	A canvas whose sides share no common factor, like 1001 × 667, can't be scaled down evenly, so it draws at full size at every choice.
740

746	=== timeline/preview-window.mdx
747	---
748	title: "The Preview Window"
749	description: Show the picture in a second window with no handles or guides, on another display or full screen.
750	---
751	
752	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
753	
754	The Preview Window shows the picture on its own, with no handles or guides over it. Use it to put the picture on a second display while you edit in the main window.
755	
756	<AtAGlance menu="View ▸ Preview Window" keys="⇧⌘P" />
757	
758	## Open the Preview Window
759	
760	Press <kbd>⇧⌘P</kbd> or choose **View ▸ Preview Window**. The same key hides it again, and the menu item has a checkmark while it's open. It opens on an empty timeline too, where the window is black.
761	
762	The window is titled after the project, for example "Intro — Preview", and has a black surround. You can resize it down to 320 × 200, and it can go full screen.
763	
764	It uses the same player as the main preview, so the two never drift apart. [Preview Quality](/timeline/preview-quality/), **Show Ungraded**, **Show Selection** and **Show SDR Version** all apply to it, but the [corner tags](/timeline/preview/#preview-tags) don't appear in it.
765	
766	The window is only for looking. Safe-area guides, zoom and the handles for moving clips stay in the main preview.
767	
768	## Remembered position
769	
770	The window remembers its position and size between launches, so it opens where you last left it, on a second display for example. The first time, it opens at 640 × 360 in the middle of the screen. It stays visible when you switch to another app.
771	
772	It closes with its project window. Whether it's open isn't remembered, so it starts off in each new window.
773	
774	## Keys
775	
776	The window doesn't take you away from the editor. While it has the focus:
777	
778	- Playback keys work: <kbd>Space</kbd>, <kbd>J</kbd>, <kbd>K</kbd>, <kbd>L</kbd>, the arrows, Home and End.
779	- The editor's other single-letter keys work too, such as <kbd>M</kbd> for a marker or <kbd>I</kbd> and <kbd>O</kbd> for the range.
780	- Every editor ⌘ command works, so <kbd>⌘E</kbd> opens the export sheet and <kbd>⌘T</kbd> splits.
781	- <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> undoes the project's last step, and <kbd>⇧⌘Z</kbd> redoes it, the same steps as in the editor.
782	- <kbd>⌘W</kbd> closes the Preview Window, not the project.
783	
784	Single-letter keys stop while a field in the editor window is being edited, or while the editor has a sheet open.
785	
786	## Good to know
787	
788	- There's one saved position for every project. With two projects' Preview Windows open at once, the second opens on top of the first, and only one of them saves where it's moved to.
789	- The window isn't listed in the **Window** menu. Use **View ▸ Preview Window** to find it.
790	- After you save a project under a new name, the title updates the next time you show the window.
791

802	---
803	
804	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
805	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
806	
807	The preview shows the frame under the playhead, so you can see what you're making while you edit and play.
808	
809	<AtAGlance
810	  menu={['View ▸ Safe Areas', 'View ▸ Show Ungraded', 'View ▸ Show Selection', 'View ▸ Show SDR Version', 'View ▸ Show Subjects', 'View ▸ Scopes', 'View ▸ Loudness Meter']}
811	  keys={['⌃⌘U', '⌃⌘W', '⌃⌘L']}
812	  where="The editor window, top left, above the timeline"
813	/>
814	
815	## What it shows
816	
817	The picture keeps the canvas's shape, letterboxed to fit the pane to the left of the inspector. Under it, a small caption gives the canvas size and frame rate, for example `1920 × 1080 · 30 fps`.
818	
819	The preview is also where you work on the picture: selecting clips, then moving, scaling, rotating and cropping them. That's covered in [The canvas](/canvas/the-canvas/), and zooming it in [Zoom and pan the preview](/canvas/zoom-and-pan/).
820	
821	Two settings change how the preview is drawn, and neither touches an export:
822	
823	- [Preview Quality](/timeline/preview-quality/) draws it smaller, so heavy projects play more smoothly.
824	- [The Preview Window](/timeline/preview-window/) shows the same picture in a second window, for another display.
825	
826	## Preview tags
827	
828	Small tags in the top-left corner of the pane tell you when the picture isn't the plain one. Each shows only while its **View** item is on.
829	
830	| Tag | Means | View item |
831	| --- | --- | --- |
832	| **Ungraded** | The picture shows no clip's grade. | [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/) |
833	| **Selection** | The picture shows which pixels the selected adjustment clip's qualifier picks. | [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/) |
834	| **SDR Version** | The picture shows the project's SDR version. | [Show SDR Version](/hdr/show-sdr-version/) |
835	
836	<Shot
837	  name="04b-preview-scopes.preview"
838	  alt="The preview pane with the Ungraded tag in its top-left corner, the picture with its caption 960 × 540 · 30 fps underneath, and the scopes panel beside it showing a waveform over a vectorscope."
839	/>
840	
841	The tags sit in that order, and a hidden tag leaves no space, so **Selection** moves into the corner when **Ungraded** is off. **SDR Version** shows in an SDR project too, where the picture doesn't change.
842	
843	## Other View items
844	
845	The **View** menu holds the other switches for the preview. Each has its own page.
846	
847	| Item | Keys | What it does | Remembered |
848	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
849	| [**Safe Areas**](/canvas/safe-areas/) | | Shows the title-safe and action-safe guides, the same as the toolbar's **Safe** box. Checked when on. | Yes |
850	| [**Show Ungraded**](/color/show-ungraded/) | <kbd>⌃⌘U</kbd> | Shows the picture as if no clip were graded. | No |
851	| [**Show Selection**](/color/show-selection/) | | Shows what an adjustment clip's qualifier picks. It needs a selected adjustment clip to turn on. | No |
852	| [**Show SDR Version**](/hdr/show-sdr-version/) | | Shows an HDR project's SDR version. | No |
853	| [**Show Subjects**](/framing/show-subjects/) | | Draws the faces, people and salient regions found for the selected clip. | No |
854	| [**Scopes**](/color/scopes/) | <kbd>⌃⌘W</kbd> | Shows the scopes panel beside the picture. | No |
855	| [**Loudness Meter**](/audio/loudness-meter/) | <kbd>⌃⌘L</kbd> | Shows the live loudness column beside the picture. | No |
856	
857	Remembered means between launches, for every project. The items that aren't remembered start off in each new window, as the [Preview Window](/timeline/preview-window/) does, and none of these changes an export.
858	
859	**View ▸ Assistant** (<kbd>⌃⌘A</kbd>) sits nearby but doesn't change the picture. It opens the inspector's Assistant tab, beside the preview. See [Chat with the Assistant](/assistant/chat/).
