867	=== timeline/reading-a-clip.mdx
868	---
869	title: Reading a clip on the timeline
870	description: What every colour, symbol, line and handle on a clip block means, so you can read a timeline without selecting anything.
871	---
872	
873	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
874	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
875	
876	A clip on the timeline tells you what it is, what it holds and what's been done to it, without being selected. This page is the key to those marks. Each mark's control has its own page, linked from here.
877	
878	<AtAGlance where="The timeline's lanes" tools={['set_selection', 'set_audio']} />
879	
880	<Shot
881	  name="04-editor.window"
882	  alt="The editor with four tracks on the timeline: a green audio clip with its fade handles and a white volume line, two teal clips for a shape and a graphic, and an amber text clip. Each clip has its name in a darker strip along the top with a small symbol for its kind, and the playhead runs through every track."
883	/>
884	
885	## The clip block
886	
887	Each clip draws as one block with 2 pt rounded corners and a thin border, so you can always see where one clip ends and the next begins.
888	
889	From top to bottom, a block holds its name strip, its action lane if it has actions, its filmstrip and its waveform. The filmstrip sits under a tint of the clip's own colour and the waveform is drawn on that colour, so a clip reads as one coloured object rather than a row of photographs.
890	
891	The action lane shows a band for each [action](/motion/action-lane/). The selected action's span is also tinted down the whole height of the clip, in the action colour: mint in dark mode, a deeper green in light mode.
892	
893	## Colour by kind
894	
895	A clip's colour and the symbol on its name strip tell you its kind.
896	
897	| Kind | Colour | Symbol |
898	| --- | --- | --- |
899	| Video | Slate | A strip of film |
900	| Audio | Green | A waveform |
901	| Image | Violet | A photo |
902	| Freeze frame | Violet | A snowflake |
903	| Text | Amber | Letters |
904	| Shape | Teal | A square on a circle |
905	| Graphic | Teal | Curly braces |
906	| Nest | Grey | A stack of squares |
907	| Adjustment | Rose | Overlapping filter circles |
908	
909	The kind comes from what the clip shows, not only from its file. A video file's clip with its picture switched off reads as audio, in green with the waveform symbol. That's how the sound half of a [Detach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/) pair looks.
910	
911	A [label](/timeline/names-and-labels/) never changes the block's colour, because the colour says what the clip is and a label is something you said about it.
912	
913	## The name strip
914	
915	The darker strip along the top of a clip carries, from left to right, its kind symbol, a link symbol if it's [linked](#linked-clips), its name, a wave if it has a During motion, and its label dot.
916	
917	A clip with a name of its own shows that. Otherwise it shows what it holds: a nest's name, the file's name, the text itself, or the shape's kind. A clip with none of those reads as its kind, such as **Graphic** or **Adjustment**. A name too long for the strip ends in an ellipsis.
918	
919	On a narrow clip the strip leaves out what won't fit. The kind symbol stays longest, and the dot and the wave are left out when they'd run into the symbols.
920	
921	### The label dot
922	
923	A labelled clip shows a small dot in its label colour at the right end of the name strip. See [Clip names and labels](/timeline/names-and-labels/).
924	
925	### Motion marks
926	
927	Two small marks show a clip's active [motion presets](/motion/motion-presets/):
928	
929	- **A wedge** along the bottom of the name strip, from the left end for an In preset and from the right end for an Out preset. It's as long as the preset's duration at the current zoom, and it rises towards its inner end, so you can see how far into the clip the motion runs. It's never shorter than 2 pt or wider than the clip.
930	- **A small wave** at the right end of the strip, to the left of any label dot, for a During movement.
931	
932	## Picture and sound
933	
934	Below the name strip, a clip shows what it holds: its picture as a filmstrip, its sound as a waveform, or both.
935	
936	### Filmstrip
937	
938	Thumbnails run along the picture part of a video or image clip, each 34 pt wide and cropped to fill its tile.
939	
940	A file's strip holds one frame for each second, so a thumbnail shows that point in the clip to within a second or so. It follows the clip's trims, speed, reverse and speed ramps. A filmstrip of a log file with a [Camera Log](/hdr/camera-log/) set, or of an HDR file in PQ or HLG, shows the converted picture, matching the preview, not the flat image in the file.
941	
942	The strip covers the first 600 seconds of a file. Later in a longer file, the clip shows its plain colour.
943	
944	An image has one thumbnail, so only the first second of an image clip shows it. A freeze frame's strip starts at the moment it froze.
945	
946	Text, shape, graphic, nest and adjustment clips have no thumbnails.
947	
948	### Waveform
949	
950	A clip with sound draws it as a waveform, below the filmstrip when the clip has both. The waveform follows the clip's source time through speed changes and ramps. A nest clip draws no waveform, even when it has sound.
951	
952	The waveform draws faded when the clip or its track is muted, or when another track's solo silences it. A track's mute button stays unlit under another track's solo, so the waveform is the place to look to see what's in the mix. See [How audio works](/audio/how-audio-works/) and [Mute and solo tracks](/audio/mute-and-solo/).
953	
954	### Filling in after import
955	
956	Filmstrips and waveforms are made once for each file and kept with the project, so they fill in a moment after you add a file. See [On-device media analysis](/projects/media-analysis/).
957	
958	## Lines over a clip
959	
960	Up to four thin lines show how a clip changes over time, and each has its own control.
961	
962	### The volume line
963	
964	A thin white line over the waveform shows the level you hear from the clip, with its volume, fades, ducking and volume actions folded in. The top of the audio part is +30 dB and the bottom is −60 dB, and a silenced clip's line lies along the bottom. Small squares in the action colour mark where a volume action ends.
965	
966	Nest clips don't draw it. To change the level from the timeline, see [The volume line](/audio/volume-line/).
967	
968	### The duck line
969	
970	A thin yellow line over a clip set to duck by speech shows where the rest of the mix goes down and comes back. The top of the audio part is the mix at full level and the bottom is silence.
971	
972	A duck set to **Clip Length** draws no line, because it lasts as long as the clip. See [Duck by Speech](/audio/duck-by-speech/).
973	
974	### The Hide While Silent line
975	
976	A teal line across the picture part of a clip with [Hide While Silent](/effects/hide-while-silent/) on shows where the clip fades out in each pause and back in before speech. The top is fully shown and the bottom is fully hidden. The line appears once Frame Job has analysed the speech in the file the clip follows.
977	
978	### The rate line
979	
980	A clip with a [speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/) draws its rate as a white line with a dark edge across its action lane, here and in the Clip tab's lane. The bottom of the lane is the clip's own slowest rate and the top its fastest, so a small ramp looks as tall as a big one. Read the numbers in the Speed section.
981	
982	The timeline draws it at the Medium and Large [track heights](/timeline/track-height/), not at Small.
983	
984	## Fade handles
985	
986	Small white squares at the top corners of a clip's audio part set its fades. Drag one inward to fade in or out. The square sits at the corner with no fade, and at the end of the fade once there is one.
987	
988	The fade's length snaps to whole frames and stops at the clip's length. It doesn't snap to clip edges. The handles write the same two values as the Fades section, so see [Audio fades](/audio/fades/) for the rest.
989	
990	## The transition zone
991	
992	The overlap between two clips draws as a hatched zone with a solid edge down each side. The transition's kind is written in it when the whole word fits. On a short transition the word is left out, and the [Transition section](/motion/transition-settings/) still names it. See [Transitions](/motion/transitions/).
993	
994	## Selected clips
995	
996	A selected clip gets a 2 pt coral ring, and most commands act on it. When the clip is wide enough to trim and its track is unlocked, it also shows a [trim](/editing/trimming/) grip at each end. See [Select clips](/timeline/selecting-clips/).
997	
998	## Linked clips
999	
1000	A picture and the sound Detach Audio split from it each show a link symbol after their kind symbol. Select one and the other gets a dashed ring in your Mac's accent colour, because moving one moves both. See [Detach and Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/).
1001	
1002	## Dimmed clips
1003	
1004	A clip draws dimmed when its track is hidden, or when both its picture and its sound are switched off. A muted clip isn't dimmed. Only its waveform fades.
1005	
1006	## Adjustment clips
1007	
1008	An [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) is a plain rose block with only its name strip and action lane. It has no filmstrip or waveform, and its track is as tall as a picture track.
1009	
1010	## Good to know
1011	
1012	- A short track leaves marks out. The filmstrip needs 10 pt of height, the waveform, duck line and Hide While Silent line 8 pt, the fade handles 10 pt and the volume line 12 pt. A text clip at the Small [track height](/timeline/track-height/) is little more than its name strip.
1013	- A [locked track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/) draws a faint hatch across its whole lane, over its clips. Clips on it show no trim grips, and their fade handles don't drag.
1014	- On a [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/), clips draw at half strength with a dashed outline.
1015	- Inside an open [nest](/editing/nests/), a Hide While Silent line that follows a file outside the nest stays flat along the top, though the clip still fades.
1016	
1017	## Related
1018

1024	=== timeline/ruler-and-playhead.mdx
1025	---
1026	title: The ruler and playhead
1027	description: Read the timeline's time ruler, scrub along it, and see how the playhead decides where edits land.
1028	---
1029	
1030	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
1031	
1032	The ruler is the strip of time above the tracks. The playhead marks one moment on it: the frame the preview shows, and the point where most edits land.
1033	
1034	<AtAGlance where="The ruler above the timeline's tracks" tools="set_playhead" />
1035	
1036	## The playhead
1037	
1038	The playhead is the coral line down every track, with a triangle head on the ruler. A click or a drag lands it on a frame.
1039	
1040	## Scrub on the ruler
1041	
1042	Click the ruler to move the playhead there, and drag along it to scrub. Pressing on the ruler pauses playback, and it stays paused when you let go.
1043	
1044	While you scrub, you hear the sound under the playhead. The press plays a short piece of it, and the drag plays more as it reaches new frames. See [Hear a scrub](/audio/scrub-audio/).
1045	
1046	The scrub [snaps](/timeline/snapping/) like any other drag. Hold <kbd>⌘</kbd> to scrub without snapping.
1047	
1048	A press within 6 pt of a marker's flag grabs the [marker](/timeline/markers/), not the ruler, so start the scrub beside it.
1049	
1050	## Lane clicks
1051	
1052	A click in a lane doesn't move the playhead. On empty space it starts a [marquee selection](/timeline/selecting-clips/), and a plain click there clears the selection.
1053	
1054	The exception is a click on an [action band](/motion/action-lane/), which moves the playhead to the end of that action so the preview shows its end state.
1055	
1056	## The edit point
1057	
1058	These commands work at the playhead, so put it where you want the edit first:
1059	
1060	| Command | Key |
1061	| --- | --- |
1062	| [**Clip ▸ Split**](/editing/splitting/) | <kbd>⌘T</kbd> |
1063	| [**Clip ▸ Trim Start to Playhead**](/editing/trimming/#trim-to-the-playhead) | <kbd>W</kbd> |
1064	| [**Clip ▸ Trim End to Playhead**](/editing/trimming/#trim-to-the-playhead) | <kbd>E</kbd> |
1065	| [**Clip ▸ Freeze Frame**](/speed/freeze-frame/) | <kbd>⇧⌘F</kbd> |
1066	| [**Edit ▸ Paste**](/editing/copy-and-paste/) | <kbd>⌘V</kbd> |
1067	| [**Edit ▸ Insert at Playhead**](/editing/insert-and-overwrite/) | No key |
1068	| [**Edit ▸ Overwrite at Playhead**](/editing/insert-and-overwrite/) | No key |
1069	| [**Mark ▸ Add Marker**](/timeline/markers/) | <kbd>M</kbd> |
1070	
1071	To place the playhead exactly, [step by frames](/timeline/playback/#step-frames) or [jump around the timeline](/timeline/move-the-playhead/).
1072	
1073	## Ticks and labels
1074	
1075	The ruler's ticks adapt to the zoom. Zoomed in, they mark single frames. As you zoom out, they step through 2, 5 and 10 frames, then 1, 2, 5, 10, 15 and 30 seconds, then 1, 2, 5, 10, 15 and 30 minutes, and at the widest one hour.
1076	
1077	Labels use the project's timecode format, **Frames** or **Milliseconds**, set in [the Document tab](/projects/background-and-timecode/). A timeline under an hour long drops the leading `00:` from its labels so they fit.
1078	
1079	The ruler also carries [markers](/timeline/markers/), the [in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/) and the selected [action's](/motion/action-lane/) span. Inside an open [nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/), it counts from the nest's own start and shows no markers.
1080	
1081	## Following the playhead
1082	
1083	The timeline scrolls itself to keep the playhead in view, during playback and after a jump. When the playhead comes within 24 pt of either edge of the visible part, or leaves it, the view moves so the playhead sits about a third of the way in.
1084	
1085	## With an agent
1086	
1087	`set_playhead` moves the playhead and the preview, in silence. It isn't an edit, so there's nothing to undo. An agent that splits, freezes a frame or adds a marker without giving a time works at the playhead. See [Tools: playhead, range and selection](/mcp/tools-view-state/).
1088

1097	---
1098	title: "Select clips"
1099	description: "Pick the clips you want to work on by clicking, dragging a marquee, or choosing a whole track or everything after the playhead."
1100	---
1101	
1102	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
1103	
1104	The selection tells Frame Job which clips you mean. The inspector, the handles on the canvas and the commands in the menus all work on it. Selecting a clip changes nothing in the project.
1105	
1106	<AtAGlance
1107	  menu={['Edit ▸ Select All', 'Edit ▸ Select After Playhead', 'Edit ▸ Select All on Track']}
1108	  keys={['⌘A', '⌥⌘A']}
1109	  where={['Click, ⇧-click or drag on the timeline', '⌥-click a track header']}
1110	  tools="set_selection"
1111	/>
1112	
1113	## Click a clip
1114	
1115	Click a clip to select it alone. It gets an outline, and the timeline bar names it.
1116	
1117	Clicking a clip that's already part of a larger selection keeps the whole selection, so you can drag the clips together. To get down to one clip, click empty space first, then click the clip.
1118	
1119	You can click a clip on a [locked track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/) to select it and read it in the inspector, but you can't drag or trim it.
1120	
1121	A double-click goes further: it [renames the clip](/timeline/names-and-labels/), or goes inside a [nest](/editing/nests/).
1122	
1123	## Add or remove a clip
1124	
1125	<kbd>⇧</kbd>-click a clip to add it to the selection. <kbd>⇧</kbd>-click a selected clip to take it out.
1126	
1127	## Drag a marquee
1128	
1129	Drag from any empty part of the timeline: a gap in a lane, the strip under the ruler, or the space below the last lane. A band follows the pointer and selects every clip it touches, however little of the clip it covers.
1130	
1131	- A plain drag replaces the selection.
1132	- <kbd>⇧</kbd>-drag adds to the selection. Clips already selected stay selected.
1133	- Clips on locked tracks are skipped.
1134	
1135	## Clear the selection
1136	
1137	Click an empty part of a lane, or the space above or below the lanes.
1138	
1139	:::caution
1140	A double-click in an empty part of a lane [closes that gap](/editing/close-gaps/). That's an edit, not a deselect. Press <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> if you did it by accident.
1141	:::
1142	
1143	## Select all the clips
1144	
1145	**Edit ▸ Select All** (<kbd>⌘A</kbd>) selects every clip in the timeline you're editing, on locked tracks too. With a nest open, it selects the clips inside the nest.
1146	
1147	While you're typing in a field, <kbd>⌘A</kbd> selects the field's text instead. With the [Transcript tab](/captions/transcript-keys/)'s text in focus, it selects the words.
1148	
1149	## Select everything after the playhead
1150	
1151	**Edit ▸ Select After Playhead** (<kbd>⌥⌘A</kbd>) selects every clip whose start is at or after the playhead, on every track, including locked ones. A clip the playhead is partway through isn't included.
1152	
1153	Use it to push the rest of a project along: select everything after the playhead, then [drag it to make room](/editing/close-gaps/#open-room-by-hand).
1154	
1155	## Select all the clips on a track
1156	
1157	<kbd>⌥</kbd>-click a track's header to select every clip on that track, locked or not. On an empty track, this leaves nothing selected.
1158	
1159	**Edit ▸ Select All on Track** does the same for the current track, which is the track of the first selected clip, or the [front track](/timeline/tracks/) (the top lane) when nothing is selected. It's dimmed when the timeline has no clips, and it beeps when the current track is empty.
1160	
1161	## See what's selected
1162	
1163	The left end of the timeline bar names the selection.
1164	
1165	| Selected | The bar shows |
1166	| --- | --- |
1167	| One clip | A chip in the colour of the clip's kind (video, audio, text and so on), the clip's name, and its track and kind under it, such as `Track 2 · video` |
1168	| Several clips | A count such as `3 clips`, over the track (or `2 tracks`) and the kind (or `mixed`) |
1169	| Nothing | `No selection` |
1170	
1171	This block is a fixed width, so a long name is cut short and the tools beside it never move.
1172	
1173	## How a selection behaves
1174	
1175	A selection isn't an edit. It's never an undo step, it doesn't mark the project as changed, and it isn't saved, so a project always opens with nothing selected.
1176	
1177	- Selecting clips, on the timeline or with the Edit menu's commands, switches the inspector from the **Media** or **Document** tab to its **Clip** tab. The **Transcript** tab stays where it is.
1178	- The timeline and the canvas share one selection. See [Select on the canvas](/canvas/select-on-canvas/).
1179	- A clip that's deleted drops out of the selection.
1180	- Going into a nest or coming back out changes the selection, because the clips on show are different.
1181	
1182	## With an agent
1183	
1184	`set_selection` sets the selection, and with no clips it clears it. An agent doesn't need it to edit, because its tools name their own clips. It matters for what depends on the selection, such as the canvas handles and the inspector. With a nest open, it selects inside the nest. See [Tools: playhead, range and selection](/mcp/tools-view-state/).
1185

1192	=== timeline/snapping.mdx
1193	---
1194	title: "Snapping"
1195	description: "Make timeline drags catch clip edges, markers, the playhead and the in and out points, and turn it off when you don't want it."
1196	---
1197	
1198	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
1199	
1200	Snapping makes a drag catch the useful points on the timeline, so a clip lines up with the next cut instead of landing a frame away from it. This page is about the timeline. For dragging on the picture, see [Canvas snapping](/canvas/canvas-snapping/).
1201	
1202	<AtAGlance
1203	  menu="View ▸ Snapping"
1204	  keys="N"
1205	  where="The Snap checkbox in the timeline bar"
1206	/>
1207	
1208	## Turn snapping on or off
1209	
1210	Press <kbd>N</kbd>, click the **Snap** checkbox in the timeline bar, or choose **View ▸ Snapping**, which has a tick when snapping is on. The menu item shows no key, because <kbd>N</kbd> is one of the keys the editor handles itself.
1211	
1212	Snapping is on by default, and your choice is remembered between launches. One setting serves both the timeline and the canvas. There's no agent tool for it.
1213	
1214	## What a drag snaps to
1215	
1216	These drags snap:
1217	
1218	- moving clips
1219	- trimming a clip's edge
1220	- a [rate stretch](/speed/rate-stretch/)
1221	- a [roll](/editing/slip-and-roll/)
1222	- dragging a [marker](/timeline/markers/)
1223	- scrubbing along the [ruler](/timeline/ruler-and-playhead/)
1224	
1225	They catch these targets:
1226	
1227	- the start and the end of the timeline
1228	- the edges of other clips, but never of the clips you're dragging
1229	- markers
1230	- the playhead
1231	- the in and out points
1232	
1233	A target catches when it's within 8 points on screen, the unit macOS measures the screen in. That's the same distance at every zoom, so when you're zoomed out it covers more time. If two targets are equally close, the earlier one wins.
1234	
1235	When you move clips, it's the start of the earliest clip you're dragging that snaps, and the whole group moves with it. The end of a moved clip doesn't catch anything.
1236	
1237	Inside a [nest](/editing/nests/), there are no markers to catch, and the other targets are the nest's own.
1238	
1239	## Turn snapping off for one drag
1240	
1241	Hold <kbd>⌘</kbd> during the drag. It works from the moment you press or at any time during the drag, and it takes effect the next time the pointer moves. Let go of <kbd>⌘</kbd> and the drag snaps again.
1242	
1243	This works on the canvas too, and it changes nothing that's remembered.
1244	
1245	## See what a drag caught
1246	
1247	When a drag snaps, a thin vertical line runs across the timeline at the target it caught. Scrubbing the ruler snaps too, but it draws no line. The playhead is already there to show you.
1248	
1249	## Drags land on whole frames
1250	
1251	A drag that doesn't snap still lands on a whole frame. That's true with snapping off, while you're holding <kbd>⌘</kbd>, and when nothing is close enough to catch.
1252	
1253	## What never snaps
1254	
1255	- A [slip](/editing/slip-and-roll/) never snaps.
1256	- A row from the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/) dropped on a lane lands on the nearest frame at the pointer, and doesn't snap to edges.
1257	- Dragging an [action band](/motion/action-lane/) lands on whole frames, and doesn't snap.
1258	- Dragging a [fade handle](/audio/fades/) doesn't snap.
1259	
1260	## Good to know
1261	
1262	A window reads the setting when it opens. If two projects are open, changing it in one leaves the other as it is until you close that project and open it again.
1263	
1264	## Related

1272	---
1273	title: Track height
1274	description: Choose small, medium or large track rows, and see how a track's contents and the row size change what a clip shows.
1275	---
1276	
1277	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
1278	
1279	Track height sets how tall the timeline's rows are. Go small to see more tracks at once, or large to get more room for filmstrips, waveforms and actions.
1280	
1281	<AtAGlance
1282	  menu={['View ▸ Timeline Track Height ▸ Small', 'View ▸ Timeline Track Height ▸ Medium', 'View ▸ Timeline Track Height ▸ Large']}
1283	  where="The S / M / L control at the right end of the timeline bar"
1284	/>
1285	
1286	## Small, Medium, Large
1287	
1288	Click **S**, **M** or **L** at the right end of the timeline bar, or choose a size from **View ▸ Timeline Track Height**. The menu checks the size you're on.
1289	
1290	Medium is the default. Your choice is remembered between launches and applies to every project, because it's a view setting and not part of the project. It makes no undo step, and no agent tool sets it.
1291	
1292	## Height follows contents
1293	
1294	A track's height also depends on what it holds, so sound-only and text tracks draw shorter than picture tracks.
1295	
1296	| Track holds | Small | Medium | Large |
1297	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
1298	| Only text and shapes | 30 pt | 44 pt | 58 pt |
1299	| Only clips with sound and no picture | 40 pt | 60 pt | 82 pt |
1300	| Anything else, an empty track included | 54 pt | 84 pt | 116 pt |
1301	
1302	The row changes as the track's contents do. A music track grows to picture height when you drop a video on it, for example. An adjustment clip, a graphic or a nest counts as picture.
1303	
1304	A clip's own switches count. A detached sound, with its picture off, is a clip with sound and no picture.
1305	
1306	## What each size shows
1307	
1308	Every clip keeps its 16 pt name strip, and the rest of the row goes to its filmstrip, its waveform and its actions. So at Small a clip shows little more than its name: 8 pt is left under the strip on a text row, 18 pt on a sound row and 32 pt on a picture row.
1309	
1310	The action lane under the name strip changes with the size:
1311	
1312	| Size | Lane height | Each action band shows |
1313	| --- | --- | --- |
1314	| Small | 5 pt | A plain bar. |
1315	| Medium | 12 pt | Its number in time order, and a zoom glyph for a zoom action. |
1316	| Large | 18 pt | The same, plus the properties it changes. |
1317	
1318	See [Reading a clip on the timeline](/timeline/reading-a-clip/) for what each part of a clip means.
1319	
1320	## Good to know
1321	
1322	- A size change applies to the window you made it in. Other windows that are already open keep their size, and the next one you open uses your latest choice.
1323	- While you drag a clip, lanes keep their heights, so the track you're aiming at doesn't move under the pointer. They settle when you drop.
1324

1330	=== timeline/tracks.mdx
1331	---
1332	title: Tracks
1333	description: What a track is, how tracks stack, which track a command acts on, and what the switches in a track header do.
1334	---
1335	
1336	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
1337	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
1338	
1339	A track is a row on the timeline that holds clips. Tracks are the layers of your video: what sits on a higher lane draws in front of what sits on a lower one.
1340	
1341	<AtAGlance
1342	  menu={['Track ▸ Hide Video', 'Track ▸ Mute Audio', 'Track ▸ Lock Track', 'Track ▸ Solo', 'Track ▸ Mix…']}
1343	  where={['The header at the left of each track', 'Right-click a track header or an empty stretch of its lane']}
1344	  tools={['set_track']}
1345	/>
1346	
1347	<Shot
1348	  name="04-editor.window"
1349	  alt="The editor window. Along the bottom, the timeline has one row per track. Each row has a header on the left with the track's name and its row of switches, and the track's clips run along the lane to the right."
1350	/>
1351	
1352	## One kind of track
1353	
1354	Frame Job has one kind of track, and it holds any mix of clips: video, audio, a still, text, a shape, a graphic, a nest or an adjustment clip. There are no separate video and audio tracks, so a title and a music file can sit on the same track. What a track holds only changes [how tall its lane is drawn](/timeline/track-height/).
1355	
1356	Clips on one track play one after another. To show two things at once, put them on two tracks. Overlapping two clips on the same track makes a [transition](/motion/transitions/), not a layer.
1357	
1358	## Stacking order
1359	
1360	The top lane is the front-most track and the bottom lane is the back. Where two clips overlap in the frame, the one on the higher lane draws over the one below.
1361	
1362	The order affects the picture, not the sound. To change it, [drag a track header](/timeline/manage-tracks/#reorder-tracks). A [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/) is the one case where a track's neighbour matters, because it cuts the track directly behind it.
1363	
1364	## The current track
1365	
1366	Some commands act on one track without asking which. They use the current track: the track of the first selected clip, or the front-most track when nothing is selected. To aim one of these commands at a track, select a clip on it first.
1367	
1368	| Command | What it does to the current track |
1369	| --- | --- |
1370	| **Track ▸ Remove Track** | Removes it. |
1371	| **Track ▸ Hide Video**, **Mute Audio**, **Lock Track** and **Solo** | Flips that switch. |
1372	| **Track ▸ Mix…** and **Track ▸ Matte** | Opens its mix panel, or sets its matte. |
1373	| **Clip ▸ Close Gap** | Closes the gap under the playhead on it. |
1374	| **Edit ▸ Select All on Track** | Selects every clip on it. |
1375	| **Edit ▸ Insert at Playhead** and **Edit ▸ Overwrite at Playhead** | Places the Media tab's selected file on it. |
1376	
1377	The [track context menu](/timeline/manage-tracks/#the-track-context-menu) doesn't use the current track. It acts on the track you clicked, whatever is selected.
1378	
1379	With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, the current track is one of the nest's own tracks.
1380	
1381	## Track names
1382	
1383	Each header shows its track's name. A new track gets a name such as `Track 3`, from the number of tracks there were when you added it. That name is the track's own, so it stays when you reorder the stack, and two tracks can end up with the same name.
1384	
1385	A track with no name at all shows `Track N` instead, counting up from the back track as 1. That label follows the track's place in the stack.
1386	
1387	To change a name, see [Rename a track](/timeline/manage-tracks/#rename-a-track).
1388	
1389	## The track header
1390	
1391	Each track has a header on the left with its name and five switches. Click a switch to use it.
1392	
1393	| Switch | Symbol, off and on | What it does |
1394	| --- | --- | --- |
1395	| **Hide Video** | Eye, struck-through eye | Takes the track's picture out of the preview and the export. See [Hide Video](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/#hide-video). |
1396	| **Mute Audio** | Speaker, crossed-out speaker | Silences the track's sound. See [Mute and solo tracks](/audio/mute-and-solo/). |
1397	| **Lock Track** | Open padlock, closed padlock | Protects the track from edits. See [Lock Track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/#lock-track). |
1398	| **Solo** | Headphones, both | Silences every other track that isn't soloed too. Pictures stay. See [Mute and solo tracks](/audio/mute-and-solo/). |
1399	| **Mix** | Sliders, both | Opens the track's mix panel: volume, pan, compressor and limiter. See [Track volume and pan](/audio/track-volume-and-pan/). |
1400	
1401	A switch that's on is lit in the accent colour with a highlight behind it, so you can read a track's state from the symbol or the highlight. **Solo** and **Mix** keep the same symbol either way, so the highlight is what tells you. **Mix** is lit while the track's volume or pan is off its default, or a compressor or limiter is on.
1402	
1403	Each flip of **Hide Video**, **Mute Audio**, **Lock Track** or **Solo** is one undo step. **Mix** opens its panel and changes nothing by itself.
1404	
1405	The header itself does more than hold the switches:
1406	
1407	| To | Do this |
1408	| --- | --- |
1409	| Rename the track | Double-click the header. |
1410	| Move it up or down the stack | Drag the header. |
1411	| Select every clip on it | <kbd>⌥</kbd>-click the header. |
1412	| Open its menu | Right-click or <kbd>⌃</kbd>-click the header. |
1413	
1414	A [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/) also carries a tag in its header.
1415	
1416	## With an agent
1417	
1418	`set_track` changes a track's name, its four switches, its matte and its mix in one call, and anything it leaves out keeps its value. A compressor or limiter it sets replaces that whole setting, and only the timeline's tracks have them, so it can't set either on a track inside a nest. See [Tools: tracks, markers and canvas](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/#set_track).
1419

1428	---
1429	title: "Zoom and scroll the timeline"
1430	description: "Zoom the timeline out to see a whole project or in to single frames, and scroll along it."
1431	---
1432	
1433	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
1434	
1435	Zoom the timeline out to see a whole project at once, or in to place a cut on a single frame. Everything on this page changes the timeline only. To zoom the picture, see [Zoom and pan the preview](/canvas/zoom-and-pan/).
1436	
1437	<AtAGlance
1438	  menu="View ▸ Fit Timeline"
1439	  keys="⇧Z"
1440	  where={['The zoom controls at the right of the timeline bar', 'Pinch, or ⌥ or ⌘ and scroll, over the timeline']}
1441	/>
1442	
1443	## Zoom about the pointer
1444	
1445	Put the pointer on the part of the timeline you care about, then either:
1446	
1447	- pinch on a trackpad, or
1448	- hold <kbd>⌥</kbd> or <kbd>⌘</kbd> and scroll.
1449	
1450	The time under the pointer stays where it is while everything else spreads out or closes in around it, which makes this the best way to get close to one cut.
1451	
1452	## Use the zoom slider
1453	
1454	Drag the **Timeline Zoom** slider in the timeline bar. It zooms about the middle of the view, and it covers the whole zoom range on a log scale, so the same travel always changes the zoom by the same ratio.
1455	
1456	## Step with the zoom buttons
1457	
1458	The **Zoom Out** (−) and **Zoom In** (+) buttons sit either side of the slider. Each click moves the zoom by 5 % of the slider's travel, which is about 1.6 times, and keeps the middle of the view in place. Twenty clicks cross the whole range.
1459	
1460	## Fit the whole project
1461	
1462	Press <kbd>⇧Z</kbd>, click **Fit Timeline** (the double-arrow button after the + button), or choose **View ▸ Fit Timeline**. The whole project fits across the timeline pane and the view scrolls to the start.
1463	
1464	The menu item shows no key, because <kbd>⇧Z</kbd> is one of the keys the editor handles itself. This is the only timeline zoom with a menu item or a key.
1465	
1466	A project under 1 second long fits as if it were 1 second. With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, Fit Timeline fits the nest.
1467	
1468	:::note
1469	**View ▸ Zoom In**, **Zoom Out** and **Zoom to Fit** zoom the preview, not the timeline.
1470	:::
1471	
1472	## How far it zooms
1473	
1474	A window opens with each second of the timeline 42 points wide on screen, not fitted to the project, so press <kbd>⇧Z</kbd> to see all of a long project. A point is the unit macOS measures the screen in.
1475	
1476	The zoom runs from 0.35 points per second, where an hour is 1,260 points wide, to 4,000 points per second, where one frame of a 30 fps project is about 133 points wide. It stops at either limit.
1477	
1478	The zoom isn't saved. Every window opens at 42 points per second again, and an agent has no tool to set it.
1479	
1480	## Scroll the timeline
1481	
1482	Scroll, or swipe with two fingers, over the timeline. The track headers stay at the left and the ruler stays at the top while the lanes move.
1483	
1484	The timeline keeps 260 points of empty room past the last clip, so you can reach the end and drag a clip beyond it.
1485	
1486	The view also moves by itself to keep the playhead in sight. See [The ruler and playhead](/timeline/ruler-and-playhead/).

1	=== mcp/tools-move-and-trim
2	---
3	title: "Tools: moving and trimming"
4	description: The agent tools that move clips, trim their edges, slip their source, roll a cut and switch a clip's picture or sound, with every argument and refusal.
5	---
6	
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	These tools change where a clip sits and what it shows. They name clips by id, so read them from `get_project` first.
10	
11	<AtAGlance tools={['move_clip', 'trim_start', 'trim_end', 'slip', 'roll', 'set_enabled']} />
12	
13	## What the tools share
14	
15	Each one is one undo step. It answers `ok: true` and the `project` summary. See [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/).
16	
17	**Held to the limits.** Most of these hold a time to what the clip's source allows and do as much as they can. Read the clip back to see where it landed. When the limits leave nothing to do, the answer says "*Step* made no change", and no undo step is made.
18	
19	**Times** are ticks, 600,000 per second, rounded to the project's frame grid. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/).
20	
21	**`project`** is the path of an open project as `get_project` reports it. Without it the call goes to the frontmost project.
22	
23	**`scope`** is a nest id. With it, the call's ids and times are looked up inside that nest. Without it, the call goes wherever the app is looking. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/).
24	
25	**Linked pairs.** After [`detach_audio`](/mcp/tools-copy-and-nest/), a picture and its sound move together. The partner comes along only when it's on an unlocked track. A lock on a named clip's own track doesn't stop these tools.
26	
27	**A boolean** may also be sent as `"true"`, `"1"`, `"false"` or `"0"`.
28	
29	## `move_clip`
30	
31	Shifts clips along the timeline, and optionally onto another track, as [dragging a clip](/editing/move-clips/) does.
32	
33	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
34	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
35	| `clips` | array of integers | Yes | The clip ids. At least one. |
36	| `delta` | integer | Yes | How far to shift, in ticks. Negative moves earlier. |
37	| `track` | integer | No | The destination track for the first clip. The first clip is the one on the back-most track, then the earliest. Leave it out to stay on the current tracks. |
38	| `scope` | integer | No | The nest the clips are in. |
39	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. |
40	
41	Several clips keep their relative track offsets, so a selection spanning two tracks lands two tracks apart.
42	
43	Starts stop at 0. It's the earliest clip that stops there, linked partners included, and the rest keep their distance from it.
44	
45	A linked pair moves together in time, but only the clips you name change track. So you can drop a sound half onto a track of its own while its picture stays.
46	
47	It's refused:
48	
49	- when the destination breaks the overlap rule: a clip may overlap at most one neighbour on each side, and each overlap may be at most half of the shorter clip
50	- when a clip would land off either end of the track list
51	
52	A clip that gains an overlap with the clip before it, and has no transition, gains a `cross_dissolve`. The undo step is called "Move Clip".
53	
54	## `trim_start`
55	
56	Moves a clip's start, as [dragging its left edge](/editing/trimming/) or pressing <kbd>W</kbd> does. The content stays in place: the source's in point advances by the same amount, so nothing after the new start shifts.
57	
58	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
59	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
60	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip id. |
61	| `to` | integer | Yes | The new start, in ticks. |
62	| `alone` | boolean | No | `true` moves this clip's edge without its linked partner's, which makes a [J-cut or L-cut](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/). The timeline does this for a dragged sound. Default `false`. |
63	| `scope` | integer | No | The nest the clip is in. |
64	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. |
65	
66	It stops at the source's own beginning and one frame short of the clip's end, because a clip is at least one frame long.
67	
68	On a linked pair, the other half's start follows when it was the same as this clip's.
69	
70	Timed words stay on the speech they time, and a graphic's own clock moves with the edge. Actions stay where they are in the clip. See [What a trim keeps](/editing/trimming/#what-a-trim-keeps).
71	
72	On a clip with a [speed ramp](/speed/edit-a-ramped-clip/), the ramp stays where it is in the clip, so what plays after the new start can change. The start is held where the clip still fits its media.
73	
74	It's refused when the new start would break the [overlap rule](#move_clip). The undo step is called "Trim Start".
75	
76	## `trim_end`
77	
78	Moves a clip's end, as [dragging its right edge](/editing/trimming/) or pressing <kbd>E</kbd> does.
79	
80	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
81	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
82	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip id. |
83	| `to` | integer | Yes | The new end, in ticks. |
84	| `alone` | boolean | No | `true` moves this clip's edge without its linked partner's, which makes a [J-cut or L-cut](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/). Default `false`. |
85	| `scope` | integer | No | The nest the clip is in. |
86	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. |
87	
88	It stops at the last frame the source has left after the in point, and one frame after the clip's start.
89	
90	On a linked pair, the other half's end follows when it was the same as this clip's.
91	
92	It's refused when the new end would break the [overlap rule](#move_clip). The undo step is called "Trim End".
93	
94	## `slip`
95	
96	Slides the source under a fixed clip, as [<kbd>⌥⇧</kbd>-dragging a clip's body](/editing/slip-and-roll/#slip-a-clip) does. What the clip shows changes, and where it sits doesn't, so nothing downstream moves.
97	
98	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
99	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
100	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip id. |
101	| `delta` | integer | Yes | How far to slide the source, in timeline ticks. The source moves by `delta` times the clip's speed. Positive shows later material. |
102	| `scope` | integer | No | The nest the clip is in. |
103	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. |
104	
105	The slide stops so the window stays inside the media. A [freeze clip](/speed/freeze-frame/) moves the frame it holds instead, and stops one frame short of the file's end.
106	
107	A linked partner on an unlocked track slips too, by whichever of the two can move less, so the sound stays on its picture. Actions don't move.
108	
109	Only a clip of a media file or a freeze clip can slip. Any other, such as a text clip, is an error. The undo step is called "Slip".
110	
111	## `roll`
112	
113	Moves a hard cut between two clips, as [<kbd>⌥⇧</kbd>-dragging a clip's edge](/editing/slip-and-roll/#roll-a-cut) does. This clip's start and the end of the clip before it both become `to`. One grows by exactly what the other loses, and the pair's outer edges and total length don't move.
114	
115	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
116	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
117	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip to the right of the cut. |
118	| `to` | integer | Yes | Where the cut moves to, in ticks. |
119	| `alone` | boolean | No | `true` moves this cut without rolling the linked partner's. Default `false`. |
120	| `scope` | integer | No | The nest the clip is in. |
121	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. |
122	
123	The clip before is the one on the same track that ends exactly at this clip's start.
124	
125	The cut stops so each clip keeps a frame and neither asks for source it doesn't have. On a [speed ramp](/speed/edit-a-ramped-clip/) it's held where the clip still fits its media.
126	
127	The linked half of a pair rolls its own cut too, when it starts at the same time and has a hard cut of its own there.
128	
129	It's refused when no clip on the track ends where this one begins, with "no clip on track … ends where clip … begins". That covers a gap and an overlap. An overlap is a transition, so use [`set_transition_duration`](/mcp/tools-transitions/) to change its length. The undo step is called "Roll".
130	
131	## `set_enabled`
132	
133	Turns one clip's picture or sound on or off, the two halves [**Clip ▸ Detach Audio**](/editing/enable-picture-and-sound/) flips. A half that's off adds nothing to the picture or the mix, and the clip stays where it is.
134	
135	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
136	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
137	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip id. |
138	| `video` | boolean | No | Show this clip's picture. Left out, it stays as it is. |
139	| `audio` | boolean | No | Play this clip's sound. Left out, it stays as it is. |
140	| `scope` | integer | No | The nest the clip is in. |
141	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. |
142	
143	It's refused when neither `video` nor `audio` is given. A value the clip already has changes nothing. The undo step is called "Clip Enabled".
144

152	=== mcp/tools-cut-and-delete
153	---
154	title: "Tools: cutting and deleting"
155	description: "The agent tools that split clips, remove clips or stretches of time, and open or close gaps, with their arguments, answers and limits."
156	---
157	
158	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
159	
160	These tools cut the timeline: they split clips, remove clips or stretches of time, and open or close gaps.
161	
162	<AtAGlance
163	  tools={['split', 'split_at_shots', 'delete', 'ripple_delete', 'ripple_delete_range', 'ripple_delete_ranges', 'lift_range', 'insert_time', 'close_gap']}
164	/>
165	
166	## Pick a tool
167	
168	| You want to | Use |
169	| --- | --- |
170	| Cut clips in two at one time | [`split`](#split) |
171	| Cut clips at every shot change inside them | [`split_at_shots`](#split_at_shots) |
172	| Remove clips and leave the gaps | [`delete`](#delete) |
173	| Remove clips and close the gaps | [`ripple_delete`](#ripple_delete) |
174	| Remove a stretch of time and close it | [`ripple_delete_range`](#ripple_delete_range) |
175	| Remove many stretches as one undo step | [`ripple_delete_ranges`](#ripple_delete_ranges) |
176	| Remove a stretch of time and leave the hole | [`lift_range`](#lift_range) |
177	| Open empty time | [`insert_time`](#insert_time) |
178	| Close one gap on a track | [`close_gap`](#close_gap) |
179	
180	## What these tools share
181	
182	- **Times** are in ticks, 600,000 to the second, and are rounded to the project's frame grid before anything happens. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/).
183	- **One call is one undo step**, however many clips it touches.
184	- **The answer** is `ok: true`, the ids of anything created, such as `new_clips`, and a `project` summary. A call that changes nothing says so and leaves no undo step. See [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/).
185	- **Locked tracks** never move, and a stretch of time removed from the timeline leaves them alone. Lock a track to keep it out of a timeline-wide edit.
186	- **Markers** stay at their times under every ripple. Of the tools on this page, only `insert_time` moves them.
187	- **Linked clips.** A clip and its [detached sound](/audio/detach-and-attach/) stay together, as each tool below says. A partner on a locked track is never pulled in.
188	
189	## `split`
190	
191	Cuts clips in two at one time. The second piece plays on from where the first stopped, so the join can't be seen.
192	
193	It mirrors **Clip ▸ Split** (<kbd>⌘T</kbd>). See [Split clips](/editing/splitting/).
194	
195	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
196	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
197	| `at` | integer, ticks | No | Where to cut. Left out, the playhead. |
198	| `clips` | array of integers | No | The clips to cut, at least one. Left out, every clip on an unlocked track that `at` falls inside, as the menu item does with nothing selected. |
199	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by the path `get_project` reports. Left out, the frontmost. |
200	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside it. Left out, whatever is open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
201	
202	Each piece keeps the actions on its side, and an action that crosses the cut becomes two. The first piece keeps the clip's id and any transition into it. A clip you name on a locked track is still cut. Its linked partner is cut too when the partner is on an unlocked track and `at` falls inside it, and the new halves are linked to each other.
203	
204	**Answers** `new_clips`, the second pieces.
205	
206	**Changes nothing** for a named clip `at` isn't strictly inside, which is skipped. If no clip can be cut, the answer is "Split made no change". An unknown clip id is an error.
207	
208	## `split_at_shots`
209	
210	Cuts clips of a video file at every hard cut inside the part of the file they play, as one undo step named Split at Shot Changes. It shows no sheet.
211	
212	It mirrors **Clip ▸ Split at Shot Changes**. See [Split at Shot Changes](/editing/split-at-shot-changes/), which says what counts as a hard cut.
213	
214	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
215	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
216	| `clips` | array of integers | No | The clips to split. An empty list is an error. Left out, every clip of a video file on an unlocked track in what's open. |
217	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by the path `get_project` reports. Left out, the frontmost. |
218	
219	It has no `scope` argument. It works in the nest [`set_scope`](/mcp/tools-view-state/) has open, or on the timeline.
220	
221	A clip it can cut is a clip of a video file with its picture on. Any other clip you name is reported under `skipped`. A clip you name on a locked track is still cut, and its linked partner is cut too when the partner is on an unlocked track.
222	
223	The cuts are found on your Mac, with no key and no upload, and they're kept in the project's cache, so a second call doesn't have to look for them again. Each cut is worked out through the clip's speed, ramp and reversal, and lands on the frame grid. A cut within one frame of either end of the clip isn't made. To read the cuts without splitting, use [`get_media_analysis`](/mcp/tools-analysis/).
224	
225	**Answers:**
226	
227	| Key | What it holds |
228	| --- | --- |
229	| `cuts` | One `{clip, at}` for each clip that was cut, `at` being a list of timeline ticks. |
230	| `added` | How many clips the splits made, linked partners included. |
231	| `skipped` | The ids of named clips it couldn't cut. |
232	| `cached` | True when nothing had to be read first. |
233	| `new_clips` | The new clips' ids. The original id keeps the first piece. |
234	
235	With no cut inside any clip, `added` is 0, a `note` says so, and there's no undo step.
236	
237	**Won't run** in these cases, and nothing is split:
238	
239	- No clip qualifies. The message says none of the clips shows a moving picture.
240	- The splits would pass 4,096 clips. The message gives how many it would add, counting linked partners, and how many fit.
241	- The analysis takes longer than 60 s. What was covered is kept, so call again to carry on.
242	- The analysis failed, was stopped, or the file can't be read.
243	- The project or the open nest changed during the wait. Call again.
244	
245	## `delete`
246	
247	Removes clips and leaves the gaps. Nothing else moves.
248	
249	It mirrors <kbd>⌫</kbd> and **Edit ▸ Delete** with clips selected. See [Delete, Ripple Delete and Lift](/editing/delete-clips/#delete-clips-and-leave-a-gap).
250	
251	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
252	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
253	| `clips` | array of integers | Yes | The clips to remove, at least one. |
254	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by the path `get_project` reports. Left out, the frontmost. |
255	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside it. Left out, whatever is open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
256	
257	A clip you name on a locked track is still removed. A picture takes its linked sound with it, unless the sound's track is locked. A linked sound named alone goes alone, and the picture stays, silent.
258	
259	**Answers** the usual `ok` and `project`. An unknown clip id or an empty list is an error.
260	
261	## `ripple_delete`
262	
263	Removes clips and closes each hole: everything that starts after a removed clip's span, on every unlocked track, slides left by that span's length.
264	
265	It mirrors <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> and **Edit ▸ Ripple Delete** with clips selected. See [Ripple delete clips](/editing/delete-clips/#ripple-delete-clips).
266	
267	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
268	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
269	| `clips` | array of integers | Yes | The clips to remove, at least one. |
270	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by the path `get_project` reports. Left out, the frontmost. |
271	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside it. Left out, whatever is open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
272	
273	A clip you name on a locked track is still removed, but clips on locked tracks don't move. Each clip's linked partner on an unlocked track goes too, whichever half you name. A clip on another track that crosses a removed span stays where it is, and two removed clips that touch leave one hole. A clip that slides onto a neighbour gets a Cross Dissolve over the overlap. See [How a ripple closes holes](/editing/delete-clips/#how-a-ripple-closes-holes).
274	
275	**Won't run** when the shift would push a linked clip before the start of the timeline, as a sound leading its picture in a [J-cut](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/) can. The message names both clips, and nothing moves. An unknown clip id or an empty list is an error.
276	
277	## `ripple_delete_range`
278	
279	Cuts one stretch of time out of the timeline and closes it. Every clip on an unlocked track is cut at both ends of the range, what's between is removed, and the rest slides left by the range's length.
280	
281	It mirrors <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> with an [in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/) set and nothing selected. See [Ripple delete a range](/editing/delete-clips/#ripple-delete-a-range).
282	
283	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
284	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
285	| `from` | integer, ticks | Yes | Where the range starts. |
286	| `to` | integer, ticks | Yes | Where the range ends. It must be after `from` once both are on the frame grid. |
287	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by the path `get_project` reports. Left out, the frontmost. |
288	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside it. Left out, whatever is open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
289	
290	Clips on locked tracks are neither cut, removed nor moved, even inside the range. A clip that slides onto a neighbour gets a Cross Dissolve.
291	
292	**Answers** `new_clips`, the piece left after the range of any clip cut at `to`. That piece has a new id.
293	
294	**Won't run** when `to` isn't after `from`, which is an error, or when the shift would push a linked clip before the start of the timeline. The undo step is named Ripple Delete.
295	
296	## `ripple_delete_ranges`
297	
298	Cuts several stretches of time out of the timeline as one edit and one undo step, named Ripple Delete, however many ranges there are.
299	
300	[Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) and [Remove Filler Words](/cleanup/remove-filler-words/) make this cut from their sheets. See [Ripple delete several ranges](/editing/delete-clips/#ripple-delete-several-ranges).
301	
302	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
303	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
304	| `ranges` | array of `[from, to]` pairs of ticks | Yes | The stretches to cut, at least one. A single pair may be written flat, as `[from, to]`. |
305	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by the path `get_project` reports. Left out, the frontmost. |
306	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside it. Left out, whatever is open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
307	
308	`detect_silence` and `detect_fillers` return ranges in this shape. A `cut_start` and `cut_end` from `get_timeline_transcript` make a pair too, so a run of words is one range from its first word's `cut_start` to its last word's `cut_end`. See [Tools: clean-up](/mcp/tools-clean-up/).
309	
310	Each pair is rounded to the frame grid and put in order, so a reversed pair is the same range. Pairs that touch or overlap then merge, and what's left is cut from right to left, each cut as `ripple_delete_range` makes it. So every time you send is a time in the project as you read it, and this isn't the same as calling `ripple_delete_range` once per pair: two ranges that meet make one shift, not two.
311	
312	**Answers** `new_clips`, the pieces left after each range of any clip cut at a range's end.
313	
314	**Won't run** when `ranges` is empty, which is an error, or when a shift would push a linked clip before the start of the timeline. A list whose pairs are all empty changes nothing. Each cut can add a clip, so a list that would pass 4,096 clips is an error and nothing is cut.
315	
316	## `lift_range`
317	
318	Cuts a stretch of time out and leaves the hole. Every clip on an unlocked track is cut at both ends of the range and what's between is removed, and nothing moves. Use it when a mix or a caption track is already timed.
319	
320	It mirrors <kbd>⌫</kbd> with an [in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/) set and nothing selected. See [Lift a range](/editing/delete-clips/#lift-a-range).
321	
322	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
323	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
324	| `from` | integer, ticks | Yes | Where the range starts. |
325	| `to` | integer, ticks | Yes | Where the range ends. It must be after `from` once both are on the frame grid. |
326	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by the path `get_project` reports. Left out, the frontmost. |
327	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside it. Left out, whatever is open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
328	
329	Clips on locked tracks are neither cut nor removed. To close the hole as well, use [`ripple_delete_range`](#ripple_delete_range).
330	
331	**Answers** `new_clips`, the piece left after the range of any clip cut at `to`. The undo step is named Lift.
332	
333	**Won't run** when `to` isn't after `from`, which is an error. A range with nothing an unlocked track can give up changes nothing.
334	
335	## `insert_time`
336	
337	Opens empty time: every clip on an unlocked track that starts at or after a point moves later, and so does every marker at or after that point.
338	
339	It has no menu item or gesture of its own. See [Insert time](/editing/close-gaps/#insert-time).
340	
341	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
342	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
343	| `at` | integer, ticks | Yes | Where the gap opens. |
344	| `length` | integer, ticks | Yes | How much room to open. It must come to at least one frame. |
345	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by the path `get_project` reports. Left out, the frontmost. |
346	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside it. Left out, whatever is open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
347	
348	Clips that cross `at` stay in place, so nothing is cut. To open a gap inside a clip, call [`split`](#split) first. A moved clip's linked partner on an unlocked track moves with it. No marker can land on another, because they all move by the same length.
349	
350	**Answers** the usual `ok` and `project`. The undo step is named Insert Time.
351	
352	**Won't run** when `length` is zero or negative once it's on the frame grid, which is an error.
353	
354	## `close_gap`
355	
356	Closes the empty stretch on a track that contains a time. Everything from the far side of the gap, on every unlocked track, slides left by the gap's length.
357	
358	It mirrors double-clicking a gap in a lane, and **Clip ▸ Close Gap**. See [Close gaps and insert time](/editing/close-gaps/).
359	
360	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
361	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
362	| `track` | integer | Yes | The track the gap is on. |
363	| `at` | integer, ticks | Yes | A time inside the gap. |
364	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by the path `get_project` reports. Left out, the frontmost. |
365	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside it. Left out, whatever is open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
366	
367	The gap runs between the nearest clip edges on that track, or from the start of the timeline when no clip comes before it. A gap closes fully or not at all, so a smaller gap never means it stopped part-way.
368	
369	**Answers** the usual `ok` and `project`. A clip that slides onto a neighbour by an amount the [overlap rule](/getting-started/refused-edits/) allows gets a Cross Dissolve.
370	
371	**Won't run** in these cases. Each message names what's in the way, and nothing moves:
372	
373	- `at` is on a clip, so it isn't in a gap.
374	- No clip on the track starts after `at`.
375	- The track is locked. Its own clips are the ones that would stay behind.
376	- The shift would break the overlap rule on a track it moves.
377	- The shift would push a linked clip before the start of the timeline.
378	
379	An unknown track is an error.
380

389	=== mcp/tools-copy-and-nest
390	---
391	title: "Tools: copying and nesting"
392	description: "The agent tools that duplicate and paste clips, copy one clip's look onto others, and group clips into a nest, with their arguments, answers and limits."
393	---
394	
395	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
396	
397	These tools make more of what's already on the timeline. They copy clips, copy one clip's settings onto others, and group clips into one clip or take that group apart.
398	
399	<AtAGlance tools={['duplicate', 'paste', 'paste_attributes', 'nest', 'unnest']} />
400	
401	## Pick a tool
402	
403	| You want to | Use |
404	| --- | --- |
405	| Copy clips to straight after the originals | [`duplicate`](#duplicate) |
406	| Place clips from a payload at a time, in this project or another | [`paste`](#paste) |
407	| Copy one clip's settings onto other clips | [`paste_attributes`](#paste_attributes) |
408	| Group clips into one clip | [`nest`](#nest) |
409	| Take a group apart again | [`unnest`](#unnest) |
410	
411	## What these tools share
412	
413	- **Times** are in ticks, 600,000 to the second, and are rounded to the project's frame grid. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/).
414	- **One call is one undo step**, however many clips it touches.
415	- **The answer** is `ok: true`, the ids of anything created, such as `new_clips`, and a `project` summary. A call that changes nothing says so and leaves no undo step. See [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/).
416	
417	## The payload
418	
419	`paste` and `paste_attributes` both take a `payload`, an object in the form **Edit ▸ Copy** puts on the clipboard. No tool reads the clipboard, so an agent builds its own from what `get_project` lists:
420	
421	```json
422	{
423	  "clips": [],
424	  "media": [],
425	  "nests": []
426	}
427	```
428	
429	| Key | Required | What it holds |
430	| --- | --- | --- |
431	| `clips` | Yes, at least one | Clip objects as `get_project` lists them, each with its `track` changed as below. |
432	| `media` | When a clip uses a file | The media rows those clips use, as `get_project` lists them. |
433	| `nests` | When a clip shows a nest | The nests those clips show, and any nest inside them, as `get_project` lists them. |
434	
435	Two things differ from what `get_project` gives you:
436	
437	- **A clip's `track` is a depth, not a track id.** 0 is the front-most lane, 1 the lane behind it, and so on, because a track id means nothing in another project.
438	- **Ids are only used inside the payload**, to tie clips to their media and nests. Everything that lands gets a fresh id, so a payload can be pasted again and again, into any project.
439	
440	Keys Frame Job doesn't know are ignored. A payload that isn't an object, or has no clips, is an error.
441	
442	## `duplicate`
443	
444	Copies clips onto their own tracks, placed straight after the span the originals cover, so a selection keeps its internal timing.
445	
446	It mirrors **Edit ▸ Duplicate** (<kbd>⌘D</kbd>). See [Duplicate clips](/editing/duplicate-clips/).
447	
448	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
449	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
450	| `clips` | array of integers | Yes | The clips to copy, at least one. |
451	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by the path `get_project` reports. Left out, the frontmost. |
452	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside it. Left out, whatever is open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
453	
454	Follow it with [`move_clip`](/mcp/tools-move-and-trim/#move_clip) to put the copies anywhere else. A clip's linked partner on an unlocked track is copied too, and the two copies are linked to each other. A copy of a nest clip shows the same nest as the original. See [Shared and independent nest copies](/editing/nest-copies/).
455	
456	**Answers** `new_clips`, the copies.
457	
458	**Won't run** when a copy would break the [overlap rule](/getting-started/refused-edits/) on its track. Later clips aren't pushed out of the way. An overlap the rule allows gets a Cross Dissolve. An unknown clip id or an empty list is an error.
459	
460	## `paste`
461	
462	Places a [payload](#the-payload)'s clips on the timeline. The earliest clip lands exactly at `at`, and the others keep their distance from it, so a copied arrangement pastes back intact.
463	
464	It mirrors **Edit ▸ Paste** (<kbd>⌘V</kbd>), without touching the clipboard. See [Copy, cut and paste](/editing/copy-and-paste/).
465	
466	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
467	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
468	| `payload` | object | Yes | The clips to place. See [The payload](#the-payload). |
469	| `at` | integer, ticks | No | Where the earliest clip lands. Left out, the playhead. |
470	| `track` | integer | No | The track id where depth 0 lands, and the other depths follow behind it. Left out, the front-most track. |
471	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by the path `get_project` reports. Left out, the frontmost. |
472	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside it. Left out, whatever is open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
473	
474	What Frame Job does to make the clips fit:
475	
476	- **Media** is matched to this project by path. A row the project already has is reused, and one it lacks is added. Only files the pasted clips use come across.
477	- **Nests** are always copied, never matched, so editing one copy afterwards leaves the other alone. Copy itself writes no `nests` key, so a nest clip on the clipboard can't be pasted, but a payload that carries the nest can.
478	- **Times** are rounded to this project's frame grid.
479	- **Missing tracks** are added at the back.
480	- **No room:** a clip that would break the overlap rule on its track goes on a new track in front instead of being dropped. A smaller overlap the rule allows gets a Cross Dissolve.
481	- **Links:** a linked pair in the payload lands as a linked pair. A clip whose partner isn't in the payload loses its link.
482	
483	**Answers** `new_clips`, and `new_tracks` and `new_media` when any were added.
484	
485	**Won't run** in these cases, and a paste lands whole or not at all:
486	
487	- The payload isn't an object, has no clips, or holds a clip that isn't in the form `get_project` lists.
488	- A clip uses a file or shows a nest the payload doesn't carry, or a media row has an empty path.
489	- A value is out of range. The message names the clip by its id in the payload.
490	- `track` doesn't exist in this project.
491	- A clip's depth is past the 64-track limit, or the paste would pass 64 tracks or 4,096 clips.
492	- It would put an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) inside a nest.
493	
494	## `paste_attributes`
495	
496	Copies one clip's settings onto other clips. It reads only the payload's earliest clip: the one with the earliest start, then the front-most, then the lower id. Never assume that's the first clip in the array.
497	
498	It mirrors **Edit ▸ Paste Attributes** (<kbd>⌥⌘V</kbd>) and, with `groups` set to `["graphic"]` and `skip_missing` on, **Edit ▸ Paste Graphic Properties**. See [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/).
499	
500	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
501	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
502	| `clips` | array of integers | Yes | The clips to change, at least one. |
503	| `payload` | object | Yes | Holds the clip to copy from. See [The payload](#the-payload). |
504	| `groups` | array of strings | No | Which groups travel: `video`, `audio`, `text`, `shape`, `graphic`. Left out, each of the first four that both clips have, and never `graphic`. An empty list is an error. |
505	| `skip_missing` | boolean | No | Only with `groups`. On, a group the payload's clip lacks is dropped, and a clip that can't take a group is skipped for it. Default off. |
506	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by the path `get_project` reports. Left out, the frontmost. |
507	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside it. Left out, whatever is open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
508	
509	Each group replaces the target's whole group, and nothing is merged:
510	
511	| Group | What travels | What the target keeps |
512	| --- | --- | --- |
513	| `video` | Every picture setting, position and scale included. | An adjustment clip keeps its own [qualifier](/color/qualifiers/) when the copied clip isn't an adjustment clip. A picture clip takes no qualifier. |
514	| `audio` | Every sound setting, mute and keep pitch included. | Nothing. |
515	| `text` | Every text setting. | Its words and their timings. |
516	| `shape` | Every shape setting. | Its kind, width, height, and `from` and `to` points. |
517	| `graphic` | The graphic's properties, whole, onto clips drawn by the same graphic. | Its name, size, in point and length, and any property an action on that clip animates that the copied clip lacks. |
518	
519	Speed, whether the picture and sound are on, actions, the transition, the clip's name and its label never travel. A [look](/color/luts/) brings its `.cube` file by path when the payload's `media` carries it, and a look whose file isn't there comes across as no look.
520	
521	**Answers** the usual `ok` and `project`, and `new_media` when a look's `.cube` file was added.
522	
523	**Won't run** in these cases, and no clip changes:
524	
525	- `groups` is empty or names something else.
526	- Without `skip_missing`, a named group is one the copied clip lacks, or a target lacks. The message names the group or the clip.
527	- Without `skip_missing`, `graphic` meets a clip drawn by another graphic. The message names both.
528	- A copied value is one the inspector wouldn't accept on that clip. See [When a paste stops](/editing/paste-attributes/#when-a-paste-stops).
529	
530	When the paste would leave every clip as it was, the answer is "Paste Attributes made no change".
531	
532	## `nest`
533	
534	Collapses clips into one clip that stands for the group. From then on the group moves, trims, fades and transforms as one thing.
535	
536	It mirrors **Clip ▸ Nest** (<kbd>⌘G</kbd>). See [Nests](/editing/nests/).
537	
538	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
539	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
540	| `clips` | array of integers | Yes | The clips to group, at least one. |
541	| `name` | string | No | What to call the group. Left out or blank, `Nest <n>`. |
542	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by the path `get_project` reports. Left out, the frontmost. |
543	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside it. Left out, whatever is open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
544	
545	The clips move whole, keeping their ids, settings, actions, transitions, relative times and stacking, with the earliest starting at 0 inside the nest. A linked partner on an unlocked track goes in with its clip. The nest clip lands on the front-most track the clips were on, and runs from the earliest start to the latest end. If those tracks include a [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/), it lands on the front-most track that isn't one, or the front-most track when all of them are.
546	
547	The nest's canvas is fixed at the project's current size, so a later [`set_canvas`](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/#set_canvas) can't re-lay out what's inside.
548	
549	**Answers** `new_clips`, which is the nest clip, and `new_tracks`, the nest's own tracks. `get_project` lists the group under `nests`, and the nest clip's `source.project` gives its id, which is what `scope` takes.
550	
551	**Won't run** when:
552	
553	- The clips include an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/), which can't go inside a nest.
554	- The nest clip would overlap something unselected by more than the [overlap rule](/getting-started/refused-edits/) allows. An overlap the rule allows gets a Cross Dissolve.
555	- It would pass 64 tracks, counting the nest's own, or eight levels of nesting.
556	
557	`clips` holding only a clip that's already a nest changes nothing. An empty list or an unknown clip id is an error.
558	
559	## `unnest`
560	
561	Opens a nest clip: its contents return to the timeline and the nest clip goes.
562	
563	It mirrors **Clip ▸ Un-nest** (<kbd>⇧⌘G</kbd>). See [Un-nest](/editing/nests/#un-nest).
564	
565	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
566	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
567	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The nest clip to open. |
568	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by the path `get_project` reports. Left out, the frontmost. |
569	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside it. Left out, whatever is open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
570	
571	It's the inverse of `nest`, apart from the ids, which are all fresh. Clips land at the nest clip's start plus their own, on tracks counted back from the nest clip's own, and missing tracks are added behind it. A clip the overlap rule won't allow goes on a new track in front instead of being dropped.
572	
573	A nest clip trimmed shorter than its contents gives all of them back, because trimming a nest hides what's inside and doesn't cut it. When another clip still shows the same nest, the nest stays for that clip.
574	
575	**Answers** `new_clips`, the returned clips, and `new_tracks` when any were added.
576	
577	**Won't run** on a clip that isn't a nest, which is an error.
578	
579	## Related
