389	=== mcp/tools-copy-and-nest
390	---
391	title: "Tools: copying and nesting"
392	description: "The agent tools that duplicate and paste clips, copy one clip's look onto others, and group clips into a nest, with their arguments, answers and limits."
393	---
394	
395	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
396	
397	These tools make more of what's already on the timeline. They copy clips, copy one clip's settings onto others, and group clips into one clip or take that group apart.
398	
399	<AtAGlance tools={['duplicate', 'paste', 'paste_attributes', 'nest', 'unnest']} />
400	
401	## Pick a tool
402	
403	| You want to | Use |
404	| --- | --- |
405	| Copy clips to straight after the originals | [`duplicate`](#duplicate) |
406	| Place clips from a payload at a time, in this project or another | [`paste`](#paste) |
407	| Copy one clip's settings onto other clips | [`paste_attributes`](#paste_attributes) |
408	| Group clips into one clip | [`nest`](#nest) |
409	| Take a group apart again | [`unnest`](#unnest) |
410	
411	## What these tools share
412	
413	- **Times** are in ticks, 600,000 to the second, and are rounded to the project's frame grid. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/).
414	- **One call is one undo step**, however many clips it touches.
415	- **The answer** is `ok: true`, the ids of anything created, such as `new_clips`, and a `project` summary. A call that changes nothing says so and leaves no undo step. See [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/).
416	
417	## The payload
418	
419	`paste` and `paste_attributes` both take a `payload`, an object in the form **Edit ▸ Copy** puts on the clipboard. No tool reads the clipboard, so an agent builds its own from what `get_project` lists:
420	
421	```json
422	{
423	  "clips": [],
424	  "media": [],
425	  "nests": []
426	}
427	```
428	
429	| Key | Required | What it holds |
430	| --- | --- | --- |
431	| `clips` | Yes, at least one | Clip objects as `get_project` lists them, each with its `track` changed as below. |
432	| `media` | When a clip uses a file | The media rows those clips use, as `get_project` lists them. |
433	| `nests` | When a clip shows a nest | The nests those clips show, and any nest inside them, as `get_project` lists them. |
434	
435	Two things differ from what `get_project` gives you:
436	
437	- **A clip's `track` is a depth, not a track id.** 0 is the front-most lane, 1 the lane behind it, and so on, because a track id means nothing in another project.
438	- **Ids are only used inside the payload**, to tie clips to their media and nests. Everything that lands gets a fresh id, so a payload can be pasted again and again, into any project.
439	
440	Keys Frame Job doesn't know are ignored. A payload that isn't an object, or has no clips, is an error.
441	
442	## `duplicate`
443	
444	Copies clips onto their own tracks, placed straight after the span the originals cover, so a selection keeps its internal timing.
445	
446	It mirrors **Edit ▸ Duplicate** (<kbd>⌘D</kbd>). See [Duplicate clips](/editing/duplicate-clips/).
447	
448	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
449	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
450	| `clips` | array of integers | Yes | The clips to copy, at least one. |
451	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by the path `get_project` reports. Left out, the frontmost. |
452	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside it. Left out, whatever is open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
453	
454	Follow it with [`move_clip`](/mcp/tools-move-and-trim/#move_clip) to put the copies anywhere else. A clip's linked partner on an unlocked track is copied too, and the two copies are linked to each other. A copy of a nest clip shows the same nest as the original. See [Shared and independent nest copies](/editing/nest-copies/).
455	
456	**Answers** `new_clips`, the copies.
457	
458	**Won't run** when a copy would break the [overlap rule](/getting-started/refused-edits/) on its track. Later clips aren't pushed out of the way. An overlap the rule allows gets a Cross Dissolve. An unknown clip id or an empty list is an error.
459	
460	## `paste`
461	
462	Places a [payload](#the-payload)'s clips on the timeline. The earliest clip lands exactly at `at`, and the others keep their distance from it, so a copied arrangement pastes back intact.
463	
464	It mirrors **Edit ▸ Paste** (<kbd>⌘V</kbd>), without touching the clipboard. See [Copy, cut and paste](/editing/copy-and-paste/).
465	
466	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
467	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
468	| `payload` | object | Yes | The clips to place. See [The payload](#the-payload). |
469	| `at` | integer, ticks | No | Where the earliest clip lands. Left out, the playhead. |
470	| `track` | integer | No | The track id where depth 0 lands, and the other depths follow behind it. Left out, the front-most track. |
471	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by the path `get_project` reports. Left out, the frontmost. |
472	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside it. Left out, whatever is open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
473	
474	What Frame Job does to make the clips fit:
475	
476	- **Media** is matched to this project by path. A row the project already has is reused, and one it lacks is added. Only files the pasted clips use come across.
477	- **Nests** are always copied, never matched, so editing one copy afterwards leaves the other alone. Copy itself writes no `nests` key, so a nest clip on the clipboard can't be pasted, but a payload that carries the nest can.
478	- **Times** are rounded to this project's frame grid.
479	- **Missing tracks** are added at the back.
480	- **No room:** a clip that would break the overlap rule on its track goes on a new track in front instead of being dropped. A smaller overlap the rule allows gets a Cross Dissolve.
481	- **Links:** a linked pair in the payload lands as a linked pair. A clip whose partner isn't in the payload loses its link.
482	
483	**Answers** `new_clips`, and `new_tracks` and `new_media` when any were added.
484	
485	**Won't run** in these cases, and a paste lands whole or not at all:
486	
487	- The payload isn't an object, has no clips, or holds a clip that isn't in the form `get_project` lists.
488	- A clip uses a file or shows a nest the payload doesn't carry, or a media row has an empty path.
489	- A value is out of range. The message names the clip by its id in the payload.
490	- `track` doesn't exist in this project.
491	- A clip's depth is past the 64-track limit, or the paste would pass 64 tracks or 4,096 clips.
492	- It would put an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) inside a nest.
493	
494	## `paste_attributes`
495	
496	Copies one clip's settings onto other clips. It reads only the payload's earliest clip: the one with the earliest start, then the front-most, then the lower id. Never assume that's the first clip in the array.
497	
498	It mirrors **Edit ▸ Paste Attributes** (<kbd>⌥⌘V</kbd>) and, with `groups` set to `["graphic"]` and `skip_missing` on, **Edit ▸ Paste Graphic Properties**. See [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/).
499	
500	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
501	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
502	| `clips` | array of integers | Yes | The clips to change, at least one. |
503	| `payload` | object | Yes | Holds the clip to copy from. See [The payload](#the-payload). |
504	| `groups` | array of strings | No | Which groups travel: `video`, `audio`, `text`, `shape`, `graphic`. Left out, each of the first four that both clips have, and never `graphic`. An empty list is an error. |
505	| `skip_missing` | boolean | No | Only with `groups`. On, a group the payload's clip lacks is dropped, and a clip that can't take a group is skipped for it. Default off. |
506	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by the path `get_project` reports. Left out, the frontmost. |
507	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside it. Left out, whatever is open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
508	
509	Each group replaces the target's whole group, and nothing is merged:
510	
511	| Group | What travels | What the target keeps |
512	| --- | --- | --- |
513	| `video` | Every picture setting, position and scale included. | An adjustment clip keeps its own [qualifier](/color/qualifiers/) when the copied clip isn't an adjustment clip. A picture clip takes no qualifier. |
514	| `audio` | Every sound setting, mute and keep pitch included. | Nothing. |
515	| `text` | Every text setting. | Its words and their timings. |
516	| `shape` | Every shape setting. | Its kind, width, height, and `from` and `to` points. |
517	| `graphic` | The graphic's properties, whole, onto clips drawn by the same graphic. | Its name, size, in point and length, and any property an action on that clip animates that the copied clip lacks. |
518	
519	Speed, whether the picture and sound are on, actions, the transition, the clip's name and its label never travel. A [look](/color/luts/) brings its `.cube` file by path when the payload's `media` carries it, and a look whose file isn't there comes across as no look.
520	
521	**Answers** the usual `ok` and `project`, and `new_media` when a look's `.cube` file was added.
522	
523	**Won't run** in these cases, and no clip changes:
524	
525	- `groups` is empty or names something else.
526	- Without `skip_missing`, a named group is one the copied clip lacks, or a target lacks. The message names the group or the clip.
527	- Without `skip_missing`, `graphic` meets a clip drawn by another graphic. The message names both.
528	- A copied value is one the inspector wouldn't accept on that clip. See [When a paste stops](/editing/paste-attributes/#when-a-paste-stops).
529	
530	When the paste would leave every clip as it was, the answer is "Paste Attributes made no change".
531	
532	## `nest`
533	
534	Collapses clips into one clip that stands for the group. From then on the group moves, trims, fades and transforms as one thing.
535	
536	It mirrors **Clip ▸ Nest** (<kbd>⌘G</kbd>). See [Nests](/editing/nests/).
537	
538	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
539	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
540	| `clips` | array of integers | Yes | The clips to group, at least one. |
541	| `name` | string | No | What to call the group. Left out or blank, `Nest <n>`. |
542	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by the path `get_project` reports. Left out, the frontmost. |
543	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside it. Left out, whatever is open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
544	
545	The clips move whole, keeping their ids, settings, actions, transitions, relative times and stacking, with the earliest starting at 0 inside the nest. A linked partner on an unlocked track goes in with its clip. The nest clip lands on the front-most track the clips were on, and runs from the earliest start to the latest end. If those tracks include a [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/), it lands on the front-most track that isn't one, or the front-most track when all of them are.
546	
547	The nest's canvas is fixed at the project's current size, so a later [`set_canvas`](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/#set_canvas) can't re-lay out what's inside.
548	
549	**Answers** `new_clips`, which is the nest clip, and `new_tracks`, the nest's own tracks. `get_project` lists the group under `nests`, and the nest clip's `source.project` gives its id, which is what `scope` takes.
550	
551	**Won't run** when:
552	
553	- The clips include an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/), which can't go inside a nest.
554	- The nest clip would overlap something unselected by more than the [overlap rule](/getting-started/refused-edits/) allows. An overlap the rule allows gets a Cross Dissolve.
555	- It would pass 64 tracks, counting the nest's own, or eight levels of nesting.
556	
557	`clips` holding only a clip that's already a nest changes nothing. An empty list or an unknown clip id is an error.
558	
559	## `unnest`
560	
561	Opens a nest clip: its contents return to the timeline and the nest clip goes.
562	
563	It mirrors **Clip ▸ Un-nest** (<kbd>⇧⌘G</kbd>). See [Un-nest](/editing/nests/#un-nest).
564	
565	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
566	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
567	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The nest clip to open. |
568	| `project` | string | No | The open project to act on, by the path `get_project` reports. Left out, the frontmost. |
569	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside it. Left out, whatever is open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
570	
571	It's the inverse of `nest`, apart from the ids, which are all fresh. Clips land at the nest clip's start plus their own, on tracks counted back from the nest clip's own, and missing tracks are added behind it. A clip the overlap rule won't allow goes on a new track in front instead of being dropped.
572	
573	A nest clip trimmed shorter than its contents gives all of them back, because trimming a nest hides what's inside and doesn't cut it. When another clip still shows the same nest, the nest stays for that clip.
574	
575	**Answers** `new_clips`, the returned clips, and `new_tracks` when any were added.
576	
577	**Won't run** on a clip that isn't a nest, which is an error.
578	
579	## Related

583	- [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/)

587	=== mcp/tools-adding-clips
588	---
589	title: "Tools: adding clips"
590	description: The agent tools that place media, titles, shapes, adjustment clips and backgrounds on the timeline, with every argument, answer and refusal.
591	---
592	
593	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
594	
595	These tools put new clips on the timeline. Three place a media file, three make a clip with no source, and two make a backdrop on a new track of its own.
596	
597	<AtAGlance
598	  tools={['add_clip', 'insert_clip', 'overwrite_clip', 'add_text_clip', 'add_shape_clip', 'add_adjustment_clip', 'add_background', 'add_blurred_background']}
599	/>
600	
601	## What the tools share
602	
603	Each one is one undo step. It answers `ok: true`, `new_clips` (the ids it made), `new_tracks` when it made a track, and the `project` summary. See [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/).
604	
605	Times and lengths are ticks, 600,000 per second, rounded to the project's frame grid. A negative `at` is taken as 0. Colours are four numbers, `[r, g, b, a]`, each from 0 to 1. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/).
606	
607	**`project`** is the path of an open project as `get_project` reports it. Without it the call goes to the frontmost project.
608	
609	**`scope`** is a nest id. With it, the call's ids and times are looked up inside that nest. Without it, the call goes wherever the app is looking. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/).
610	
611	**The overlap rule** stops a placement that breaks it. A clip may overlap at most one neighbour on each side, and each overlap may be at most half of the shorter clip, because an overlap is a transition. A new clip that overlaps the clip before it and has no transition gets a cross dissolve.
612	
613	**A locked track** doesn't stop these tools, apart from `insert_clip`. Locks hold back gestures in the window and what a timeline-wide shift may touch.
614	
615	## `add_clip`
616	
617	Places a whole media file as one clip, as [dragging a Media-tab row onto a track](/editing/add-clips/#drag-media-onto-a-track) does.
618	
619	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
620	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
621	| `track` | integer | Yes | The track id. `get_project` lists them. |
622	| `media` | integer | Yes | The media id. `import_media` returns one. |
623	| `at` | integer | Yes | Where the clip starts on the timeline, in ticks. |
624	| `scope` | integer | No | The nest to place it in. |
625	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. |
626	
627	The clip starts at source time 0 and runs the media's whole length, rounded down to whole frames so it never outruns the file. Trim it afterwards with [`trim_start`](/mcp/tools-move-and-trim/#trim_start) and [`trim_end`](/mcp/tools-move-and-trim/#trim_end). A picture with no length of its own runs 5 seconds.
628	
629	It's given Fit scale when the project's `fit_new_clips` is on, which it is by default, and the source is bigger than the canvas.
630	
631	It's refused when it would break the overlap rule. A file shorter than a frame or with no duration can't be placed, and neither can a LUT, which is applied as a [look](/mcp/tools-set-video/). The undo step is called "Add Clip".
632	
633	## `insert_clip`
634	
635	The insert edit, as [**Edit ▸ Insert at Playhead**](/editing/insert-and-overwrite/#insert-a-file) or <kbd>⌥</kbd>-dropping a Media-tab row does. It makes room for the whole media at `at`, so nothing is covered.
636	
637	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
638	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
639	| `track` | integer | Yes | The track id. |
640	| `media` | integer | Yes | The media id. |
641	| `at` | integer | Yes | Where to insert, in ticks. |
642	| `scope` | integer | No | The nest to insert in. |
643	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. |
644	
645	In one step:
646	
647	1. The clip `at` falls inside on `track` is split.
648	2. Every unlocked track opens by the media's length. Clips starting at or after `at` move later, and so do markers at or after it.
649	3. The media lands in the hole.
650	
651	Only the destination track is cut. A clip straddling `at` on another track stays whole, which is what keeps a music bed unbroken. The exception is a cut clip's linked partner on an unlocked track, which is cut at `at` too and paired with it.
652	
653	It's refused when `track` is locked, because the room can't be made there, and when the split or the placing can't be done, with that step's own reason. A file `add_clip` can't place can't be inserted either. The undo step is called "Insert".
654	
655	## `overwrite_clip`
656	
657	The overwrite edit, as [**Edit ▸ Overwrite at Playhead**](/editing/insert-and-overwrite/#overwrite-with-a-file) or <kbd>⇧⌥</kbd>-dropping a Media-tab row does. It takes the room instead of making it.
658	
659	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
660	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
661	| `track` | integer | Yes | The track id. |
662	| `media` | integer | Yes | The media id. |
663	| `at` | integer | Yes | Where to overwrite, in ticks. |
664	| `scope` | integer | No | The nest to overwrite in. |
665	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. |
666	
667	The span the media needs is cleared on `track` alone: cut at both ends, and whatever is left inside removed. Nothing shifts, so the clips after the span and every other track stay where they are.
668	
669	The exception is a cut clip's linked partner on an unlocked track, which is cut at the same bounds and paired. The partner's middle piece stays, unlinked.
670	
671	The named track is cleared even when it's locked. It's refused when the clip can't be placed once the span is clear, and a file `add_clip` can't place can't be used here either. The undo step is called "Overwrite".
672	
673	## `add_text_clip`
674	
675	Adds a text clip, a title, as the [**Add Text**](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/#add-a-text-clip) button does. It has no source, so it can be any length. Style it afterwards with `set_text` and place it with `set_video`.
676	
677	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
678	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
679	| `track` | integer | Yes | The track id. |
680	| `at` | integer | Yes | Where it starts, in ticks. |
681	| `duration` | integer | No | Its length, in ticks. Default 5 seconds (`3000000`). |
682	| `text` | object or string | No | A plain string is the words. An object is a `set_text` patch merged over the Title preset. Default: the preset's own placeholder, "Title". |
683	| `scope` | integer | No | The nest to add it in. |
684	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. |
685	
686	A new clip is the Title preset: 72 px white Source Sans 3 Bold, centred. An object can set anything [`set_text`](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/) can, including `content`, `font`, `size`, `color`, `align`, `valign`, `outline`, `backdrop`, `width`, `animation`, `case`, `words` and `word_style`. See [Patches](/mcp/patches/).
687	
688	```json
689	{ "track": 3, "at": 1800000, "text": "Chapter one" }
690	{ "track": 3, "at": 1800000, "duration": 1200000,
691	  "text": { "content": "Chapter one", "size": 96, "align": "left" } }
692	```
693	
694	It's refused for a duration under one frame, for an unknown key or a bad value in the patch, by name, and when it would break the overlap rule. The undo step is called "Add Text".
695	
696	## `add_shape_clip`
697	
698	Adds a rectangle, ellipse, line or arrow drawn over the video, as [**Add Shape**](/text-and-shapes/shape-clips/#add-a-shape-clip) does. Like text, it has no source and can be any length. [`set_shape`](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/) changes it afterwards and `set_video` places it.
699	
700	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
701	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
702	| `track` | integer | Yes | The track id. |
703	| `at` | integer | Yes | Where it starts, in ticks. |
704	| `duration` | integer | No | Its length, in ticks. Default 5 seconds (`3000000`). |
705	| `shape` | object or string | No | A plain string is a kind: `rectangle`, `ellipse`, `line` or `arrow`. An object is a `set_shape` patch merged over the default rectangle. |
706	| `scope` | integer | No | The nest to add it in. |
707	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. |
708	
709	Leave out `shape` for the default: a 320×120 rectangle, outlined with no fill. An object can set `kind`, `width`, `height`, `stroke`, `fill`, `radius`, `arrow_start`, `arrow_end`, `from`, `to` and `gradient`.
710	
711	A rounded rectangle is a rectangle with a `radius`, not a kind of its own. An arrow is created with its head on, so pass `arrow_end: false` for a bare diagonal. A box bigger than the canvas gets Fit scale when `fit_new_clips` is on, as oversized footage does.
712	
713	It's refused for a duration under one frame, for an unknown kind, key or value, by name, and when it would break the overlap rule. The undo step is called "Add Shape".
714	
715	## `add_adjustment_clip`
716	
717	Adds an adjustment clip, as [**Insert ▸ Adjustment Clip**](/color/adjustment-clips/#insert-an-adjustment-clip) does. It has no picture of its own. While it lasts, it grades everything drawn behind it: every lower track and the canvas background, never a track in front.
718	
719	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
720	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
721	| `track` | integer | Yes | The track id. |
722	| `at` | integer | Yes | Where it starts, in ticks. |
723	| `duration` | integer | No | Its length, in ticks. Default 5 seconds (`3000000`). |
724	| `scope` | integer | No | Leave it out. Passing it is refused, because this edit has no meaning inside a nest. |
725	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. |
726	
727	Grade it with [`set_video`](/mcp/tools-set-video/): `color`, `wheels`, `curves`, `look`, `qualifier`, and the point filters (sepia, noir, vignette and invert). Its `opacity` is the grade's strength. On a track cut by a [matte](/canvas/matte-tracks/) it grades only inside the matte, and on a matte track it does nothing.
728	
729	It's refused:
730	
731	- inside a nest, whether you pass `scope` or a nest is open
732	- in any transition or overlap. Fade it with `opacity` instead.
733	
734	Later, `set_video` gives an error for blur, sharpen, pixelate or a blend mode on it. The undo step is called "Add Adjustment Clip".
735	
736	## `add_background`
737	
738	Puts a backdrop on a new back-most track, starting at 0 and running the timeline's length, as [**Clip ▸ Add Background**](/canvas/backgrounds/) does. The clip is named "Background".
739	
740	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
741	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
742	| `color` | array of four numbers | No | The plate's colour, as `[r, g, b, a]`, each from 0 to 1. White when left out. |
743	| `media` | integer | No | A media id to show instead of a colour. `import_media` adds a file. |
744	| `duration` | integer | No | Its length, in ticks. Default: the whole timeline's length, and never less than one frame. |
745	| `scope` | integer | No | The nest to add it in. |
746	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. |
747	
748	With no arguments it's a canvas-sized white rectangle, which is what the menu's **Solid Color** row sends. It's white because the canvas is already black, so a black plate would appear to do nothing. A full-canvas gradient is this clip with [`set_shape`](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/)'s `gradient` after it.
749	
750	With `media` the picture goes there at Fill scale, where `add_clip` would Fit it, because a plate that leaves the canvas showing down one side has failed. A video plate stops where its file does, whatever `duration` says. A picture runs the timeline, or for `duration` when you give one.
751	
752	It answers both `new_tracks` and `new_clips`, and the track holds the lower id.
753	
754	These are errors, and nothing is added:
755	
756	- `media` and `color` together
757	- a `duration` under one frame
758	- a file with no picture, such as a sound file
759	- a colour that isn't four numbers from 0 to 1
760	
761	The undo step is called "Add Background".
762	
763	## `add_blurred_background`
764	
765	The screencast backdrop, as [**Clip ▸ Add Blurred Background**](/canvas/backgrounds/#blurred-background) does. It copies a clip onto a new back-most track at the same start, duration, speed and source window, so the two play exactly the same frames.
766	
767	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
768	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
769	| `clip` | integer | Yes | The clip id. `get_project` lists them. |
770	| `scope` | integer | No | The nest the clip is in. |
771	| `project` | string | No | The project to act on. |
772	
773	The copy is named "Blurred Background". It's scaled to fill the canvas, centred, uncropped, blended normally and blurred at full strength.
774	
775	Its sound is off, or the mix would play one recording twice. It drops the original's ducking, because a copy keeping it would duck the whole mix, and it drops its transition, actions and label too.
776	
777	It answers both `new_tracks` and `new_clips`, and the track holds the lower id.
778	
779	These are errors, and nothing is added:
780	
781	- a nest clip, whose copy would come out sharp
782	- a source with no pixel size, such as a text clip or a sound-only clip
783	- a clip with no video properties
784	
785	The undo step is called "Add Blurred Background".

794	=== mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers
795	---
796	title: "Tools: tracks, markers and canvas"
797	description: "The agent tools that add, reorder and set up tracks, place and change markers, and change the project's canvas."
798	---
799	
800	These tools change the three things a project's clips sit in: the track stack, the markers on the ruler and the canvas. Each call that changes something is one undo step.
801	
802	Track `index` 0 is the back of the layer stack, the bottom lane of the timeline. A higher index draws in front. Ids come from [`get_project`](/mcp/get-project/), and times are ticks, 600,000 to the second. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/).
803	
804	## `add_track`
805	
806	Adds an empty track. It's **Track ▸ New Track** (<kbd>⇧⌘N</kbd>, see [New Track](/timeline/manage-tracks/#new-track)), except that an agent can choose where in the stack the track goes. The menu item always adds at the front.
807	
808	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
809	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
810	| `index` | integer | No | Where in the stack, from 0 at the back to the track count at the front. Default: the front. |
811	| `name` | string | No | The track's name, such as `Titles`. Spaces at either end are dropped. Default: `Track` and the new count, so `Track 4` when there were three. A name of only spaces counts as no name. |
812	| `scope` | integer | No | Add the track inside this nest. `index` then counts that nest's own tracks. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
813	| `project` | string | No | Path of the open project to act on. Default: the frontmost one. |
814	
815	**Answers** with `new_tracks`, holding the new track's id, and the [project summary](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/).
816	
817	**Refuses** an `index` past the front, naming the range. A project holds at most 64 tracks, and that limit counts the tracks in every nest as well as the timeline's.
818	
819	## `remove_track`
820	
821	Removes a track. It's **Track ▸ Remove Track**, see [Remove Track](/timeline/manage-tracks/#remove-track). Where the menu item asks in an alert before it removes clips, the tool never asks: it refuses until you pass `with_clips`.
822	
823	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
824	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
825	| `track` | integer | Yes | The track's id. |
826	| `with_clips` | boolean | No | Remove the track's clips too. Default: false. |
827	| `scope` | integer | No | Look the track up inside this nest. |
828	| `project` | string | No | Path of the open project to act on. Default: the frontmost one. |
829	
830	**Answers** with the project summary.
831	
832	**Refuses** two things:
833	
834	- The only track left. A project always keeps one, and `with_clips` doesn't get past this.
835	- A track that still holds clips, unless `with_clips` is true. The message names up to three of the clips, gives a count for the rest, and says to pass `with_clips: true`.
836	
837	## `move_track`
838	
839	Moves a track to a new place in the layer stack, sliding the tracks it passes the other way. It's dragging a track header, see [Reorder tracks](/timeline/manage-tracks/#reorder-tracks).
840	
841	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
842	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
843	| `track` | integer | Yes | The track's id. |
844	| `index` | integer | Yes | Its new position, from 0 at the back to one less than the track count. |
845	| `scope` | integer | No | Look the track up inside this nest. `index` then counts that nest's own tracks. |
846	| `project` | string | No | Path of the open project to act on. Default: the frontmost one. |
847	
848	**Answers** with the project summary. A track that's already at `index` answers "made no change".
849	
850	**Refuses** an `index` past the last track, naming the range.
851	
852	## `set_track`
853	
854	Changes a track's name, its four switches, its matte and its mix. Anything you leave out keeps its value.
855	
856	The switches are the track header's toggles and **Track ▸ Hide Video**, **Mute Audio**, **Lock Track** and **Solo**, see [Hide and lock tracks](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/) and [Mute and solo tracks](/audio/mute-and-solo/). `volume` and `pan` are **Track ▸ Mix…**, see [Track volume and pan](/audio/track-volume-and-pan/).
857	
858	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
859	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
860	| `track` | integer | Yes | The track's id. |
861	| `name` | string | No | The track's new name. Spaces at either end are dropped, and an empty name leaves the track unnamed. |
862	| `hidden` | boolean | No | Drops the track's picture from the composition. |
863	| `muted` | boolean | No | Silences the track's sound. |
864	| `locked` | boolean | No | Keeps every ripple, insert and range edit off the track. |
865	| `solo` | boolean | No | Silences every other track in the same container that isn't also soloed. Mute wins on a track that's both, and pictures aren't touched. |
866	| `matte` | string | No | `none`, `alpha`, `alpha_inverted`, `luma` or `luma_inverted`. See [Track mattes](#track-mattes). |
867	| `volume` | number | No | The track's fader as a linear gain from 0 to 4, multiplying every clip's own volume on it. 1 is unity, 4 is +12.04 dB and 0 is silent. |
868	| `pan` | number | No | The track's balance, from −1 (left) to 1 (right). It's a constant-power balance after each clip's own pan, and a mono source isn't panned. |
869	| `compressor` | object | No | The track's compressor, or `null` for off. See [A track's compressor and limiter](#a-tracks-compressor-and-limiter). |
870	| `limiter` | object | No | The track's limiter, or `null` for off. See [A track's compressor and limiter](#a-tracks-compressor-and-limiter). |
871	| `scope` | integer | No | Look the track up inside this nest. |
872	| `project` | string | No | Path of the open project to act on. Default: the frontmost one. |
873	
874	A container is the timeline, or one nest's own tracks. `volume` and `pan` play through nests: a nested clip is affected by its own track and by the track of every nest clip around it.
875	
876	**Answers** with the project summary. A call that sets what's already there answers "made no change".
877	
878	**Refuses** a call that names none of the optional arguments, and a `volume` or `pan` outside its range. Neither value is clamped.
879	
880	### Track mattes
881	
882	`matte` makes a track cut the track directly behind it in its container, as **Track ▸ Matte** does. See [Matte tracks](/canvas/matte-tracks/).
883	
884	| Value | In **Track ▸ Matte** | What cuts the track behind |
885	| --- | --- | --- |
886	| `none` | **Off** | Nothing. It's an ordinary track again. |
887	| `alpha` | **Alpha** | The matte track's alpha. |
888	| `alpha_inverted` | **Inverted Alpha** | Its alpha, inverted. |
889	| `luma` | **Luma** | Its brightness. |
890	| `luma_inverted` | **Inverted Luma** | Its brightness, inverted. |
891	
892	The matte track's clips aren't drawn, but they still sound. Where the matte track shows nothing, the track behind shows uncut. A back-most matte track, or one in front of another matte track, cuts nothing.
893	
894	### A track's compressor and limiter
895	
896	`compressor` and `limiter` are **Track ▸ Mix…**'s **Compressor** and **Limit peaks**, see [Track compressor and limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/). They run on the track's sub-mix, after every clip, its volume and its pan, compressor first. The limiter's ceiling is on what the track hands the mix.
897	
898	Each takes an object, and that object **replaces the whole setting**. A key you leave out takes its default, not the value the track had. This is the opposite of [`set_audio`](/mcp/tools-set-audio/#set_audio), where objects merge. `null` clears the setting, and leaving the argument out keeps it.
899	
900	| `compressor` key | Range | Default |
901	| --- | --- | --- |
902	| `threshold_db` | −60 to 0 dB | −18 |
903	| `ratio` | 1 to 20 | 3 |
904	| `attack` | 0 or more ticks | 6,000 (10 ms) |
905	| `release` | 0 or more ticks | 120,000 (200 ms) |
906	| `makeup_db` | 0 to 24 dB | 0 |
907	
908	| `limiter` key | Range | Default |
909	| --- | --- | --- |
910	| `ceiling_db` | −24 to 0 dBTP | −1 |
911	| `release` | 600 to 600,000 ticks | 60,000 (100 ms) |
912	
913	An unknown key, a mistyped value or a value out of range is refused, naming the key.
914	
915	- **Timeline tracks only.** A nest's tracks have no compressor or limiter, so either argument is refused inside a nest. The track holding a nest clip is that nest's bus.
916	- **Exact in every export.** The preview runs them approximately.
917	- **Measuring tools don't hear them.** Normalize, the Loudness readout, Enhance Voice and Match Audio all measure without the track's compressor and limiter.
918	
919	## `remove_empty_tracks`
920	
921	Removes every track that holds no clips. It's **Track ▸ Remove Empty Tracks**, see [Remove Empty Tracks](/timeline/manage-tracks/#remove-empty-tracks).
922	
923	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
924	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
925	| `scope` | integer | No | Tidy this nest's tracks instead. |
926	| `project` | string | No | Path of the open project to act on. Default: the frontmost one. |
927	
928	When every track is empty, the back-most one stays, because a project always keeps one.
929	
930	**Answers** with the project summary, or "made no change" when no track can go.
931	
932	## `add_marker`
933	
934	Adds a marker to the timeline. It's **Mark ▸ Add Marker** (<kbd>M</kbd>), see [Add a marker](/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker), with a name, a colour and a chapter setting available in the same call.
935	
936	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
937	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
938	| `at` | integer | No | Where, in ticks. It's rounded to the project's frame grid, and a time before 0 becomes 0. Default: the playhead. |
939	| `name` | string | No | The marker's name. Default: `Marker` and the new count, so `Marker 3` when there were two. |
940	| `chapter` | boolean | No | Also make it a [chapter](/export/chapters/) of the exported file. Default: false. |
941	| `color` | string | No | A colour name such as `red`, not a hex string. See [Marker colours](/timeline/markers/#marker-colours). Default: red. |
942	| `scope` | integer | No | The tool lists it, but a nest has no markers, so naming one is refused. |
943	| `project` | string | No | Path of the open project to act on. Default: the frontmost one. |
944	
945	**Answers** with `new_markers`, holding the new marker's id, and the project summary.
946	
947	**Refuses:**
948	
949	- A frame that already has a marker. The message names that marker. Two markers can't share a frame.
950	- A project already at its limit of 1,024 markers.
951	- Any call while a nest is open, because a marker sits at project time and the times in that call would be the nest's. Leave the nest with `set_scope` and no arguments first. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/).
952	
953	## `set_marker`
954	
955	Moves or renames a marker, or changes its colour or chapter setting. Anything you leave out keeps its value. It mirrors dragging a flag on the ruler and the marker's row in the Document tab, see [Move, rename and remove a marker](/timeline/markers/#move-rename-and-remove-a-marker).
956	
957	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
958	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
959	| `marker` | integer | Yes | The marker's id. |
960	| `time` | integer | No | The new time, in ticks. It's rounded to the project's frame grid, and a time before 0 becomes 0. |
961	| `name` | string | No | The new name. An empty name leaves the marker unnamed. |
962	| `chapter` | boolean | No | Make it a chapter of the exported file, or stop it being one. |
963	| `color` | string | No | A colour name. An empty string keeps the colour it has. |
964	| `scope` | integer | No | The tool lists it, but a nest has no markers, so naming one is refused. |
965	| `project` | string | No | Path of the open project to act on. Default: the frontmost one. |
966	
967	**Answers** with the project summary.
968	
969	**Refuses** a call that names none of `time`, `name`, `chapter` and `color`, and a `time` on a frame another marker holds.
970	
971	With a nest open, `time` is refused for the same reason as in [`add_marker`](#add_marker). `name`, `chapter` and `color` still work, and the answer lists the edit under `document_ops`. See [Document edits while a nest is open](/mcp/nests/#document-edits-while-a-nest-is-open).
972	
973	## `remove_marker`
974	
975	Removes a marker. It's **Delete** in the marker's row in the Document tab, see [Move, rename and remove a marker](/timeline/markers/#move-rename-and-remove-a-marker).
976	
977	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
978	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
979	| `marker` | integer | Yes | The marker's id. |
980	| `scope` | integer | No | The tool lists it, but a nest has no markers, so naming one is refused. |
981	| `project` | string | No | Path of the open project to act on. Default: the frontmost one. |
982	
983	**Answers** with the project summary. With a nest open it still works, and the answer lists the edit under `document_ops`.
984	
985	## `set_canvas`
986	
987	Changes the project's canvas, the fixed frame every clip is drawn into. Anything you leave out keeps its value.
988	
989	It mirrors the **Canvas**, **Frame Rate** and **Appearance** sections of the [Document tab](/projects/document-tab/). See [Canvas size](/projects/canvas-size/), [Project frame rate](/projects/frame-rate/), [Canvas background and timecode](/projects/background-and-timecode/), [A project's dynamic range](/hdr/dynamic-range/) and [Blending](/hdr/blending/).
990	
991	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
992	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
993	| `width` | integer | No | Canvas width in pixels, 16 to 16,384. It must be even. |
994	| `height` | integer | No | Canvas height in pixels, 16 to 16,384. It must be even. |
995	| `rescale_clips` | boolean | No | Scale every clip's placement with the canvas, so a layout looks the same after a resize. Default: false. |
996	| `fps` | array | No | The frame rate as `[numerator, denominator]`, each a whole number of 1 or more: `[30, 1]`, `[30000, 1001]` for 29.97, `[24000, 1001]` for 23.976. A bare whole number such as `30` also works. |
997	| `background` | array | No | The colour behind every layer as `[r, g, b, a]`, four numbers from 0 to 1. |
998	| `fit_new_clips` | boolean | No | Give a new clip Fit scale when its source is bigger than the canvas. |
999	| `timecode_frames` | boolean | No | Show times as `HH:MM:SS:FF` rather than `HH:MM:SS.mmm`. |
1000	| `output` | string | No | The project's dynamic range: `sdr` (Rec. 709, the default for a project) or `hlg` (HDR, Rec. 2100 HLG). |
1001	| `blending` | string | No | How layers blend: `encoded` (the default for a project) or `linear` light. |
1002	| `scope` | integer | No | The tool lists it, but a nest's size is fixed, so naming one is refused. |
1003	| `project` | string | No | Path of the open project to act on. Default: the frontmost one. |
1004	
1005	**Answers** with the project summary, or "made no change" when the canvas already says what you sent.
1006	
1007	**Refuses:**
1008	
1009	- A call with nothing to change.
1010	- A `width` or `height` that's outside its range or odd.
1011	- An `fps` term that isn't a whole number from 1 to 4,294,967,295.
1012	- A fractional bare `fps` such as `29.97`. The message gives the pair to send.
1013	- A `background` that isn't exactly four numbers, or has a value outside 0 to 1. It isn't filled in or clamped.
1014	
1015	With a nest open, the call applies to the whole project instead, and the answer lists it under `document_ops`.
1016	
1017	**Resizing.** Without `rescale_clips`, clips keep their pixel positions. With it, each clip's `x` follows the width's ratio, its `y` the height's, and its `scale` the smaller of the two, so a layer that fitted the old canvas still fits the new one. Two things stay as they were: the end of a move or scale in an [action](/mcp/tools-animation/) keeps its old target, and the clips inside a nest don't change, because a nest keeps its own size.
1018	
1019	**Changing the frame rate** moves every clip's start and length, every action's span and every marker to the new grid, on the timeline and inside nests. On a coarser grid, two markers can land on one frame. When they do, the first in the project's list stays and the other is dropped. The change goes ahead even if two clips end up overlapping by up to a frame more.
1020	
1021	**Changing `output`** keeps every grade's settings, and a chroma key keeps keying the colour it was picked on. A qualifier's ranges read the HLG signal, so re-pick them after switching.
1022	
1023	**Changing `blending`** to `linear` makes a dissolve keep its brightness, and soft edges and glows come out brighter. Grades, keys and qualifiers work on the same values as before.

15	
16	On the timeline and the canvas, every drag that changes the project is one undo step, and **Edit ▸ Undo** names it. A click that doesn't move anything adds no step.
17	
18	## Selecting on the timeline
19	
20	| Gesture | Where | What it does |
21	| --- | --- | --- |
22	| Click | A clip | Selects it alone. Clicking a clip that's already in a multi-selection keeps the selection, so you can drag it. |
23	| <kbd>⇧</kbd>-click | A clip | Adds it to the selection, or removes it. |
24	| Click | An empty lane, or above or below the lanes | Deselects everything. |
25	| Drag | An empty lane, or above or below the lanes | Draws a marquee that selects every clip it touches. |
26	| <kbd>⇧</kbd>-drag | The same places | Draws a marquee that adds to the selection. |
27	| <kbd>⌥</kbd>-click | A track header | Selects every clip on that track. |
28	
29	A marquee skips clips on locked tracks, but a click can still select one. See [Select clips](/timeline/selecting-clips/).
30	
31	## Moving clips
32	
33	| Gesture | Where | What it does |
34	| --- | --- | --- |
35	| Drag | A clip | Moves the selected clips, in time and to other tracks. A selection across several tracks keeps its spacing. |
36	| Drag | Past the top or bottom track | Puts the clips on a new track: a new front track above the top, a new back track below the bottom. |
37	| <kbd>⌥</kbd>-drag | A clip | Duplicates the clips and moves the copies. The whole selection is copied when the clip is in it. |
38	
39	The earliest clip stops at the start of the timeline, and the others keep their offsets. A clip's linked partner, such as its [detached sound](/audio/detach-and-attach/), moves by the same time. Drag that sound to another track and only the sound changes track.
40	
41	Dragging a clip onto its neighbour on the same track makes a Cross Dissolve across the overlap, within the [overlap rule](/editing/how-edits-work/#the-overlap-rule).
42	
43	During a drag the clip skips positions the project won't allow and waits at the last allowed place. Only the drop counts. If the drop can't go where you let go, a ghost of the clip animates back to where it belongs. See [Move clips](/editing/move-clips/).
44	
45	## Trim, stretch, slip and roll
46	
47	| Gesture | Where | What it does |
48	| --- | --- | --- |
49	| Drag | A clip's edge | [Trims](/editing/trimming/) that edge. |
50	| <kbd>⌥</kbd>-drag | A clip's end edge | [Rate stretch](/speed/rate-stretch/): changes the speed so the clip fills the new length. |
51	| <kbd>⌥⇧</kbd>-drag | A clip's body | [Slip](/editing/slip-and-roll/): moves the source under the clip while the clip stays. |
52	| <kbd>⌥⇧</kbd>-drag | A clip's edge | [Roll](/editing/slip-and-roll/): moves the cut between this clip and the clip touching it. |
53	
54	**Trim.** The edge zone is 7 pt wide, and the pointer turns into the resize cursor over it. A clip 21 pt wide or less is all body, so zoom in to trim it. A trim keeps at least one frame and stays within the source file. Dragging the edge of a clip's detached sound moves the sound alone and leaves its picture, which makes a [J-cut or L-cut](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/).
55	
56	**Rate stretch** works only on a clip that plays a media file. On any other clip, and on a start edge, <kbd>⌥</kbd> trims as usual. Nothing happens past the speed limits of ×0.1 and ×1000, or under one frame, and Frame Job won't stretch a linked clip.
57	
58	**Slip** never snaps, moves a frame at a time and doesn't change the selection. A linked partner on an unlocked track slips with the clip.
59	
60	**Roll** does nothing where no clip touches that edge, so not over a gap or a transition. Each clip keeps at least one frame, and a roll snaps as a trim does.
61	
62	Clips on a locked track can't be dragged, trimmed, slipped or rolled.
63	
64	## Fades and the volume line
65	
66	| Gesture | Where | What it does |
67	| --- | --- | --- |
68	| Drag | A fade handle | Sets that clip's audio [fade](/audio/fades/) in or out. |
69	| Drag | The [volume line](/audio/volume-line/) on a clip | Changes the level at that point, in dB, shown beside the pointer. |
70	| <kbd>⌥</kbd>-click or <kbd>⌥</kbd>-drag | The volume line | Adds a volume point there as an action, then sets its level. |
71	
72	A fade handle is the small square at the top corner of a clip's audio area. It lands on whole frames, can't go past the clip's length and doesn't snap to clip edges. It doesn't work on a locked track.
73	
74	The volume line grabs within 3 pt and drags up and down only. Its scale runs from +30.1 dB at the top to −60 dB, and the very bottom is silence, shown as −∞ dB. Inside or after an action that animates volume, the drag edits that action's end. Anywhere else it edits the clip's volume.
75	
76	Adding a point beeps inside an action that also changes something else, and less than a frame after the previous action's end.
77	
78	Pressing on the line with <kbd>⇧</kbd> held, or double-clicking it, acts on the clip instead, so selecting, slipping and renaming still work there.

80	## Action bands

84	| Click | An action band | Selects the clip and that action, and moves the playhead to the action's end. The Clip tab then edits the action's end values. |
85	| Drag | An action band | Moves the action in time, on whole frames. It stops at the next action and at the clip's own length. |

130	## Snapping
131	
132	While [snapping](/timeline/snapping/) is on (<kbd>N</kbd>), moving, trimming and rolling clips, dragging a marker and scrubbing the ruler snap to clip edges, markers, the start and end of the timeline, the playhead and the in and out points. They snap within about 8 points of the pointer at every zoom, and a guide line shows the snap, except on the ruler. A slip doesn't snap. Every edit lands on the frame grid either way.
133	
134	Hold <kbd>⌘</kbd> while you drag to turn snapping off for that drag, even if you press it partway through. **View ▸ Snapping** stays as it was.

163	## Canvas: selecting and moving
164	
165	| Gesture | What it does |
166	| --- | --- |
167	| Click a clip | Selects the front-most visible clip there. |
168	| <kbd>⇧</kbd>-click a clip | Adds it to the selection, or removes it. |
169	| Click empty canvas | Deselects everything and leaves crop mode. With <kbd>⇧</kbd>, it keeps the selection. |
170	| Drag a clip | Moves the selected clips by the same amount. |
171	
172	A press on a selected clip's handle takes the handle, even with another clip under it. Clips on locked tracks don't move and can't be clicked, and neither can clips on hidden tracks.
173	
174	A drag [snaps](/canvas/canvas-snapping/) to the canvas centre, edges and thirds and to other layers' edges and centres, within 8 points at any zoom, with guide lines. <kbd>N</kbd> turns this off, and holding <kbd>⌘</kbd> suspends it, even partway through a drag.

176	When an action is selected, a drag sets the value at that action's end, not the clip's own value.

273	## How the keys are shared
274	
275	- **Keys with no modifier belong to the editor window.** That's <kbd>Space</kbd>, the letters and punctuation on this page and the arrow keys. They don't work while you're typing in a field or while a sheet is open. <kbd>⇧</kbd> and Caps Lock still count as no modifier. <kbd>⌘</kbd>, <kbd>⌥</kbd> and <kbd>⌃</kbd> never do.
276	- **Shortcuts with a modifier are menu shortcuts.** A shortcut does nothing while its menu item is greyed out.
277	- **<kbd>⌫</kbd>, <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd>, <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> and <kbd>⌘↑</kbd> switch off while you type in a text field,** where they keep their usual text meaning.
278	- **In a sheet,** <kbd>↩</kbd> presses the default button and <kbd>⎋</kbd> cancels.
279	- **The Preview Window takes the same keys.** Keys with no modifier do nothing there while a field in the editor window is being typed in, or while a sheet is open on it. Keys with a modifier go through the editor's menus.
280	
281	A field takes the keys only when you click in it, or choose a command that opens one for typing, such as **Clip ▸ Rename…** or **View ▸ Assistant**. <kbd>↩</kbd>, keypad Enter, <kbd>Tab</kbd> or a click anywhere outside the field applies what you typed and gives the keys back, so <kbd>Space</kbd> plays straight away. With macOS Full Keyboard Access on, <kbd>Tab</kbd> moves to the next control instead. In a multi-line field, such as the Text tab's **Content**, <kbd>↩</kbd> applies and <kbd>⇧↩</kbd> starts a new line. The Assistant's message field [sends on <kbd>↩</kbd>](#assistant-message-field).

283	## Playback and moving the playhead
284	
285	None of these has a menu item.
286	
287	| Key | What it does |
288	| --- | --- |
289	| <kbd>Space</kbd> | Play or pause, wherever the focus is in the window. <kbd>⇧Space</kbd> does the same. |
290	| <kbd>L</kbd> | Play forward. Press it again for 2× and again for 4×. While playing in reverse, it goes straight to 1× forward. |
291	| <kbd>J</kbd> | Play in reverse. Press it again for 2× and again for 4×. While playing forward, it goes straight to 1× in reverse. |
292	| <kbd>K</kbd> | Pause. |
293	| <kbd>←</kbd> <kbd>→</kbd> | Pause and step back or forward one frame. |
294	| <kbd>⇧←</kbd> <kbd>⇧→</kbd> | Pause and step back or forward ten frames. |
295	| <kbd>↑</kbd> | Go to the previous edit point, or to the start when there isn't one. |
296	| <kbd>↓</kbd> | Go to the next edit point. On the last point it stays there. |
297	| <kbd>Home</kbd> <kbd>End</kbd> | Pause and go to the start or end of the project. The keypad and fn versions of these keys work too. |
298	
299	An edit point is the start or end of a clip, or either end of the project. <kbd>J</kbd> and <kbd>L</kbd> beep when there's nothing loaded to play.
300	
301	<kbd>Space</kbd> does something else in three places:
302	
303	- In a text field, <kbd>Space</kbd> types a space.
304	- With macOS Full Keyboard Access on, a focused button, pop-up or segmented control keeps <kbd>Space</kbd> to press itself.
305	- With the preview canvas focused, a tap of <kbd>Space</kbd> plays or pauses when you release it, because holding it down is how you [pan](/canvas/zoom-and-pan/). A <kbd>Space</kbd> held to pan doesn't change playback.
306	
307	The arrow keys move by word in the [Transcript tab](#transcript-text), and move a selected [curve point](/reference/gestures/#color-tab-controls) in the Color tab. They don't move a clip on the canvas. To place a clip by the pixel, type its [position](/canvas/move-scale-rotate/#nudge).

423	## Keys in text and fields
424	
425	### Text on the canvas
426	
427	These work while you [edit a text clip in place](/text-and-shapes/edit-text-on-canvas/) on the preview.
428	
429	| Key | What it does |
430	| --- | --- |
431	| <kbd>↩</kbd> or keypad Enter | Applies the text and stops editing. Clicking away applies it too. |
432	| <kbd>⇧↩</kbd>, <kbd>⌘↩</kbd>, <kbd>⌥↩</kbd> or <kbd>⌃↩</kbd> | Starts a new line. |
433	| <kbd>⎋</kbd> | Stops editing. If the text changed, a sheet asks "Apply your changes to this text?" |
434	
435	In that sheet, **Apply** is the default, on <kbd>↩</kbd>. **Revert** throws the changes away, and **Cancel** goes back to editing. While an input method is composing, <kbd>↩</kbd> and <kbd>⎋</kbd> belong to it.

438	
439	The name field that opens on the timeline for a clip, a track or a marker.
440	
441	| Key | What it does |
442	| --- | --- |
443	| <kbd>↩</kbd> or <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Saves the new name. A click elsewhere does too. |
444	| <kbd>⎋</kbd> | Closes the field and keeps the old name. |
445	
446	Saving an unchanged or empty field does nothing. To clear a clip's name, use the name field at the top of the Clip tab.

450	These work while the [Transcript tab](/captions/transcript-tab/)'s text has the keyboard. [Transcript keys](/captions/transcript-keys/) has the detail.

456	| <kbd>⇧</kbd> with an arrow | Extends the selection without moving the playhead. |
457	| <kbd>⌘A</kbd> | Selects every word. |

498	## Modes that Esc leaves
499	
500	| What's under way | How to leave it |
501	| --- | --- |
502	| A canvas drag: move, scale, rotate, crop, a line's endpoint or an obscure region | <kbd>⎋</kbd> puts everything back as it was before the drag, and adds no undo step. |
503	| [Crop mode](/canvas/crop/) | <kbd>⎋</kbd> or <kbd>↩</kbd> while the canvas has the focus, or <kbd>C</kbd>. A click on empty canvas or on a different clip leaves it too. |
504	| Region mode, from <kbd>Z</kbd> or the Obscure section's **Place on Canvas** | <kbd>⎋</kbd>. If you started it with <kbd>Z</kbd>, <kbd>Z</kbd> again leaves it too. |
505	| The key-colour or qualifier eyedropper | <kbd>⎋</kbd>. The hint on screen reads "Click to pick … · Esc to cancel". |
506	| A selected curve point in the Color tab | <kbd>⎋</kbd> deselects it. |
507	
508	Timeline drags have no such cancel. To take one back, use **Edit ▸ Undo** after you let go.
509	
510	Region mode also ends by itself when the selection stops being the clip it started for, or the playhead leaves that clip. Only one of these canvas tools can be on at a time, so starting one ends the others.

532	
533	| Symbol | Key |
534	| --- | --- |

536	| ⌥ | Option |
537	| ⇧ | Shift |
538	| ⌃ | Control |
539	| ⌫ | Delete |

541	| ⎋ | Escape |

544	- **(key)** after a shortcut means a bare key the menu doesn't draw: <kbd>W</kbd>, <kbd>E</kbd>, <kbd>M</kbd>, <kbd>I</kbd>, <kbd>O</kbd>, <kbd>N</kbd> and <kbd>⇧Z</kbd>. The editor handles these itself rather than the menu, so a text field can never lose the letter to them. They work in the editor window and the [Preview Window](/timeline/preview-window/), and not while you're typing in a field or while a sheet is open.
545	- **A ⌘ shortcut does nothing while its item is greyed out.**
546	- **Always** in the last column means whenever a project window is in front with no sheet on it. While a sheet is up, every command that acts on the project is greyed out, and so is every such command when no project window is open.

904	
905	**Transition ▸** sets the transition into the clip. See [Add or remove a transition](/motion/add-a-transition/).
906	
907	The rows are **Cross Dissolve**, **Fade Through Black**, **Fade Through White**, **Push Left**, **Push Right**, **Push Up**, **Push Down**, **Wipe**, **Slide**, **Zoom**, **Wipe Left**, **Wipe Up** and **Wipe Down**, then **None**. A checkmark shows the selected clip's transition.

913	
914	At a hard cut it aims for a transition 0.5 s long, snapped to frames, and makes a shorter one when the clips have less footage to spare. Where neither side of the cut has a frame to spare, a sheet says so and offers **Shift Clips Left**, which slides the second clip and everything after it on unlocked tracks left by half a second.

963	| **Corner ▸** | The whole camera fitted in a box in the corner you pick, with the screen at its full placement. The box is a quarter of the canvas wide, a third tall and 5 % in from the edges. |

8:## Projects and the timeline
10:- **Action.** An animation on a clip: a span on its action lane with an end state its properties ease to. See [Actions](/motion/actions/).
11:- **Adjustment clip.** A clip with no picture of its own that grades every track behind it. See [Adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/).
12:- **Canvas.** The fixed frame every clip is drawn into. Every export starts from its size. See [The canvas](/canvas/the-canvas/).
13:- **Clip.** One placed piece on a track: a stretch of a media file, or a text, shape, image, graphic, adjustment or nest clip. See [Core concepts](/getting-started/core-concepts/).
14:- **Current track.** The track of the first selected clip, or with nothing selected the front-most track. Track commands act on it. See [Menus](/reference/menus/).
15:- **Edit point.** A clip's start or end, where <kbd>↑</kbd> and <kbd>↓</kbd> stop. See [Jump around the timeline](/timeline/move-the-playhead/).
16:- **Frame grid.** The frames of the project's rate. Every time you set lands on one. See [Core concepts](/getting-started/core-concepts/).
17:- **In–Out range.** The span set with <kbd>I</kbd> and <kbd>O</kbd>, which many commands act on. See [The in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/).
18:- **Linked pair.** A picture clip and its detached sound, which move, split and ripple together. See [Detach and Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/).
19:- **Media.** A file the project has imported, listed in the Media tab. Clips refer to it. See [The Media tab](/projects/media-tab/).
20:- **Nest.** A clip that wraps other clips into a timeline of its own. See [Nests](/editing/nests/).
21:- **No-change edit, or identity.** An edit that was understood and had nothing to change. It beeps, makes no undo step and shows no message. See [When an edit is refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/#a-beep-with-no-message).
22:- **Package.** A `.framejob` project, a folder the Finder shows as one file. See [The .framejob package](/reference/framejob-package/).
23:- **Playhead.** The current time on the timeline. See [The ruler and playhead](/timeline/ruler-and-playhead/).
24:- **Refusal.** A rule stopping an edit. Frame Job beeps and shows the rule's sentence after "Refused: " at the foot of the inspector. Nothing changes and no undo step is made. See [When an edit is refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/).
25:- **Ripple.** An edit that closes the gap it leaves by moving later clips along. See [Delete, Ripple Delete and Lift](/editing/delete-clips/).
26:- **Selected action.** The one action of the single selected clip that the Clip tab is editing. While it's chosen, the fields show and write its end state. See [Select an action](/motion/select-an-action/).
27:- **Tick.** Frame Job's unit of time, 600,000 to the second, which divides every common frame duration exactly. The "Refused: " line and agent tools give lengths in ticks. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/).
28:- **Track.** A lane of clips. The front track is the top lane, and it's drawn over those behind it. See [Tracks](/timeline/tracks/).
30:## Picture and sound
32:- **Camera Log.** A file's setting saying which camera log curve it holds, so it's converted at the start of the picture. See [Camera Log](/hdr/camera-log/).
33:- **Cue.** One timed caption. See [Captions are text clips](/captions/how-captions-work/).
34:- **Cutout.** A clip with Remove Background on. See [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/).
35:- **Deep.** A picture with more than 8 bits for each colour component. See [Precision and bit depth](/hdr/precision/).
36:- **Ducking.** Lowering a clip's sound under another's. See [Ducking](/audio/ducking/).
37:- **Dynamic range.** Whether the project works in SDR or HDR (HLG). See [A project's dynamic range](/hdr/dynamic-range/).
38:- **J-cut and L-cut.** The sound of a linked pair starting before, or ending after, its picture. See [J-cuts and L-cuts](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/).
39:- **Look.** A built-in grade or a `.cube` LUT on a clip. See [Looks](/color/looks/).
40:- **LUFS.** The unit of loudness. See [Normalize](/audio/normalize/).
41:- **LUT.** A colour lookup table in a `.cube` file. See [.cube LUTs](/color/luts/).
42:- **Matte.** A track that cuts the track behind it by its alpha or brightness. See [Matte tracks](/canvas/matte-tracks/).
43:- **Plate.** A clip that fills the canvas behind everything, such as a solid colour or a picture from **Add Background**. See [Backgrounds](/canvas/backgrounds/).
44:- **Qualifier.** An adjustment clip's pick of the pixels it grades, by hue, saturation and brightness. See [Qualifiers](/color/qualifiers/).
45:- **Ramp.** A speed change over time, a Speed action on the action lane. See [Speed ramps](/speed/speed-ramps/).
46:- **Scopes.** The waveform, parade, vectorscope and histogram beside the preview. See [Scopes](/color/scopes/).
47:- **Slate.** What a clip draws in place of a picture it doesn't have, such as missing media. See [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/).
48:- **Stem.** One track's sound written as its own file beside the mix. See [Audio stems](/export/stems/).
49:- **Transition.** The change from one clip to the next across their overlap on one track. See [Transitions](/motion/transitions/).
51:## Graphics and agents
53:- **Assistant.** The chat in the inspector that edits the open project on your own Anthropic key. See [Chat with the Assistant](/assistant/chat/).
54:- **Category.** The list a module is filed under in the Graphic dialog. See [Bundled templates](/graphics/templates/).
55:- **Error card.** What a graphic draws in its own box when it can't draw itself. See [Edit a module](/graphics/edit-a-module/).
56:- **Graphic.** A clip whose picture is drawn by code. It's the clip's content, not an effect. See [What a graphic is](/graphics/what-is-a-graphic/).
57:- **Graphic package.** A `.fjgraphic` file holding a module and the fonts and pictures it uses. See [Share a graphic](/graphics/share-a-graphic/).
58:- **Kept revision.** An earlier text of a module the app kept, the last 10 for each module. See [Rename, delete and restore graphics](/graphics/manage-graphics/).
59:- **MCP.** The protocol an agent uses to drive Frame Job, through the `framejob-mcp` helper. See [How an agent reaches Frame Job](/mcp/overview/).
60:- **Module.** A graphic's source, one JavaScript module returning SVG for each frame. See [Write a graphic module](/graphics/write-a-module/).
61:- **Op.** Short for operation: one edit to a project, applied whole. Most agent tools each make one. See [How tool calls behave](/mcp/tool-calls/).
62:- **Patch.** An object an agent sends holding only the properties it wants to change. See [Patches](/mcp/patches/).
63:- **Props.** The values a graphic is drawn with, stored on its clip. See [Graphic properties](/graphics/properties/).
64:- **Template.** A module the app ships, copied into the package when you insert it. See [Bundled templates](/graphics/templates/).
66:## Related
---
title: Limits
description: Every hard number in Frame Job in one place, from how many clips a project holds to each area's ceilings.
---

The hard numbers, in one place. Each section gives an area's ceilings and links to the page that explains them. For what to do when you hit one, see [Troubleshooting](/reference/troubleshooting/).

## Project size

| A project holds at most | |
| --- | --- |
| Clips | 4,096 |
| Tracks | 64 |
| Markers | 1,024 |
| Media files | 1,024 |
| Levels of nesting | 8 |

Clips and tracks inside [nests](/editing/nests/) count towards the same totals.

An edit that would go past one of these isn't made, and an alert names the limit, for example "too many clips: 4097 (max 4096)". A project file already past a limit won't open, the message names the limit, and the package isn't rewritten.

A [recording](/recording/where-it-lands/) that needs a new track can't be added to a project at its track limit. Its files stay on disk and the note names them.

Files in a project have one more limit: a [`.cube` LUT](#colour) can be at most 32 MiB.

## Canvas and layers

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| [Canvas](/projects/canvas-size/) width and height | Even numbers, 16 to 16,384 px |
| [Scale](/canvas/transform/) | 1 to 1,000 % |
| [Shape](/text-and-shapes/shape-settings/) width and height | 1 to 20,000 px in the fields. A drag on the canvas stops at 4 and 20,000 px. |
| [Filters](/effects/filters/) on one clip | 4 |
| [Obscure](/effects/obscure/) regions on one clip | 4 |
| An obscure region's width and height | 1 to 20,000 source pixels in the fields |
| [Gradient](/text-and-shapes/gradients/) stops | 2 to 8 |
| [Preview zoom](/canvas/zoom-and-pan/) steps | Fit, 50%, 100%, 200% |

Scale is uniform for pictures. Only a shape's box and a text clip's wrap width can be stretched on one axis.

Crop, Corner Radius and Chroma Key work only on video, image and still clips. A nest clip can't take a [blend mode](/canvas/blend-modes/), and Add Blurred Background isn't offered for one.

## Timeline and editing

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Overlaps | On one track, a clip may overlap at most one neighbour on each side, and each overlap may be at most half the length of the shorter clip |
| Shortest clip after a trim or roll | 1 frame |
| [Timeline zoom](/timeline/zoom-and-scroll/) | 0.35 to 4,000 points per second, 42 by default |
| [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/) radius | 8 points, on the timeline and on the [canvas](/canvas/canvas-snapping/) |

A media clip can't be trimmed, rolled or slipped past either end of its file. Every time you set lands on the project's frame grid. See [How edits work](/editing/how-edits-work/).

[Markers](/timeline/markers/) live on the main timeline only. Inside a nest you can't add one, step to one or jump to one, though the Document tab can still rename, chapter and delete them. Only an agent can change a marker's colour.

## Speed

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Slowest rate | ×0.1 |
| Fastest rate | ×1000 |
| Fastest rate with sound | ×12, with Keep pitch on or off |
| [Freeze frame](/speed/freeze-frame/) length, when none is given | 2 s |
| [Speed Ramp…](/speed/make-a-ramp/) **Hold** | None, 25%, 50% or 75%, 50% by default. An agent can use any hold from 0 to 0.9. |

Frame Job asks before an edit takes a clip with sound past ×12. On a ramped clip, one rate above ×12 anywhere silences the whole clip. See [Sound at high speed](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/).

With Keep pitch on, a ramp's sound can lag the picture by up to about 24 ms after a steep slow-down. See [Sound on a ramp](/speed/ramp-audio/), and [Speed at a glance](/speed/overview/) for how the rates fit together.

## Audio

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| [Clip volume](/audio/volume/) | Up to 3200 % (about +30 dB). The slider covers 0 to 400 %, and the field takes the rest. |
| [The volume line](/audio/volume-line/) | +30.1 dB to −60 dB |
| [Track volume](/audio/track-volume-and-pan/) | Up to +12 dB (×4) |
| [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/) drift correction | Up to 0.2 % from ×1 |
| [Match Audio](/audio/match-audio/) | Matches with the [EQ](/audio/eq/)'s five shelves and bands |

The [gate](/audio/gate/), the [leveller](/audio/leveller/) and the [de-esser](/audio/de-esser/) need a measured clip. A clip shorter than 0.4 s, or too quiet to measure, plays and exports without them. An export waits up to five minutes for a measurement still running, then stops and names the clip.

789	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
790	
791	The Clip menu holds the commands that act on the selected clips. This page gives every item's exact title and shortcut, and what makes it available, so you can find a key or work out why something is greyed out.
792
